meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 15, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Returning to City Hall chambers for Durham's first hybrid regular meeting, Council proclaimed David Price Day and Veterans Day, recognized 911 dispatcher Dwayne McIntyre, and hosted nearly 90 minutes of community tributes honoring retiring Council Member Pierce Freelon and Mayor Steve Schewel. Council unanimously passed the Consent Agenda 7-0 (including five Crane/Elizabeth/Eva/Gurley/Marne affordable-housing land conveyances) and adopted UDO Text Amendment TC2104 (tenant notification and permit updates) 7-0. After an extended public hearing over traffic, signalization, and school capacity, Council approved the 310-apartment Rosewalk II rezoning at West Club Blvd and North Duke St 7-0 after applicants proffered $30,000 for a traffic circle and $20,500 for DPS students, and then unanimously voted 7-0 across three motions to order $1.8M in petitioned Ardmore Drive ribbon paving and water/sewer lines while criticizing special-assessment inequity.

agenda_items.title: David Price Day, Veterans Day, 911 Dispatcher Tribute, and Farewells to Freelon & Schewel
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In Durham's first hybrid in-person meeting since the pandemic, Council presented proclamations for Congressman David Price Day and Veterans Day and honored 911 dispatcher Dwayne McIntyre. Former officials, state legislators, county commissioners, and community leaders—including Bill Bell, Brenda Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Mike Woodard—delivered lengthy farewell tributes honoring Pierce Freelon and Mayor Steve Schewel.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Boards/Commissions, FY23 Budget Schedule, Affordable Housing Conveyances, and Infrastructure Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Diana Schreiber removed Item 2 (Cultural Advisory Board nominee moved out of Durham) and Jacqueline Wagstaff withdrew her pull of Item 9 (Tenants' Bill of Rights discussion). Council voted 7-0 to approve Consent Items 1, 3-5, and 7-15, including five parcel conveyances for affordable housing, the HR&A 505 W Chapel Hill St advisory contract, and fleet/stormwater contracts.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment TC2104 — Updates for Applications, Permits, and Tenant Notifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC2104, expanding public-hearing mail notifications to renters and site occupants (not only property owners), clarifying right-of-way sign posting, and codifying street-renaming, closing, and annexation procedures (recommended 13-0 by Planning Commission). Council praised the renter-notice reform and adopted both the ordinance and consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Rosewalk II (W. Club Blvd & N. Duke St, 7.865 Acres, RU-M(D) for 310 Apartments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dan Jewell and developer Bob Chapman proposed rezoning 10 parcels at West Club Blvd and North Duke St to RU-M(D) for up to 310 apartments and an existing church while staying under 149 peak-hour trips to avoid a TIA. Nearby residents Mimi Kessler, Virginia Bowman, Mary Kopac, Joe Deem, and John Paces-Wiles warned of dangerous intersection conditions and cut-through traffic on Woodland and Ruffin Streets, while proponents Tiffany Elder and Dan Bach cited central rental supply. After applicants added proffers of $30,000 for a traffic circle and $20,500 ($500 x 41 students) for DPS, Council approved the rezoning and consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Ardmore Drive Petitioned Improvements — Ribbon Paving, Water Main, and Water/Sewer Laterals ($1.8M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works presenter Robert Joiner outlined the ~$1.8M special assessment (~$1.2M paving, ~$600k water/sewer) across 13-14 Ardmore Drive parcels, moving residents 4-5 years up the unpaved road queue compared to last year's denied petition. Residents Isaac Woods Sr. and Jr. pleaded for safe drinking water and fire hydrants after decades of contaminated wells; Middleton, Freelon, and Freeman condemned forcing Black working-class neighborhoods to pay assessments for basic services before voting 7-0 across all three statutory motions.

votes.item_title: Item 18 — Adopt UDO Text Amendment Ordinance TC2104 (Updates for Applications, Permits, and Tenant Notice)
votes.discussion_detail: Following Michael Stock's staff report and questions from Javiera Caballero on expanding the 600-foot notice radius, Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded adopting TC2104. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

votes.item_title: Item 18 — Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for UDO Text Amendment TC2104
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded adopting the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement for TC2104. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

votes.item_title: Item 19 — Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance and FLUM Amendment for Rosewalk II (RU-M(D), Up to 310 Apartments)
votes.discussion_detail: After the applicant added proffers of $30,000 for a traffic circle at Woodland/Englewood or Ruffin/Knox and $20,500 ($500 per 41 students) for DPS, DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded approving the Rosewalk II rezoning and FLUM change. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

votes.item_title: Item 19 — Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Rosewalk II
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded adopting the statutory consistency statement for Rosewalk II. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

votes.item_title: Item 20 — Accept Certificate of Sufficiency for Ardmore Drive Improvement Petition
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Charlie Reece seconded accepting the petition Certificate of Sufficiency for Ardmore Drive ribbon paving and water/sewer main and laterals. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

votes.item_title: Item 20 — Adopt Preliminary Assessment Resolution for Ardmore Drive Improvements
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the Preliminary Resolution for Ardmore Drive improvements. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

votes.item_title: Item 20 — Adopt Final Resolution Ordering Ardmore Drive Ribbon Paving and Water/Sewer Improvements
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded adopting the Final Resolution ordering the $1.8M assessed improvements on Ardmore Drive. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 15, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Rosewalk II Traffic & Intersection Safety vs. Central Infill Multifamily Housing
disagreements.summary: Neighbors of Trinity Park and Northgate Park argued that Rosewalk II's 310 apartments would exacerbate crashes at N. Duke St and W. Club Blvd and cut-through speeding while sidestepping a Traffic Impact Analysis under the 149-trip cap, whereas council members prioritized centrally located rental supply once additional proffers were added.
disagreements.side_a_position: Delay or require signal/geometric fixes and fuller neighborhood traffic mitigation before approving 310 apartments.
side_a_arguments: Residents reported repeated severe collisions and bus-passenger hazards at W. Club Blvd and N. Duke St.
Neighbors criticized capping trips below 149 to avoid a TIA and argued the driveway should be offset from Woodland Dr.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the 310-unit RU-M(D) rezoning based on central infill location, 35% lower projected rents than downtown, and new traffic/school proffers.
side_b_arguments: Lower land cost (~80% below downtown) and surface parking allow relatively moderate rents near Duke University and I-85.
Applicant committed $30,000 toward a neighborhood traffic circle and $20,500 for DPS students.
disagreements.resolution: Following the applicant's additional traffic-circle and school proffers and transportation staff review, Council unanimously passed the rezoning 7-0 while noting ongoing coordination with NCDOT.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 15, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Racial & Economic Equity of Special Assessments for Basic Water and Road Paving on Ardmore Drive
disagreements.summary: While voting unanimously to approve residents' $1.8M self-assessed petition so Ardmore Drive families receive clean water and fire protection immediately, council members criticized a city system that forces longtime Black working-class homeowners to pay steep assessments to skip a multi-year unpaved-road queue.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the resident petition now to end well contamination while condemning special assessments for basic municipal infrastructure.
side_a_arguments: Forcing residents annexed decades ago with bacteria-contaminated wells and no hydrants to pay ~$1.8M across 13-14 properties to jump ahead 4-5 years reflects systemic inequity.
Council urged reforming how Durham funds unpaved roads and water extensions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Note the statutory structure under which petitioned 100%-assessed improvements accelerate capital queue priority under existing policy.
side_b_arguments: Staff and Mayor Schewel noted the $1.8M estimate (~$1.2M paving, ~$600k water lines/laterals) relies on petitioner signatures to advance 4-5 years ahead of standard city-funded scheduling.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 on all three Ardmore Drive assessment motions so residents could receive water, fire service, and paving, while calling for future funding reforms.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Nov. 4, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson presiding in the absence of Charlie Reece and Javiera Caballero (and Mayor Steve Schewel arriving mid-session), Council congratulated newly elected Mayor Elaine O'Neal and Council Member Leonardo Williams and unanimously passed 4-0 priority-item motions updating Ardmore Drive notice dates, entering closed session on two litigation matters, and adjusting board appointments. Council reviewed the FY23 budget schedule and the 505 W Chapel Hill St HR&A contract before conducting a lengthy work-session debate with Bull City Tenants United over their 13-point Tenants' Bill of Rights, directing the City Manager and City Attorney to return with enforceable options on housing inspections, language access, right-to-counsel, Ban-the-Box, and source-of-income protections. Council also received an Equitable Pedestrian Infrastructure briefing shifting sidewalk prioritization toward racial equity and the 2021 Employee Engagement Survey showing sharp morale declines in public safety, before voting 5-0 to set the November 15 agenda and end Zoom chat.

agenda_items.title: Election Congratulations, Priority Items (Ardmore Dr & Appointments), and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson noted excused absences for Charlie Reece and Javiera Caballero and delayed arrival for Mayor Steve Schewel, as members congratulated Mayor-elect Elaine O'Neal, Council Member-elect Leonardo Williams, and re-elected incumbents. Council passed three 4-0 votes accepting Item 20's updated Ardmore Drive notice dates, holding a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for Estate of Brooklyn Maynard (Kelly) and Tony Scott Jr./Sr. litigation, and accepting Clerk priority items 6-7.

agenda_items.title: FY23 Budget Schedule and 505 W Chapel Hill Street HR&A Advisors Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On Item 8, Budget Director John Allore walked through the FY23 budget development timeline and confirmed no major structural changes. On Item 12, Stacy Poston and Deputy Manager Keith Chadwell explained why the $198k HR&A Advisors contract for redeveloping 505 W Chapel Hill St skips redoing prior community engagement and unbundles RFQ teams, while resident Stella Adams urged community land trust considerations.

agenda_items.title: Tenants' Bill of Rights Proposals (Bull City Tenants United) and Preemption Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public remarks from Bull City Tenants United organizers Howie Machtinger, Alex Perlman, Lee Ganz, Emerson Goldstein, and Irene Lawrence—plus Ajax Woolley, Stella Adams, and Jacqueline Wagstaff—Council reviewed 13 tenant protection demands alongside City Attorney Kim Rehberg's legal analysis of NC preemption limits (including NCGS 42-44 and rent-withholding limits vs. Charlotte's ordinance). Council directed the City Manager to evaluate items 1, 2, 4, and 13 (after-hours/non-fee inspections, translation, landlord registry), asked the City Attorney to draft options on items 3, 6, and 11 (Ban-the-Box, source-of-income, non-discrimination), and tasked DeDreana Freeman with drafting a symbolic bill-of-rights resolution for item 8.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Placed on Consent / Staff direction given

agenda_items.title: Equitable Pedestrian Infrastructure and Vision Zero Prioritization Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Sean Egan, Brian Taylor, and Doug Wright presented an equity-centered overhaul of sidewalk corridor and intersection prioritization toward Durham's $450M (300-mile at $1.5M/mile) sidewalk backlog, showing that 80% of the 2017 Bike+Walk priority intersections fell outside race-equity priority neighborhoods. Council members—joined by Mayor Steve Schewel, who noted upcoming Green and Equitable Infrastructure Bond needs—strongly endorsed applying racial equity scoring and low-cost traffic calming in future CIP requests.

agenda_items.title: 2021 Employee Engagement Survey, Ending Zoom Chat, Appointments, and Set Nov. 15 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant HR Director Timothy Howe and TalentKeepers CEO Christopher Mulligan presented the April-May 2021 survey (72% participation of 2,421 employees), revealing strong gains in direct-supervisor engagement (reaching the 80% goal) and governance/admin units, offset by a 20-point satisfaction drop in Public Safety (41% of respondents) and declining pay satisfaction. Schewel emphasized upcoming off-cycle public-safety pay adjustments and announced Zoom chat would end on November 15; Council heard Clerk appointments and voted 5-0 to set the November 15 agenda before recessing to closed session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Nov. 4, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Scope of Tenants' Bill of Rights Under State Preemption vs. Municipal Enforcement Resources
disagreements.summary: During the Item 9 Tenants' Bill of Rights discussion, Bull City Tenants United organizers and some council members pushed to adopt strong local anti-rent-collection and inspection ordinances modeled on Charlotte's code, while the City Attorney warned of NC state statutory preemption and council members debated how far Durham could push legal boundaries without risking invalidation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Push legal boundaries—mirroring Charlotte's minimum-housing rent prohibition and expanding after-hours inspections, translation, Ban-the-Box, and enforcement funding.
side_a_arguments: Tenants live in dangerous slum conditions and face landlords who ignore repairs or send maintenance staff as biased interpreters.
Charlotte's provision provides practical leverage for tenants seeking treble damages or warranty-of-habitability relief even without direct city prosecution.
disagreements.side_b_position: Focus on legally defensible city investments—free inspection access, language translation, eviction legal aid, and non-discrimination ordinances—while respecting NC statutory preemption.
side_b_arguments: North Carolina preemption and NCGS 42-44 prohibit cities from authorizing unilateral tenant rent withholding or escrow outside court orders, and Charlotte does not enforce its clause.
Municipal funding for legal defense and expanded code enforcement delivers immediate tangible tenant relief.
disagreements.resolution: Council directed the City Manager to assess staffing/funding for inspection access, interpretation, and landlord registration (items 1, 2, 4, 13), directed the City Attorney to review non-discrimination/Ban-the-Box/SOI options (items 3, 6, 11), and tasked DeDreana Freeman with drafting a symbolic resolution (item 8) for January 2022.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 1, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly six-hour virtual Council meeting on November 1, 2021, Council opened by celebrating Bloomberg Philanthropies funding for Durham's guaranteed income pilot and Mayor Steve Schewel's 10th annual Run with the Mayor before unanimously passing the Consent Agenda 7-0 (including CASA's Bryan Place loan and Lake Michie land acquisition). Following an extensive public hearing on Item 22 (Griffin Place, 462 homes on East Geer St/Ferrell Rd), Council voted 7-0 to continue the hearing open until January 3, 2022 to seek stronger affordable housing and buffer commitments even after the applicant raised its housing fund proffer from $150 to $500 per unit (~$230,000), and then unanimously approved Item 23 (Bethpage Office 2, IL(D) to OI(D)) 7-0. After nearly four hours of emotional neighborhood and Eno River Association testimony on Item 24 (Latta Park at Guess and Latta Roads — up to 55,000 sq ft commercial CG(D) and 200 townhomes PDR 9.906 with 10 affordable units at 60% AMI and 40kW solar), Council passed both the rezoning ordinance and consistency statement 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman casting the lone Nay vote, before approving excused absences for Caballero and Reece.

agenda_items.title: Guaranteed Income Grant, Run with the Mayor, Priority Item 14, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council celebrated Bloomberg Philanthropies' guaranteed income award and staff participation in Run with the Mayor, received City Manager Page's Item 14 attachment update (Brady Integrated Security for Water Management), and voted 7-0 to pass Consent Items 1-5, 7-10, and 13-20 (including Bryan Place Apartments loan, Lake Michie land acquisition, and Water Management contracts).

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Griffin Place (82.84 Acres, PDR 5.578 for 462 Units)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Danny Cultra and applicant Jarod Edens/Fred Shackle proposed annexing and rezoning 82.84 acres on East Geer St and Ferrell Rd for 168 single-family homes and 294 townhomes with three traffic signals, pedestrian crossings to Glenn Elementary, and 100-year stormwater ponds. Seven residents (including Taryn Kavanaugh, Kyle Marion, Robert Von Briesen, Jason Bazdula, Lindsey Dunn, Faith Neary, Shane Price, and Robin Sorrell) opposed road congestion and school overcrowding; although Edens added $34,000 for DPS and raised the affordable-housing fund proffer from $150 to $500/unit (~$230k), Mayor Schewel and council members questioned design commitments, separated product types, and industrial buffering, voting 7-0 to hold the hearing open to January 3, 2022.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred / Continued to Jan. 3, 2022 (Passed 7-0 Roll Call)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Bethpage Office 2 (5321 & 5421 Chin Page Rd, 24.62 Acres, IL(D) to OI(D))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker (representing Tri Properties) and Creekside neighborhood leader Kevin Walls urged rezoning 24.62 acres between FedEx and Creekside homes from Light Industrial to Office & Institutional with a text-only development plan (limiting traffic to 149 peak-hour trips and buffering neighbors against FedEx parking expansion). Despite questions from Schewel, Reece, and Freeman over the text-only format lacking guaranteed office vs. residential uses and administrative site-plan notice, Council approved both the rezoning and consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Latta Park (Guess & Latta Roads, 31 Acres, RS-20 to CG(D) & PDR 9.906)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Alexander Cahill and applicants Jamie Schwedler and Austin Williams (Crossland Southeast) presented Latta Park's proposal for up to 55,000 sq ft of retail/commercial on 10 acres and 200 townhomes (PDR 9.906) on 20 acres—featuring 10 on-site 60%-AMI affordable townhomes ($1.25M subsidy), 40kW solar, a 1.3-acre park, Easley Elementary bike/ped connection, dual left-turn lanes at Latta/Guess, and 100-year stormwater ponds. An organized opposition group led by Megan Gray alongside Eno River Association ED Jessica Sheffield, stormwater speakers, and residents warned of Latta Rd congestion, Eno runoff, and incompatible suburban commercial, while northern Durham proponents supported modern retail, intersection fixes, and townhomes. Council passed the rezoning and consistency statement 6-1, with DeDreana Freeman voting Nay.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (two Roll Call votes; Freeman Nay)

agenda_items.title: Excused Absences for Javiera Caballero and Steve Schewel (Nov. 4 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Prior to adjourning at 12:47 AM, Council voted unanimously 7-0 in two separate roll-call votes to grant excused absences from the November 4, 2021 work session for Javiera Caballero and Mayor Steve Schewel.

votes.item_title: Item 22 — Continue Griffin Place Public Hearing Open Until January 3, 2022
votes.discussion_detail: Even after applicant Jarod Edens added $34,000 for DPS and raised the affordable housing fund proffer from $150 to $500 per unit (~$230,000), Charlie Reece moved and Javiera Caballero seconded continuing the Griffin Place public hearing open until January 3, 2022 so the developer could return with stronger buffers, block-length/design commitments, and housing benefits. Passed 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Item 23 — Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance and FLUM Amendment for Bethpage Office 2 (IL(D) to OI(D))
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded rezoning 24.62 acres at 5321 and 5421 Chin Page Road from IL(D) to OI(D) text-only development plan and amending the FLUM to Office. Passed 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Item 23 — Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Bethpage Office 2
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded adopting the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement for Bethpage Office 2. Passed 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Item 24 — Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance and FLUM Amendment for Latta Park (RS-20 to CG(D) & PDR 9.906)
votes.discussion_detail: Following an nearly four-hour public hearing, Charlie Reece moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the ordinance rezoning 31 acres at Guess and Latta Roads to CG(D) and PDR 9.906 and amending the Future Land Use Map. Passed 6-1 on roll call with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Item 24 — Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Latta Park
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the statutory consistency statement for Latta Park. Passed 6-1 on roll call with DeDreana Freeman voting No.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence for Javiera Caballero from November 4, 2021 Work Session
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved and Pierce Freelon seconded granting an excused absence for Javiera Caballero from the November 4, 2021 work session. Passed 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence for Mayor Steve Schewel from November 4, 2021 Work Session
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded granting Mayor Steve Schewel an excused absence for attending an event with the Governor on November 4. Passed 7-0 on roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 1, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Latta Park Rezoning — Commercial Expansion, Latta Road Traffic & Eno Watershed Impacts vs. On-Site Affordable Townhomes & Intersection Fixes
disagreements.summary: Latta Park split the Council 6-1 after residents and conservation advocates argued that adding 55,000 sq ft of retail and 200 townhomes at Guess and Latta Roads violated Comprehensive Plan commercial siting, threatened Eno River water quality, and overloaded two-lane Latta Road, while the six-member majority praised unprecedented proffers including 10 60%-AMI townhomes and dual turn lanes.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the mixed-use CG(D)/PDR 9.906 rezoning as a needed supply of moderate/affordable townhomes and northern Durham neighborhood retail.
side_a_arguments: Developer proffered over 50 commitments including 10 permanently affordable townhomes at 60% AMI ($1.25M subsidy), 40kW solar, a 1.3-acre park, and 100-year residential stormwater detention.

Dual left-turn lanes improve peak morning Guess/Latta intersection level-of-service from D to C where no NCDOT upgrades are funded, and rejection leaves RS-20 $500k+ McMansions as the by-right alternative.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose commercial and high-density rezoning due to traffic bottlenecks on un-widenable Latta Road, stormwater/Eno watershed risks, and lack of transit walkability.
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman voted No after extensive opposition testimony citing level-of-service D egress on Latta Road, right-in/right-out U-turns on Guess Road, and Easley Elementary traffic hazards.
Opponents including Megan Gray and Eno River Association ED Jessica Sheffield noted nearby vacant commercial space, no bus service, and impervious surface runoff above West Point on the Eno.
disagreements.resolution: Council adopted both the Latta Park zoning ordinance and consistency statement by 6-1 roll-call votes, with DeDreana Freeman in dissent.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 1, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Sufficiency of Griffin Place Community Benefits, Affordable Housing Proffer, and Product Integration
disagreements.summary: Council paused the 462-unit Griffin Place annexation and rezoning in eastern Durham because members found initial housing-fund payments, perimeter buffers, and segregated single-family/townhome layouts insufficient relative to the project's scale and state-road congestion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold the public hearing open until January 3, 2022 to extract stronger affordable housing contributions, better industrial/residential buffering, block-length limits, and improved traffic clarity.
side_a_arguments: Even after raising the affordable housing fund proffer from $150 to $500/unit during the hearing, Council noted the ~$115M project needed stronger design commitments, less rigid product segregation, and better buffering adjacent to Scannell industrial land.
State roads around Cheek and Ferrell Roads lack funded DOT widening, raising urgency around community benefits.
disagreements.side_b_position: Recognize already-proffered traffic signals, 100-year ponds, and Glenn Elementary pedestrian crossings while negotiating additional terms.
side_b_arguments: Applicant argued residential zoning cut trips vs. current industrial zoning and committed to three traffic signals and a $34,000 DPS school contribution.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 to continue the Griffin Place public hearing open until January 3, 2022.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Oct. 21, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: The October 21, 2021 Work Session was largely procedural and informational, with seven unanimous Council votes accepting City Manager and City Clerk priority items, suspending the rules to pass two urgent Water Management facility IT/AV contracts (ePlus Technology and Contact Systems), and setting the November 1 Regular Meeting agenda. During pulled items, Council examined cost overruns and CDBG 1.5 expenditure-test risks on Reinvestment Partners' 2816 Ross Road rehabilitation (Item 10), and heard public testimony from GoDurham operators Tamika Walker and Kurt Mitchell pressing for stronger bus safety shields and reduced late-night service. Council members clashed over the Ratio States aquatics study at Wheels Fun Park (Item 18), with Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, and Pierce Freelon opposing any option that would eliminate the roller skating rink while Steve Schewel and Javiera Caballero favored gathering broad public survey data on aquatics needs. Council also received presentations on Durham's Source Water Risk and Response Plan, a proposed $300,000 Cultural Master Plan, and the Clerk's timeline to return to in-person Council meetings on November 15.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Council Announcements, and Acceptance of Manager & Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the work session to order with all seven Council members present and offered brief remarks on upcoming appointments and community updates. City Manager Wanda Page presented priority items including suspending rules to approve two time-sensitive Water Management facility contracts (Items 11 and 12), updating the 2816 Ross Road contract motion (Item 10), and withdrawing speaker Daniel Williams on Item 25. City Clerk Diana Schreiber added a priority discussion on returning Council and boards/commissions to in-person meetings.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (two separate votes on Manager and Clerk priority items)

agenda_items.title: ePlus Technology Inc. Network Infrastructure Contract for Department of Water Management
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page requested suspension of the rules due to supply-chain lead times for integral network infrastructure at the new Department of Water Management facility complex. Council unanimously suspended the rules and authorized execution of the contract with ePlus Technology Inc.

agenda_items.title: Contact Systems Inc. Audio-Visual Equipment Contract for Department of Water Management
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page requested rule suspension to lock in procurement pricing and delivery for audio-visual equipment at the Department of Water Management facility complex. After clarifying that Brady Integrated Security (Item 14) had been withdrawn by the department rather than slated for a vote today, Council suspended the rules and approved the Contact Systems contract.

agenda_items.title: Reinvestment Partners Contract Amendment for Rehabilitation of 2816 Ross Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Item 10 to review significant pandemic-driven construction cost increases on Reinvestment Partners' affordable housing rehab at 2816 Ross Road, which staff proposed revising back to the original contract figure after a previous amendment push. Members questioned project timeline delays, contractor oversight, and HUD CDBG 1.5 timeliness-test implications if funds remained unspent.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Bus Operator Safety Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: GoDurham bus operator Tamika Walker and union leader Kurt Mitchell addressed Council following recent assaults and threats against drivers, urging immediate installation of enclosed operator safety barriers and questioning late-night route hours. City Manager Wanda Page committed that Deputy City Manager Keith Chadwell and Transportation Director Sean Egan would review the concerns and follow up.

agenda_items.title: Durham Parks and Recreation Outdoor Aquatics Study Contract (Wheels Fun Park / Ratio States)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the contract with Ratio States NC to design aquatic facility plans at the former Wheels Fun Park site alongside public comment from Ideal Ortiz warning against displacing the community roller skating rink. Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, and Pierce Freelon insisted that destroying the skating rink was non-negotiable, while Steve Schewel and Javiera Caballero argued residents should first weigh in through an open survey balancing aquatics needs and skating preservation.

agenda_items.title: Source Water Risk and Response Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Department of Water Management staff presented Durham's Source Water Risk and Response Plan detailing protection of Lake Michie, Little River Reservoir, and surrounding watersheds against contamination spills and drought events. Council praised the long-term utility planning and emergency coordination protocols.

agenda_items.title: Durham Cultural Advisory Board FY23 Cultural Master Plan Funding Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff and Cultural Advisory Board representatives presented a $300,000 proposal to commission a comprehensive Cultural Master Plan ahead of FY23 budget deliberations. Council asked questions about equitable artist engagement, consultant scope, and alignment with ongoing Equity and Inclusion efforts.

agenda_items.title: Return to In-Person Meetings Timeline and Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Clerk Diana Schreiber reviewed logistics for transitioning City Council back to in-person meetings on November 15 and allowing boards and commissions to vote to return in January 2022, following up on Council's board appointments (Items 2-6). Members discussed COVID-19 masking, hybrid public comment access, and room safety protocols.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Agenda for November 1, 2021 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page recommended placing Items 1-10 and 13-20 on the November 1 Consent Agenda and Items 22-24 on the General Business Agenda Public Hearings. Council approved the agenda unanimously and adjourned at 3:43 PM.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's priority additions and revisions, including rule-suspension requests for Items 11 and 12, revised Item 10 motion language for 2816 Ross Road, and removal of speaker Daniel Williams from Item 25.

votes.item_title: Accept City Clerk's Priority Items (Return to In-Person Meetings Discussion)
votes.discussion_detail: Added the City Clerk's priority discussion regarding transitioning City Council and boards/commissions back to in-person meetings.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 11 (ePlus Technology Network Contract)
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Council rules at the work session to take immediate final action on Item 11 due to IT hardware supply-chain urgency.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Purchase Contract with ePlus Technology Inc. for Department of Water Management Network Infrastructure
votes.discussion_detail: Approved purchase contract with ePlus Technology Inc. for network infrastructure at the new Department of Water Management facility complex.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 12 (Contact Systems Audio-Visual Contract)
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Council rules at the work session to vote immediately on Item 12.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Purchase Contract with Contact Systems for Department of Water Management Audio-Visual Equipment
votes.discussion_detail: Approved contract with Contact Systems for audio-visual equipment at the Department of Water Management facility complex.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for November 1, 2021 Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Auto-captions masked the first three roll-call names under '[Music]' before capturing Freelon, Freeman, Middleton, and Reece voting Aye, and the Clerk/Mayor announced the motion passed unanimously (all 7 members present).
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted City Manager Wanda Page's recommended November 1 Regular Meeting agenda placing Items 1-10 and 13-20 on Consent and Items 22-24 on GBA Public Hearings.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Oct. 21, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Preserving Wheels Fun Park Roller Skating Rink vs. Full Aquatics Site Redevelopment (Item 18)
disagreements.summary: Council members split over how the Ratio States NC aquatics study at Wheels Fun Park should treat the existing indoor roller skating rink, with three members drawing a hard red line to preserve the rink while two others urged waiting for broad community survey input.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explicitly rule out demolishing the roller skating rink and prioritize preserving an affordable Black and community skating institution alongside aquatics improvements.
side_a_arguments: Wheels' roller skating rink is a uniquely important, beloved recreation institution for Durham families and youth of color that should not be put on the chopping block.
Community advocates, including speaker Ideal Ortiz, warned against sacrificing the only local indoor roller rink without clear guarantees.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid prejudging design scenarios before conducting an open community survey on both public aquatics needs and the rink.
side_b_arguments: Durham faces a severe shortage of public swimming pool capacity, and early engineering/community feedback should evaluate all site configurations openly.
Restricting consultant study options prematurely could limit viable ways to meet citywide aquatics equity goals.
disagreements.resolution: Informational / Placed on Consent Agenda (staff instructed to convey Council's feedback on preserving skating alongside robust public engagement)

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 18, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: The October 18, 2021 Regular Meeting featured two major split roll-call votes on Council compensation and neighborhood property tax relief alongside four unanimous approvals. Council passed Item 24 by a 6-1 margin (DeDreana Freeman voting Nay) to raise annual Council pay to $35,200 and the Mayor's salary to $40,536 effective January 1, 2022, aligning elected stipends with Durham's minimum livable wage despite Freeman's objection to raising Council pay during the pandemic after skipped employee step raises. On pulled Item 26, Council voted 2-5 (Pierce Freelon and DeDreana Freeman voting Aye) to reject Freeman's amendment adding Braggtown and Merrick-Moore to the Longtime Homeowner Grant Program due to City Attorney warnings about state constitutional constraints without prior affordable housing investments, before unanimously (7-0) expanding the pilot to Walltown and extending eligibility through the 2020 tax year. Council also approved the Consent Agenda, $60 million in TEFRA retirement facility bonds for United Methodist Retirement Homes, and the permanent citywide Outdoor Seating Ordinance (50% interior cap), all 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Recognition of Durham Firefighters, and Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel convened the meeting with all seven members present and read a recognition honoring Durham Fire Department's response to recent incidents. Following announcements and approval of priority items, Council pulled Item 7 (Outdoor Seating Ordinance) and Item 26 (Longtime Homeowner Grant Program) from the Consent Agenda and approved the remaining Consent items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Vote on City Council Salary Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting Budget Director John Allore presented the proposal aligning Council pay to the city's $35,200 full-time minimum livable wage ($40,536 for Mayor) starting January 1, 2022, followed by public speakers criticizing the timing and optics during the pandemic. Six Council members supported the raise as an equity measure to lower financial barriers to holding office, while DeDreana Freeman opposed it because city employee pay steps had been skipped and structural campaign barriers remained.

agenda_items.title: TEFRA Public Hearing and Bond Approval for United Methodist Retirement Homes (Croasdale Village)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Finance Director Christina Desiderio conducted the Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act (TEFRA) public hearing on up to $60 million in Public Finance Authority Series 2021 revenue bonds for United Methodist Retirement Homes facilities including Croasdale Village. No public speakers appeared, and Council approved the resolution unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Permanent Citywide Outdoor Seating Ordinance Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff clarified that the revised ordinance text struck out the ambiguous 40% special-exception language so businesses citywide could occupy outdoor right-of-way seating up to 50% of interior square footage subject to transportation safety rules and parking fees. Charlie Reece moved adoption with the clarified text correction.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Expansion of Longtime Homeowner Grant Program (Walltown & Amendment for Braggtown / Merrick-Moore)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Neighborhood advocates Bonita Green and Wanda Wright urged expanding city property tax relief beyond Walltown to Braggtown and Merrick-Moore, and DeDreana Freeman moved an amendment to include both neighborhoods plus the 2019-2020 tax years. City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg warned that expanding the city pilot to neighborhoods lacking prior city affordable housing investments risked state constitutional challenges under the emoluments clause, leading a 5-member majority to defeat the amendment (2-5) before unanimously (7-0) approving Walltown's addition and the 2020 tax-year extension while pledging to press Durham County to expand the countywide relief program to 60% AMI.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 18, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: City Council Salary Adjustments During Pandemic Budget Cycle (Item 24)
disagreements.summary: Six Council members voted to raise Council salaries to Durham's $35,200 livable-wage floor starting January 1, 2022 to open officeholding to working-class residents, while DeDreana Freeman dissented over optics and equity toward city employees whose step raises had been paused.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adjust Council member salaries to the city's full-time minimum livable wage ($35,200) and Mayor's salary to $40,536 effective January 1, 2022.
side_a_arguments: Council service requires full-time commitment and dozens of board obligations; sub-living stipends exclude working-class residents and low-wealth candidates.

Outgoing members (including Freelon and Schewel) argued it is an institutional equity reform comparable to recent adjustments in Charlotte and Raleigh, and the City Attorney advised Council cannot bind future budget cycles without passing it now.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose raising Council salaries at this time and prioritize restoring skipped pay steps for municipal workers and resident COVID relief.
side_b_arguments: City staff missed step raises during the pandemic and Council should focus budget dollars on city employees and residents facing hardship first.
Raising post-election stipends alone does not overcome structural fundraising and campaign barriers that prevent working-class candidates from running.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 18, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Adding Braggtown and Merrick-Moore to the Longtime Homeowner Grant Program (Item 26)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 2-5 on DeDreana Freeman's amendment to immediately include Braggtown and Merrick-Moore in the city's tax-relief pilot alongside Walltown before unanimously approving Walltown alone.
disagreements.side_a_position: Immediately expand the city's Longtime Homeowner Grant criteria to add Braggtown and Merrick-Moore for the 2019-2020 tax years.
side_a_arguments: Legacy Black homeowners in Braggtown and Merrick-Moore are facing urgent tax-bill spikes and gentrification displacement, and the countywide program only begins with 2021 taxes.
If Council can allocate $79,000 for its own raises, it should extend equivalent relief to long-time homeowners fighting to stay housed.
disagreements.side_b_position: Restrict the city pilot to Walltown based on documented city affordable housing investments while pressing Durham County to expand the countywide relief program to 60% AMI.
side_b_arguments: City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg advised that granting neighborhood tax relief where the city had not made qualifying affordable housing investments creates serious North Carolina constitutional emoluments risk.
A countywide program administered with Durham County at 60% AMI is legally sound and covers all underserved neighborhoods equitably without a patchwork city carve-out.
disagreements.resolution: Amendment Failed 2-5; original Walltown & 2020 tax-year motion subsequently Passed 7-0

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Oct 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Convening shortly after an extended closed session with Charlie Reece on an excused absence, the October 7, 2021 Work Session saw Council suspend the rules (6-0) to immediately adopt the grant budget ordinance and MOU with StepUp Durham and the Reinvent Stockton Foundation for Project Excel, Durham's guaranteed income pilot (6-0). During Citizen Matters and pulled Item 9, residents Larisa Seibel, gunshot-injury victim Sanden Nelson, and Donald Hughes underscored acute eviction and ERAP delays as Community Development Director Reginald Johnson explained Durham County DSS could no longer administer the city's $6.6 million ERAP 2 tranche, forcing the city to search urgently for an external administrator alongside approving $1.8 million in COVID ESG homelessness and shelter contracts. Council also heard Accordion Club owner Scott Ritchie's parking-loss objections on the permanent Outdoor Seating Ordinance (Item 7), reviewed the 20-year $88 million Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Action Plan (Item 18) and Green Source Advantage solar filing (Item 19), and debated commuter rail versus bus-first equity trade-offs in Phase 2 Durham County Transit Plan survey findings before setting the October 18 agenda (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Project Excel Announcements, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the work session to order at 1:05 PM after closed session with six members present and Charlie Reece on an excused absence; DeDreana Freeman did not respond during initial roll call and the first priority vote but joined before Item 5. Mark-Anthony Middleton praised StepUp Durham's fundraising for the Project Excel guaranteed income pilot, and Council approved City Manager Wanda Page's priority additions—including urgent action on Item 5 and adding Item 26 (Walltown Longtime Homeowner Grant expansion)—by a 5-0 vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-0 (Freeman absent for roll call; Reece excused)

agenda_items.title: Project Excel Guaranteed Income MOU (StepUp Durham & Reinvent Stockton Foundation) and Grant Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To meet an October/November 1 execution deadline, City Manager Wanda Page asked Council to suspend rules and adopt the Project Excel guaranteed income grant budget ordinance and MOU with StepUp Durham and the Reinvent Stockton Foundation. With DeDreana Freeman present, Council suspended the rules 6-0 and adopted the ordinance and MOU 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Urgent Eviction Prevention & ERAP 2 Access Appeals (Seibel, Nelson, Hughes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Larisa Seibel and McDougald Terrace shooting victim Sanden Nelson urged Council to rapidly reopen the city's Emergency Rental Assistance Program after County ERAP closed and DSS denied Nelson assistance while recovering from a chest wound. Later at 00:43:26, Donald Hughes pressed Council to fund immediate emergency rental relief ahead of considering Council salary increases.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Permanent Citywide Outdoor Seating Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Mr. Dubrinsky) and Transportation Director Sean Egan reviewed downtown restaurant feedback (including Elizabeth Turnbull's suggestion of pre-approved templates) and clarified the corrected 50% interior cap and citywide scope. Downtown Durham Inc.'s Nicole Thompson backed permanent outdoor dining, whereas Accordion Club owner Scott Ritchie objected that losing on-street downtown parking harms bars/restaurants outside the downtown loop and amounts to a city subsidy.

agenda_items.title: ERAP 2 ($6.6M) Administrator Search and Interlocking $1.8M ESG-CV Homelessness Contracts (Items 9-13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson explained that Durham County DSS declined to administer the city's $6.6 million ERAP 2 allocation due to capacity overload, leaving the city searching for scarce third-party vendors (including exploring Legal Aid partnerships) while City Manager Wanda Page joined the recruitment effort. Homeless System Manager Colin Davis then walked through how five interlocking ESG-CV contracts totaling $1.8 million (Families Moving Forward, Open Table Ministry, Project Access, Urban Ministries, and Volunteers of America) fund winter shelter, street homelessness prevention, and Carolina Duke Inn supportive services alongside County FEMA funds.

agenda_items.title: Quaker Creek Solar Farm & Duke Energy Green Source Advantage Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Division Manager Summer Alston and Duke Energy Green Source Advantage Manager Wendy Flener briefed Council on an urgent September 17 Utilities Commission filing adjusting interconnection rules ahead of the October 31 program deadline. Both expressed optimism that Durham's 34.9 MW solar application with Quaker Creek Solar Farm will qualify, with August 2022 UNC/military unused capacity as a backup.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Action Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Summer Alston and GDS Associates Managing Director Angela Strickland presented Durham's 30-year Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Action Plan targeting 50% GHG reduction and 80% renewables by 2030, carbon neutrality by 2040, and 100% renewable energy by 2050 via energy efficiency (12%), on-site/Green Source Advantage solar (44%), and fleet/transit electrification (44%) requiring ~$88 million in capital over 20 years offset by lifecycle savings. Council praised the concrete plan while urging minimal reliance on carbon offsets and swift EV bus/charging buildout.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Plan Phase 2 Outreach Summary & Governance Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Transportation Manager Ellen Beckman and DCHC MPO Planning Manager Aaron Cain presented Phase 2 engagement results from 2,300+ residents comparing Bus Improvements (Option A), Bus Rapid Transit (Option B), and Commuter Rail (Option C), showing daily riders and respondents of color prioritized late-night/Sunday bus frequency over rail. Mayor Schewel reiterated that the City must hold a full voting seat on the transit Staff Working Group, Mark-Anthony Middleton called for an accessible public accounting of past light-rail expenditures to rebuild trust, and Javiera Caballero urged doing both local bus improvements and regional transit.

agenda_items.title: Racial Equity Commission Nominations and Setting October 18 Council Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council confirmed consensus Racial Equity Commission nominations—Theodore Reuter (At-Large), Derrick S. Rhodes (Ward 1), Taylor Walker (Youth, pending city-residency verification), Tarik Woods (Ward 2 via vote switches), and Nisha Williams (Ward 3 via vote switches)—while re-advertising one At-Large seat. City Manager Wanda Page set the October 18 Consent Agenda (Items 1-4, 6-22, and 26) and GBA Public Hearings (Items 24-25), which Council approved 6-0 before adjourning at 4:06 PM.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence; Clerk announced motion passed 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the Manager's priority additions (requesting rule suspension on Item 5 Project Excel MOU, updating Item 13 attachment, noting Item 18 presentation, and adding supplemental Item 26 Walltown Longtime Homeowner Grant expansion). DeDreana Freeman did not answer the roll call at 00:12:40 and joined prior to Item 5.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 5 (Project Excel Guaranteed Income MOU & Budget Ordinance)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Council rules at the work session to act immediately on Item 5 before the November 1 contract execution deadline.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Adopt Guaranteed Income Grant Budget Ordinance and Authorize MOU with StepUp Durham & Reinvent Stockton Foundation
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the Mayor's for Guaranteed Income (Project Excel) grant budget ordinance and authorized the City Manager to execute the MOU with StepUp Durham and Reinvent Stockton Foundation.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for October 18, 2021 Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the October 18 Regular Meeting agenda with Items 1-4, 6-22, and 26 on Consent and Items 24-25 on General Business Agenda Public Hearings.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Oct 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: On-Street Parking Loss vs. Curbside Activation in Permanent Outdoor Seating Ordinance (Item 7)
disagreements.summary: Public comment and Council staff Q&A highlighted tension between downtown street-dining permits using metered parking spaces and off-corridor neighborhood businesses facing spill-over parking deficits.
disagreements.side_a_position: Make outdoor dining permanent citywide up to 50% of interior capacity while charging meter fees for occupied spaces and conducting curbside management review.
side_a_arguments: Outdoor dining kept locally owned downtown restaurants alive during COVID-19 and activates public streets.
Requiring restaurants to pay the meter rate avoids subsidizing parking loss, and the ordinance expands availability citywide alongside design templates.
disagreements.side_b_position: Address severe parking deficits in Central Park / Old North Durham and avoid effectively subsidizing downtown corridor businesses that convert public spaces.
side_b_arguments: Accordion Club owner Scott Ritchie testified that Geer Street businesses already suffer from overflow event parking deficits and lack sidewalks/street space to benefit equally from street-cafe permits.
Sidewalk cafes adjacent to businesses are reasonable, whereas claiming on-street parking spaces reduces affordable evening parking supply.
disagreements.resolution: Placed on Consent Agenda with transportation staff committing to curbside management coordination and neighbor notification review

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Oct 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Durham County Transit Plan Priorities: Bus Service Equity, Commuter Rail Costs, and City Governance Seat (Item 23)
disagreements.summary: Council and transit staff examined diverging priorities between overall survey respondents favoring commuter rail and POC/daily riders prioritizing late-night/Sunday bus service, alongside City governance representation and light-rail accountability.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize immediate frequency, late-night/weekend reliability, and a full City voting seat on the Staff Working Group alongside pursuing regional rail without over-promising.
side_a_arguments: Jillian Johnson emphasized that transit-dependent riders and POC respondents ranked evening/Sunday bus improvements far higher than commuter rail.

Steve Schewel argued Durham owns the GoDurham bus system and contributes substantial property taxes, making a voting City seat on the Staff Working Group essential, while Mark-Anthony Middleton called for transparent accounting of past light-rail expenditures.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain focus on dual local-and-regional investments including Option C (commuter rail) connectivity, especially near permanently subsidized downtown affordable housing.
side_b_arguments: Javiera Caballero argued Durham will fail unless it delivers both better local bus service and a regional transit system (Options A and C combined).

Schewel also noted Option C nearly doubles 45-minute job accessibility from subsidized downtown housing at 519 E. Main St., Willard St., and DHA sites, whereas Oxford Manor remains an accessibility outlier under all plans.
disagreements.resolution: Informational / Staff directed to bring recommended final transit plan and revised interlocal governance agreement in January 2022

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 4, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: With Charlie Reece on an excused absence, the six-member City Council deadlocked 3-3 on Item 16, defeating Epcon Communities' 133-home Courtyards at Doc Nichols annexation and rezoning (Ayes: Pierce Freelon, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton; Nays: Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero) over tensions between accessible senior housing and solar conduit proffers versus low 1.8 units/acre density, $500k+ pricing, stream crossings, and the Planning Commission's 0-12 denial. Earlier, Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (6-0, excluding Items 10 and 19). On pulled items, Council passed the $6,000 Poet Laureate Pilot Program (Item 10, 6-0), approved a CVS Health weekly COVID-19 employee testing contract up to $839,440 (Item 19, two 6-0 votes, with DeDreana Freeman voting 'very hesitantly aye' over the $70/month health insurance wellness surcharge), and adopted the Resolution in Support of Safe and Healthy Housing (Item 21, 6-0).

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Proclamations, and Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order with six members present and Charlie Reece on an excused absence, reading proclamations including encouraging voter turnout for the next day's election. Council pulled Item 10 (Poet Laureate Pilot) and Item 19 (Weekly COVID-19 Testing LOA) for public speakers and approved the remaining Consent Agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated Annexation, Zoning Map Change, and FLUM Amendment — Courtyards at Doc Nichols
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a lengthy public hearing on Epcon Communities' proposal to annex 75 acres on Doc Nichols Road and build 133 single-story accessible homes (1.8 units/acre) featuring a $120,000 affordable housing contribution, 33% tree preservation, and Durham's first solar-conduit proffer despite a 0-12 Planning Commission recommendation for denial. Following neighborhood opposition over traffic and stream impacts alongside union/equity support for aging-in-place housing, Council deadlocked 3-3, causing the project to fail.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: City of Durham Poet Laureate Pilot Program ($6,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After hearing public comment regarding the $6,000 pilot program funding and selection structure recommended by the Durham Cultural Advisory Board, Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson moved and Pierce Freelon seconded approval of the Poet Laureate pilot. Council passed the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Weekly COVID-19 Employee Testing Letter of Agreement with CVS Health ($839,440 Cap)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council heard from staff and public comment on the 12-week on-site CVS Health weekly COVID-19 testing contract paired with Option 3's $70/month 2022 wellness insurance surcharge for unvaccinated employees. DeDreana Freeman voiced lingering reservations about coercion and employee impact—casting a 'very hesitantly aye' vote—as Council passed both motions authorizing the LOA up to $839,440 and allowing minor contract negotiations within that cap.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Safe and Healthy Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up DeDreana Freeman's resolution affirming HUD healthy-home principles and city support for tenant protections against mold, lead, pests, carbon monoxide, and radon. Following one public speaker's comments, Council adopted the resolution 6-0 and adjourned at 9:13 PM.

votes.item_title: Approve Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 10 and 19)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved Consent Agenda items excluding pulled Items 10 (Poet Laureate Pilot) and 19 (CVS Health COVID-19 Testing LOA).

votes.item_title: Item 16: Consolidated Annexation and Zoning Map Change (Courtyards at Doc Nichols)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence; under North Carolina municipal rules a 3-3 tie defeats the motion.
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded approval of the Courtyards at Doc Nichols annexation/rezoning at 01:37:07; after Council remarks, roll call at 01:50:44 tied 3-3, failing for lack of a majority.

votes.item_title: Item 10: Approve City of Durham Poet Laureate Pilot Program
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $6,000 Poet Laureate Pilot Program recommended by the Durham Cultural Advisory Board.

votes.item_title: Item 19 (Motion 1): Authorize City Manager to Execute CVS Health Weekly COVID-19 Testing LOA Up to $839,440
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence; DeDreana Freeman stated she voted 'very hesitantly aye' out of concern over surcharge impact on unvaccinated workers.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized the City Manager to execute the Letter of Agreement with CVS Health for 12 weeks of mandatory weekly COVID-19 testing for unvaccinated city employees, not to exceed $839,440 (funded via the $70/month 2022 wellness surcharge structure).

votes.item_title: Item 19 (Motion 2): Authorize City Manager to Negotiate Contract Changes Within the $839,440 Cap
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized the City Manager to make minor contractual adjustments with CVS Health provided the $839,440 contract ceiling is not exceeded.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Adopt Resolution in Support of Safe and Healthy Housing
votes.notes: Charlie Reece had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the Resolution in Support of Safe and Healthy Housing championed by Council Member DeDreana Freeman, rooted in HUD's Basic Principles of Healthful Housing.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 4, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Courtyards at Doc Nichols Annexation & Rezoning — Low-Density Suburban Growth vs. Accessible Housing & Solar Proffers (Item 16)
disagreements.summary: With Charlie Reece absent, City Council deadlocked 3-3 on Epcon Communities' 133-unit accessible housing proposal in Southeast Durham, defeating the project.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 75-acre annexation and rezoning based on accessible aging-in-place housing, environmental proffers, and $120,000 affordable housing contribution.
side_a_arguments: Provided Durham's first-ever solar conduit residential proffer, 33% tree preservation, and $120,000 dedicated to the city's affordable housing fund.

Middleton and Freelon noted the single-story zero-step courtyard model serves seniors and disability needs in an underserved area, and rejected applying the un-adopted draft Southeast Focus Area Plan against a compliant application.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the rezoning as incompatible low-density greenfield sprawl with watershed/stream crossing impacts and luxury price points.
side_b_arguments: At 1.8 units/acre and $500,000-$550,000 home prices, the suburban layout conflicts with smart-growth transit/infrastructure efficiency and the emerging Southeast planning vision.
The Planning Commission recommended denial unanimously (0-12), citing environmental impacts of the stream crossing, buffer encroachment, and neighborhood road safety concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Failed 3-3 on tie vote

meetings.title: Virtual Special Council Meeting Sept 30, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Called on emergency notice ahead of an October 1, 2021 state opt-in deadline flagged by North Carolina Attorney General Josh Stein, the September 30 Special Meeting saw all seven Council members convene at 10:00 AM and vote unanimously (7-0) to adopt the resolution approving the North Carolina Memorandum of Agreement on opioid litigation settlement proceeds. Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole explained that signing onto the federal settlement and state MOA ties Durham into North Carolina's share of the $26 billion national opioid settlement ($22.7 billion allocated directly to states and localities), with Durham's proceeds restricted to approved opioid remediation programs beginning in 2022 and enhanced by 5% if both the City and County participate. Council also unanimously (7-0) granted Charlie Reece excused absences for the upcoming October 4 Regular Meeting and October 7 Work Session before adjourning at 10:14 AM.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Approving North Carolina Memorandum of Agreement on Opioid Litigation Settlement Proceeds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the 10:00 AM emergency meeting with all seven Council members present after receiving an urgent call from NC Attorney General Josh Stein ahead of an October 1 deadline. Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole explained the two-prong federal opt-in and state MOA governing local spending menus from the $26 billion national opioid settlement (with funds starting in 2022 and DeDreana Freeman highlighting the 5% bonus for joint city-county sign-on), and Council adopted the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Charlie Reece Excused Absence Requests for October 4 and October 7, 2021 Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece requested excused absences for the October 4 Regular Meeting and October 7 Work Session to attend an in-person conference scheduled six months prior. Council unanimously approved the excused absences 7-0 and adjourned at 10:14 AM.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Approving North Carolina Memorandum of Agreement on Proceeds Relating to Opioid Litigation Settlement
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the state MOA resolution committing Durham to the national $26 billion opioid litigation settlement ahead of the October 1 deadline, unlocking restricted remediation funding beginning in 2022.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absences for Council Member Charlie Reece (Oct. 4 & Oct. 7, 2021 Meetings)
votes.discussion_detail: Granted excused absences for Council Member Charlie Reece for the October 4 Regular Meeting and October 7 Work Session.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Sept. 23, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the September 23, 2021 Work Session opened with Council approving City Manager priority items (7-0), scheduling a closed session on Darryl Howard v. City of Durham (6-0 recorded on roll call), and suspending rules to immediately purchase 12 replacement GoDurham Access vehicles (Item 5, 7-0) to capture $20,000+ in expiring contract savings. Council heard urgent safety pleas from GoDurham drivers Tamika Walker and Christopher Patterson following onboard assaults and shooting threats, and gave unanimous consensus on Item 20 to draft an expansion of the Longtime Homeowner Grant Program to include Walltown alongside the joint County Low-Income Homeowners Relief Program. Extended debate centered on City Council Salary Adjustments (Item 3), where supporters backed raising pay to Durham's livable wage ($35,200 Council / ~$42,000 Mayor) while DeDreana Freeman, Charlie Reece, and speaker Jacqueline Wagstaff questioned pandemic timing, skipped staff pay steps, and taxpayer input—prompting Council consensus to hold a public hearing first—and on Item 19, where Council endorsed HR Option 3 charging unvaccinated workers a $70/month 2022 wellness surcharge to fund CVS weekly testing. Council also heard a GoDurham Access overview from Transit Director Sean Egan (with driver Marie Faison urging better vendor accountability) and Interim Police Chief Shari Montgomery's Q2 Crime Report showing lower property crime and 23 homicides amid sworn staffing at 85% and intense public criticism from Donald Hughes and Jacqueline Wagstaff.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Manager Priority Items, and Darryl Howard Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the 1:00 PM work session to order with all seven members present; Charlie Reece requested expanding the Longtime Homeowner Grant to Walltown, DeDreana Freeman circulated an updated Safe and Healthy Homes resolution (removing the voluntary certification clause per Schewel), and Mark-Anthony Middleton announced the 1000 Black Men anti-violence kickoff at Hayti Heritage Center. Council approved the Manager's priority additions 7-0 and voted to hold a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) on Darryl Howard v. City of Durham.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (7-0 Priority Items; 6-0 Closed Session recorded)

agenda_items.title: Purchase of 12 Replacement Light Transit Vehicles for GoDurham Access
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because an existing procurement contract expired prior to the October 4 regular meeting, City Manager Wanda Page asked Council to suspend rules to save over $20,000 on 12 GoDurham Access vans; Sean Egan confirmed no suitable electric/hybrid paratransit cutaways were yet available on the market. Council suspended the rules 7-0 and authorized the purchase 7-0.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Bus Operator Safety Crisis (Walker & Patterson)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eleven-year GoDurham driver Tamika Walker and 23-year veteran Christopher Patterson testified about recent assaults, a 'light the terminal up' gunfire threat at Durham Station, inadequate barriers, and an operator terminated after defending himself. Transportation Director Sean Egan detailed police patrols, conflict-de-escalation training, and plans to retrofit buses with protective barriers, while Jillian Johnson's observation about people hanging out on free buses drew pushback from Mark-Anthony Middleton (and later speaker Donald Hughes).

agenda_items.title: Low-Income Homeowners Relief ILA and Walltown Expansion of Longtime Homeowner Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Bertha Johnson and County Tax/DSS officials appeared for the joint Low-Income Homeowners Relief Program ILA, after which Charlie Reece presented Brandon Williams' research (~$27,000 cost estimate via DataWorks NC) showing prior city housing investments in Walltown. All seven Council members gave thumbs-up consensus directing staff to return with criteria adding Walltown and opening the 2020 tax year while continuing pressure on Durham County to raise countywide relief to 60% AMI.

agenda_items.title: City Council Salary Adjustments Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following opposition from speaker Jacqueline Wagstaff arguing Council seats are part-time public service under the Charter, Acting Budget Director John Allore and City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg confirmed Council could set salaries to Durham's minimum livable wage ($35,200 Council / ~$42,000 Mayor) only for the current budget cycle rather than binding a future fiscal year. Pierce Freelon, Jillian Johnson, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Javiera Caballero, and Steve Schewel endorsed livable pay to lower class barriers, while Charlie Reece expressed ambivalence over spending $78,000 and DeDreana Freeman opposed raises before restoring employee pay steps, yielding thumbs-up consensus to schedule a public hearing.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus to schedule a public hearing

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: COVID CDBG Rules, Fire Station 18 Solar, Poet Laureate, and Immigrant/Haitian Refugee Affairs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson clarified HUD deadlines on COVID CDBG public-service caps (Item 4), General Services confirmed Fire Station 18 includes rooftop solar like Station 17 (Item 9), Council reviewed the $5,000 stipend Poet Laureate timeline with Freelon proposing honoring Pauli Murray (Item 10), and NIS confirmed the Immigrant/Refugee Affairs ILA (Item 11) encompasses Haitian migrants per DeDreana Freeman's request.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Access Paratransit Services Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Sean Egan outlined the 5-year City-County paratransit merger ($5.4M annual budget, $48 per trip vs. <$4 fixed-route), upcoming same-day service pilots, livable-wage targets for National Express Transit's 62 drivers, and bus-stop ADA accessibility upgrades. Nineteen-year driver Marie Faison questioned National Express's lack of paratransit roots and commitment to community, while DeDreana Freeman criticized the North Carolina General Assembly for zeroing out ROAP/SMAP rural transit grants.

agenda_items.title: Durham Police Department 2021 Second Quarter Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Police Chief Shari Montgomery reported that in the first half of 2021 Part 1 violent crime fell 4% and property crime dropped 14% while criminal homicides rose to 23 (up from 16), priority-one average response times climbed to 6.1 minutes (target 5.8) due to sworn staffing dropping to 85%, and Misdemeanor Diversion achieved 100% completion across 374 enrollees. Public speakers Donald Hughes and Jacqueline Wagstaff lambasted Council over gun violence, criticized Johnson's bus-fare comment, demanded ShotSpotter/Black-led funding, and sought NCCU/Duke campus crime inclusion; Montgomery also clarified the body-worn camera audit stemmed from computer video tagging errors rather than officers disabling cameras.

agenda_items.title: Mandatory Weekly COVID-19 Employee Testing Options, Clerk Appointments, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR Director Regina Youngblood and City Manager Wanda Page presented three options to recover on-site CVS Health 12-week testing costs from unvaccinated workers, recommending Option 3: adding vaccination as a 2022 wellness requirement backed by a $70/month health insurance surcharge. All seven members signaled support (with Freeman urging HR to guard against anxiety-related disciplinary dings), heard Clerk nominations for Discover Durham and HSAC, and adjourned into the Darryl Howard v. City of Durham closed session at 03:26:36.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus support for Option 3 (contract returned for vote)

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the Manager's priority additions including requesting immediate action on Item 5 (GoDurham Access buses), adding supplemental Item 19 (COVID testing options) and Item 20 (Low-Income Homeowners Relief ILA), and updating attachments for Items 13 and 14.

votes.item_title: Hold Closed Session Pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for Attorney-Client Consultation (Darryl Howard v. City of Durham)
votes.notes: Six roll-call Ayes were captured in the transcript before the Mayor thanked Council at 00:21:14; Charlie Reece was present at the 00:04:38 roll call and voted Aye on the 00:19:21 and 00:23:52 roll calls.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session at the conclusion of the work session for attorney-client consultation regarding federal trial posture in Darryl Howard v. City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 5 (Purchase of 12 Replacement Light Transit Vehicles for GoDurham Access)
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Council rules to authorize an urgent fleet contract before expiration.

votes.item_title: Item 5: Authorize City Manager to Execute Purchase Contract for 12 Replacement GoDurham Access Light Transit Vehicles
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized purchase of 12 replacement light transit vehicles for GoDurham Access, saving over $20,000 before the existing contract expired ahead of the October 4 meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Sept. 23, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: City Council Salary Adjustments and Pandemic Budget Priorities (Item 3)
disagreements.summary: A Council majority endorsed raising Council stipends to Durham's livable-wage floor ($35,200 Council / ~$42,000 Mayor) to make officeholding accessible to working-class residents, while DeDreana Freeman opposed moving ahead while employee pay steps had been skipped and Charlie Reece remained torn over spending $78,000.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance an ordinance aligning Council salaries with Durham's full-time minimum livable wage, subject to a public hearing.
side_a_arguments: Pierce Freelon, Jillian Johnson, Mark-Anthony Middleton, Javiera Caballero, and Steve Schewel argued sub-living stipends lock working people out of devoting full-time hours to Council service.
Both Charlotte and Raleigh have adopted comparable compensation updates, and City Attorney/Budget staff confirmed Council cannot defer binding a future budget year.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose or question advancing Council raises during pandemic hardship when staff pay steps were skipped and residents need direct relief.
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman argued Council should focus first on restoring skipped employee step raises and doubted stipends would overcome campaign cost barriers.
Charlie Reece questioned whether $78,000 was the best pandemic budget choice while Jacqueline Wagstaff urged taxpayer control rather than moving from a part-time stipend model.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus thumbs-up to schedule a public hearing before taking a formal vote

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Sept. 23, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: GoDurham Bus Operator Assaults and Unintended Consequences of Fare-Free Transit
disagreements.summary: Following GoDurham operator testimony on assaults and gunfire threats, members and public speakers differed sharply on whether fare-free transit contributed to onboard disorder.
disagreements.side_a_position: Affirm free transit while noting that zero-fare policy increased individuals riding with nowhere to go, creating more opportunities for conflict.
side_a_arguments: Jillian Johnson emphasized fare-free buses remain a fabulous policy choice that must continue, while noting one unintended consequence reported in driver meetings was more people hanging out on buses.
Drivers cited mask-mandate enforcement conflicts alongside loss of prior private security at Durham Station.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject linking zero-fare transit access to criminal violence or assaults against drivers.
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton stressed that fare price points do not deter violence and warned against any narrative stigmatizing low-income Black and brown transit riders.
Speaker Donald Hughes called linking free bus expansion to driver assaults 'appalling' and unsupported by data.
disagreements.resolution: Informational / Staff directed to pursue bus barriers, DPD coordination, and de-escalation training
