meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Sept. 20, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In a brisk, completely unanimous session with all seven members present, the September 20, 2021 Regular Meeting opened with Hispanic Heritage Month and Durham Historic Preservation recognitions before approving the Consent Agenda 7-0, encompassing multi-family housing bonds (Crescent Drive, 300 East Main, JFK Towers), 8 diesel and 6 electric GoDurham buses, water/stormwater engineering contracts, Eno River Association parcel donations, DPAC President's Club lease amendments, and a Digital Equity Plan resolution. Following public hearings on three General Business Agenda zoning cases, Council unanimously approved all three rezonings and their accompanying statutory consistency statements (six 7-0 roll calls): 1908 Cedar Street from RS-20 to RU-5 (Item 32), a text-only development plan update at 2301 South Miami Boulevard (Item 33), and The Wine Outlet parcel consolidation at 4823/4827 Hopson Road (Item 34). No policy splits occurred during Council deliberations.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Proclamations, and Omnibus Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following opening ceremonial recognitions and announcements, Mayor Steve Schewel read the Consent Agenda including affordable housing multi-family bond authorizations, purchase of 8 diesel and 6 electric buses, infrastructure engineering contracts, Lyon Park design-build, and the Digital Equity Plan resolution. Council approved the Consent Agenda unanimously 7-0 without pulling any items.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change Public Hearing: 1908 Cedar Street (RS-20 to RU-5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented case Z2000018 rezoning a single 1908 Cedar Street parcel from Residential Suburban 20 (RS-20) to Residential Urban 5 (RU-5) to match surrounding residential urban zoning and water/sewer infrastructure. Following unrelated public safety remarks from one speaker during the open hearing, Council unanimously adopted both the UDO amendment and consistency statement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (both UDO amendment and consistency statement)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change Public Hearing: 2301 South Miami Boulevard (CN to CG(D) Text-Only Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a text-only Commercial General development-plan amendment at 2301 South Miami Boulevard (modifying permitted site design/access elements for the commercial corner parcel) and heard from applicant representatives including Kirkendall and Long. With no opposing speakers, Council adopted the zoning change and consistency statement 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (both UDO amendment and consistency statement)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change Public Hearing: The Wine Outlet, 4823 & 4827 Hopson Road (OI & CN(D) to CN(D))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented The Wine Outlet rezoning combining parcels at 4823 and 4827 Hopson Road from Office/Institutional and Commercial Neighborhood (Development Plan) into uniform Commercial Neighborhood with Development Plan (CN(D)). With no public opposition, Council adopted the UDO amendment and consistency statement 7-0 and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (both UDO amendment and consistency statement)

meetings.title: Special Virtual Durham Planning Commission & City Council Meeting 9/14/21 at 4 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: On September 14, 2021, the Durham City Council and Durham Planning Commission held a joint special virtual meeting focused on aligning development review and discussing Planning staff's draft recommendations for the Southeast Durham Focus Area. Council excused Pierce Freelon's absence by a 5-0 roll-call vote (Mayor Schewel presided without voicing an audible vote). Senior Planner Kayla Seibel and Planning staff presented a draft place type map and 24 draft policies governing rapid suburban growth east of Kemp Road and along US 70 and NC 98 ahead of Comprehensive Plan adoption in late 2022. Members of both bodies debated how much legal and policy weight to give unadopted draft recommendations in pending rezonings, with Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole and Charlie Reece warning against unenforceable denials while Mayor Steve Schewel insisted the draft provides important interim policy guidance.

agenda_items.title: Joint Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absence for Pierce Freelon
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel and Planning Commission Chair Nathaniel Busby convened the joint special virtual meeting at 4:00 PM. Council members Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, Charlie Reece, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Mayor Steve Schewel answered roll call, and Council voted to excuse Pierce Freelon's absence.

agenda_items.title: Bridging Planning Commission Recommendations and City Council Rezoning Decisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel and Planning Commission Chair Busby framed the joint session around closing the gap between Planning Commission denial recommendations and subsequent City Council approvals in Southeast Durham. Busby noted that developers often hold back community concessions until after Planning Commission hearings, making Planning Commissioners feel bypassed.

agenda_items.title: Southeast Focus Area Draft Place Type Map and 24 Policy Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Kayla Seibel and Scott Whiteman presented interim draft recommendations for Southeast Durham bounded roughly by US 70, Sherron Road, NC 98, and the county line, referencing Fire Station 17 and the Southeast Regional Lift Station. Draft proposals included Future Growth Area designations east of Kemp and Virgil Roads pending fire station capacity, Mixed Residential Neighborhood, 15-Minute Neighborhood centers, Policy 2B barring age-restriction proffers, Policy 3A prioritizing non-car infrastructure, and Policy 4B requiring half of preserved tree canopy outside stream buffers.

agenda_items.title: Legal Enforceability, Interim Weight of Draft Policies, Affordability, and Tree Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Javiera Caballero joined Planning Commissioners in debating whether draft policies should use binding 'shall' language, how to handle pending East-of-Kemp cases, and what affordability or tree-save proffers are legally permissible under North Carolina statute. Planning Director Sara Young and Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole advised using draft guidance carefully because it is not yet adopted policy, whereas Mayor Steve Schewel rejected dismissing the draft with 'a grain of salt' before adjourning at 5:18 PM.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Council Member Pierce Freelon
votes.notes: Roll call at 00:05:23 recorded explicit ayes from Johnson, Caballero, Reece, Freeman, and Middleton; Mayor Steve Schewel presided and announced the motion passed without voicing an audible aye on the transcript, and Freelon was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council excused the absence of Council Member Pierce Freelon at the opening of the joint special meeting with the Planning Commission.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special Virtual Durham Planning Commission & City Council Meeting 9/14/21 at 4 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Interim Legal Weight and Binding Language of Draft Southeast Focus Area Policies
disagreements.summary: Council members, Planning Commissioners, and legal/planning staff differed over how forcefully the unadopted Southeast Focus Area draft recommendations should be worded and applied to pending rezonings before formal Comprehensive Plan adoption in late 2022.
disagreements.side_a_position: Treat draft policies cautiously as non-binding advisory guidance and avoid legally unenforceable 'shall' mandates or density caps that risk court reversal.
side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece (00:27:38, 01:11:48) cautioned against promising residents binding affordability AMI limits, traffic rules, or tree-preservation mandates that North Carolina law and existing UDO/Comprehensive Plan standards cannot sustain on judicial review.

Planning Director Sara Young (00:31:28) and Deputy City Attorney Don O'Toole (01:13:45) explained that the draft recommendations are not yet adopted policy and therefore carry limited legal weight compared to adopted plans and UDO rules.
disagreements.side_b_position: Apply the draft Southeast Focus Area map and 24 policies as strong interim guidance and strengthen policy language from 'should' toward enforceable expectations.
side_b_arguments: Planning Commissioners Baker, Durkin, and Amendolia argued that advisory 'should' phrasing invites developers to ignore community feedback and urged clearer commitments around density, affordability, and tree protection.

Mayor Steve Schewel (01:17:07) stated he would not take the draft recommendations with 'a grain of salt' and would treat them as significant interim guidance reflecting extensive Planning Commission and staff work.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; staff committed to refining the 24 draft policies for future public review and Comprehensive Plan integration while legal counsel advised keeping interim project reviews grounded in adopted ordinances.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Sept. 9, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 9, 2021 City Council Work Session, Council approved three procedural 6-0 roll-call votes (excusing Charlie Reece's absence, accepting City Manager priority items, and setting the regular meeting agenda) alongside unanimous thumbs-up consensus on several community and cultural proposals including Poet Laureate planning, a Workers' Rights Commission PRO Act resolution, Youth Board pilot appointments, and $150,000 per year for two years matching Durham County for Aging Well Durham. The central policy clash occurred over Item 25, a $69,700-per-week CVS Health contract for mandatory weekly COVID-19 testing of unvaccinated city employees; following opposition from Mayor Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece (by email) to using Health Insurance Fund dollars for testing instead of a vaccine mandate or higher employee premiums, City Manager Wanda Page withdrew the October 18 testing rollout to return with mandate and premium options. Council also reviewed the $51.8 million ARPA equity allocation framework, an unexpected $26.6 million FY2020-21 General Fund positive variance that reduced reliance on ARPA revenue replacement, 911 call-center staffing shortages and mutual-aid routing concerns, and EVICTION diversion data showing a 76% Legal Aid tenancy-preservation rate.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence, Consensus Directives, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the work session with six members present and excused Charlie Reece's absence by a 6-0 vote. Council gave unanimous thumbs-up consensus to schedule discussions on a Durham Poet Laureate (Sept. 23), a Workers' Rights Commission PRO Act resolution (Oct. 7), and an Office on Youth board-representation pilot (Oct. 21), delegated Mark-Anthony Middleton and Charlie Reece to review Council travel allotments, and voted 6-0 to accept City Manager priority items.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (Excused Absence and Priority Items); Consensus thumbs-up on calendar additions

agenda_items.title: Eviction Crisis, ERAP Delays, Spanish Interpreters, Braggtown Bus Service, and Tax Relief
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community speakers Angela Vick Lewis and Lissa Cybel reported up to 81-82 Friday courthouse eviction hearings, DSS Emergency Rental Assistance delays, and a shortage of Spanish-speaking court interpreters. Stella Adams and Vanessa Evans raised Braggtown Route 9 bus inequities and Medicaid paratransit fees, while Jim Svar urged using ARPA funds to expand the Longtime Homeowner Grant Program citywide.

agenda_items.title: Board Stipend Bylaws (Item 8), Attendance Report (Item 10), and Bruce Allen Construction (Item 27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Item 8 on opt-in self-attestation stipends for board and commission members (with Mark-Anthony Middleton emphasizing equitable access), Item 10's annual attendance report flagging members under 50% attendance, and Item 27 (stormwater contract SD-2012-04 with Bruce Allen Construction), where staff confirmed a successful good-faith-effort appeal and agreed to document Equity & Inclusion confirmation.

agenda_items.title: Employee COVID-19 Mandatory Weekly Testing Contract with CVS Health and Vaccine Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a proposed 12-week CVS Health contract costing $69,700 per week from the self-insured Health Insurance Fund to test unvaccinated employees starting October 18. After Mayor Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece (via email read into the record) opposed spending taxpayer/fund dollars on weekly tests without a vaccine mandate or higher employee premiums, and other members debated UE150 proposals, work-hours testing, and attrition risk, City Manager Wanda Page agreed to pull the item and return with vaccine-mandate and cost-recoupment options.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Held / Removed from regular agenda by consensus

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) $51.8M Allocation Process and Equity Scorecard
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson and Leela Pedersen outlined Durham's $51.8 million ARPA allocation ($25.9M first tranche received; $7.3M spent on hazard pay; over 80 community proposals), an Equity Impact Assessment tool, a draft scoring rubric, two temporary FTEs in Budget and Finance, and a community review committee. Pierce Freelon and DeDreana Freeman requested vetting scorecard weights with Black-led community organizations.

agenda_items.title: FY2020-21 Fourth Quarter Financial Report and Fund Balance Surplus
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff (John Allore) reported a $26.6 million General Fund positive variance—comprising $8.4 million in underspending and $18.2 million in stronger-than-projected revenues led by $14 million in sales taxes and $5 million in property taxes—pushing projected unrestricted fund balance to $67.8 million ($34.7M above the 16.7% policy floor). Because General Fund revenue recovered, Durham would not need to spend ARPA funds on General Fund revenue replacement, though Transit (-$1M) and Parking (-$2.9M) funds ran deficits.

agenda_items.title: Durham Master Aging Plan (Aging Well Durham) Funding Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Master Aging Plan leaders Gina Upchurch, Chalisia Howard-Martinez, Dr. Janet Bettger, and Joy Gardner requested $150,000 annually for two years to match Durham County funding and launch community aging hubs. Council gave unanimous thumbs-up consensus directing staff to bring back a funding motion, likely from unassigned General Fund balance.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus thumbs-up directing staff funding proposal

agenda_items.title: 911 Emergency Communications Staffing Shortages, Call Metrics, and Routing Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Communications Director Randy Beaman and Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson reported 28 FTE vacancies (and 11 part-time vacancies), a five-year-high 27,009 calls in July 2021, 75.27% answered within 10 seconds (below the 90% goal), 81.03% within 20 seconds (below the 95% goal), and a 10.41-second average wait. Mark-Anthony Middleton criticized ending Wake/Raleigh mutual-aid call routing, while DeDreana Freeman recounted a four-minute wait during a Main Street shooting and proposed designating telecommunicators as First Responders.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Rental Assistance (ERAP) and Legal Aid Eviction Diversion Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson reported 6,400 ERAP applications submitted, roughly $6 million disbursed across about 1,200 households, and more than 3,600 active applications in process, while Legal Aid closed 650 cases with 76% (562) achieving tenancy preservation. Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson urged expanding Legal Aid funding by roughly $500,000 annually, and Mayor Steve Schewel asked staff to review Legal Aid's proposal for potential fund-balance support.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Nominations and Approval of Sept. 20 Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Clerk staff presented board and commission nominations, and Council voted 6-0 to settle the regular meeting docket placing Items 1-24 and 26-28 on Consent and Items 32-34 on General Business Public Hearings while holding Item 25, adjourning at 6:07 PM.

votes.notes: Charlie Reece was excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council excused the absence of Council Member Charlie Reece at the beginning of the work session.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items (Item 25 Rules Suspension, Item 30 and Items 35-36 Attachments)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council accepted the City Manager's priority additions and updated attachments for Items 25, 30, 35, and 36.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Sept. 9, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: City Funding of Weekly COVID-19 Testing (Item 25 CVS Health Contract) vs. Vaccine Mandate or Employee-Paid Testing
disagreements.summary: Council divided sharply over City Manager Wanda Page's proposed $69,700/week CVS Health contract to fund weekly testing for unvaccinated employees out of the self-insured Health Insurance Fund, ultimately pulling the item before a formal vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Do not spend taxpayer or shared employee Health Insurance Fund dollars to subsidize ongoing weekly testing for unvaccinated staff; move toward a vaccine mandate or higher health premiums/employee-paid testing.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Steve Schewel (01:14:19, 02:02:35) argued that paying nearly $70,000/week unfairly shifts costs onto taxpayers and vaccinated employees, urging either a vaccine mandate or requiring unvaccinated workers to pay for testing or higher premiums.
Charlie Reece (via email read at 02:08:53) opposed subsidizing weekly testing and favored a vaccine mandate with medical/religious exemptions and higher premiums for unvaccinated staff.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain a measured transition toward vaccination while addressing UE150 labor concerns, work-hours testing access, attrition risks, and EBO/diversity standards before imposing punitive penalties or mandates.
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton (01:19:41, 02:10:48), Jillian Johnson (01:47:01, 02:05:02), Javiera Caballero (01:28:16, 02:05:48), and Pierce Freelon (01:34:38, 02:06:55) questioned attrition impacts (with HR staff Anna Davis citing 3% at Houston Methodist and 2% at UVA), testing on work hours, UE150 union proposals, and delay options to examine premium recoupment or vaccine mandates.
Donald Hughes (01:43:41) urged Council not to waive Equal Business Opportunity diversity goals on the testing contract.
disagreements.resolution: By consensus (02:14:26-02:19:43), Item 25 was held off the regular meeting agenda, and City Manager Wanda Page agreed to cancel the October 18 testing start and return with data and revised options for a vaccine mandate or premium adjustments.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Sept. 9, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: 911 Alternate Routing Termination and Call-Center Response Adequacy
disagreements.summary: Following staff's presentation showing 28 FTE vacancies and sub-target 911 answer speeds in July 2021, council members criticized terminating Raleigh mutual-aid backup routing and questioned emergency response safety.
disagreements.side_a_position: Management decisions ending mutual-aid overflow routing to Raleigh and acute dispatcher shortages are compromising urgent resident safety and require immediate corrective remedies.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton (04:15:40, 04:28:33) criticized the ending of mutual-aid routing with Raleigh and questioned whether residents in critical danger are waiting unacceptably long.

DeDreana Freeman (04:23:09) cited a four-minute wait during a Main Street shooting call she experienced and proposed a resolution classifying 911 telecommunicators as First Responders to bolster pay and retention.
disagreements.side_b_position: Raleigh's center faced parallel staffing/routing constraints, and Durham is addressing record July call volume (27,009 calls) through active hiring classes and compensation steps.
side_b_arguments: Director Randy Beaman and Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson explained operational factors behind the mutual-aid pause, noted a hiring pipeline underway, and cautioned that August metrics would likely mirror July's backlog.
disagreements.resolution: Informational report; no formal vote was taken while staff continued recruitment and Council flagged First Responder classification for potential follow-up.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Sept. 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Because Mayor Steve Schewel had lost his voice (with a negative PCR test), Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson assumed the gavel at 00:02:33 and presided over the September 7, 2021 regular City Council meeting. Council unanimously approved 7-0 a FY22 budget amendment for the City Attorney's Office adding an attorney FTE and practice-management software, as well as the Consent Agenda (Items 1 and 3-6), while Schewel announced closed-session performance-evaluation salary increases for City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg ($206,700) and City Clerk Diana Schreiber ($103,175). The remainder of the meeting centered on the continued public hearing for Item 8, the consolidated annexation and rezoning of 79.478 acres at 1051 Olive Branch Road (Pulte Home Company LLC, up to 284 units, PDR 3.700/FJB), which the Planning Commission had recommended denying 1-11 in April 2021 and which Council had continued from June 21. Following extended debate over post-Planning Commission developer revisions, cemetery grave relocation consents, and suburban sprawl, Council approved the annexation and rezoning 5-2 with DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece dissenting, before adopting the statutory consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Mayor Pro Tem Gavel Handoff, National Recovery Month Proclamation, and Charter Officer Salaries
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Mayor Steve Schewel unable to speak easily due to losing his voice (negative PCR test), Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson presided throughout the meeting. Council recognized Larry McGill with a National Recovery Month proclamation, and Schewel announced in an emailed statement read aloud that closed-session evaluations resulted in salary increases for City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg ($206,700) and City Clerk Diana Schreiber ($103,175).

agenda_items.title: City Attorney's Office FY22 Budget Amendment (Staff Attorney FTE and Legal Software)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following up on the August 19 charter-officer evaluation follow-up, Council approved a FY2021-22 budget amendment funding one additional attorney position and legal practice-management software for the City Attorney's Office.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3-6 including Transit Plan ILA and Utility Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted Consent Items 1 and 3-6 by a single roll-call vote, including the Transit Plan governance interlocal agreement, water and wastewater master services agreements, North Carolina Investment Pool participation, and a USGS interlocal agreement.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — 1051 Olive Branch Road (Continued from June 21)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Danny Cultra) and the Pulte Home Company LLC development team returned from the June 21 continuance for the 79.478-acre site (284 single-family and townhome units, PDR 3.700/FJB, which PC opposed 1-11 in April 2021). Post-June revisions added an archaeological study, written consents from 13 of 13 identified cemetery descendant family contacts for relocation, 24% distributed tree preservation, 35% open space, and removal of three vehicular stream crossings; resident Timothy Hill spoke in opposition. After Council split 5-2 on annexation and rezoning (DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece opposed), Council unanimously passed the Consistency Statement 7-0 before adjourning at 8:20 PM.

votes.item_title: Adopt FY22 Budget Amendment for City Attorney's Office (One Attorney FTE and Practice Management Software)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not verbally named on the transcript prior to the 00:18:12 roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Added funding for one new attorney FTE and legal practice management software stemming from August 19 charter officer evaluation discussions.

votes.item_title: Item 8 Motion 1: Adopt Annexation Ordinance and Authorize Utility Extension Agreement (1051 Olive Branch Road)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved voluntary annexation and utility extension agreement with Pulte Home Company LLC for 79.478 acres at 1051 Olive Branch Road after post-June environmental and cemetery commitments.

votes.item_title: Item 8 Motion 2: Adopt Zoning Map Change (RR/FJB to PDR 3.700/FJB) and FLUM Amendment (1051 Olive Branch Road)
votes.discussion_detail: Rezoned 1051 Olive Branch Road from Residential Rural to PDR 3.700/FJB for up to 284 residential units with concurrent Future Land Use Map amendment.

votes.item_title: Item 8 Motion 3: Adopt Consistency Statement (NCGS 160D-605) for 1051 Olive Branch Road
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson initially misstated the tally as 5-2 at 01:20:49 before correcting the record at 01:21:29 to confirm a unanimous 7-0 vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the statutory plan-consistency statement under NCGS 160D-605 for the approved 1051 Olive Branch Road rezoning.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Sept. 7, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: 1051 Olive Branch Road Annexation, Suburban Growth in Southeast Durham, and Post-Planning Commission Revisions
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-2 on annexing and rezoning 1051 Olive Branch Road for 284 units after the developer revised environmental and cemetery proffers following a June 21 continuance and an April 1-11 Planning Commission denial recommendation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve annexation and rezoning because post-continuance commitments substantially improved environmental protection, resolved gravesite family outreach, and added needed housing supply.
side_a_arguments: Majority members noted that post-June revisions secured 13 of 13 descendant family consents alongside an archaeological study, raised distributed tree save to 24% and open space to 35%, and eliminated three vehicular stream crossings.
Supporters cited Durham's housing supply shortage and contiguous alignment with the previously approved adjacent 1101 Olive Branch Road project.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the suburban annexation and rezoning due to sprawling Southeast Durham growth, cumulative neighborhood impacts, and repeated developer bypassing of the Planning Commission.
side_b_arguments: Charlie Reece (01:00:16) and DeDreana Freeman (01:04:45) maintained their opposition to continued far-flung suburban annexations in the Olive Branch corridor and criticized the cumulative infrastructure and community-cost burden.
Members across Council also raised frustration that developers wait until City Council hearings—bypassing the Planning Commission—to introduce major design concessions.
disagreements.resolution: Council approved annexation and rezoning 5-2 (Freeman and Reece nay) and subsequently approved the statutory Consistency Statement 7-0.

meetings.title: Regular Durham City Council Work Session Aug. 19, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the August 19, 2021 virtual work session with six council members present, opening with a 6-0 vote to grant Council Member Charlie Reece an excused absence due to a family health matter. Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton condemned a severe night of gun violence and pressed administration for mutual-aid backup agreements after residents reported unanswered 911 calls following the end of Raleigh call rollover. Council voted 6-0 to accept the City Attorney's priority item for a closed session on City Attorney and City Clerk evaluations, heard public comments urging rezoning rather than special accommodations for Northwood Investors, and expressed consensus that appointed boards should remain virtual during the Delta surge. Following a presentation on expanding the Longtime Homeowner Grant Program citywide, members debated whether the program should stay focused on legacy neighborhoods or integrate with the County's 30% AMI grant (and push to raise eligibility to 60% AMI), resolved a Cultural Advisory Board ballot tie for Elias J.J. Torrey, and voted 6-0 to settle the upcoming agenda and enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Council Member Charlie Reece
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel noted Council Member Charlie Reece was out of state attending to a family health matter. Council voted unanimously to excuse Reece's absence.

agenda_items.title: Gun Violence Crisis and 911 Emergency Call Center Rollover Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton called gun violence and the COVID-19 Delta variant Durham's two most urgent crises after shootings the prior night, and demanded immediate exploration of mutual-aid backup agreements with other 911 centers after reports of unanswered 911 calls. City administration explained that Raleigh had asked to end its automatic call rollover arrangement and that out-of-city dispatchers carry operational challenges, though Middleton insisted on pursuing interim options.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Closed Session Request (City Attorney and City Clerk Evaluations)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the Mayor's prompt, the City Attorney requested a closed session at the conclusion of the work session to conduct personnel evaluations for the City Attorney and City Clerk. Council accepted the priority item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Northwood Investors, Pulled Items 3 & 5, and Virtual Board Meetings (Item 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens Matters speaker Brandon Williams (and community comments) urged Council to deny special site-plan accommodations to Northwood Investors and explore rezoning to secure community benefits and open space. Council also reviewed pulled Item 3 (Triangle transit governance interlocal agreement) and Item 5 (NC Investment Pool), and agreed by consensus under Item 2 that appointed boards, committees, and commissions should remain virtual.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Consensus to keep boards virtual

agenda_items.title: Plan to Develop a Citywide Longtime Homeowner Grant Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson presented framework options for expanding Durham's Longtime Homeowner Grant Program citywide while coordinating with the joint City-County $1.25 million tax grant program ($500,000 City / $750,000 County, 30% AMI). Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman, Jillian Johnson, and Mayor Steve Schewel discussed clarifying staff's charge as providing options, proactive outreach to homeowners in tax arrears, timing gaps before FY22 rollout, and lobbying Durham County to expand joint eligibility to 60% AMI.

agenda_items.title: Durham Cultural Advisory Board Appointment Ballot and Agenda Settlement

Torrey and two each for Abraham Gonzalez-Brena and Angelique Stallings; after a member shifted their vote, Torrey reached four votes for appointment. Council then settled the upcoming meeting agenda (consent item 1 and items 3–6, plus public hearing item 8) and recessed into closed session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Work Session Aug. 19, 2021
disagreements.issue: Scope and Timing of Expanding the City's Longtime Homeowner Grant Program
disagreements.summary: During Item 7, Council members diverged in emphasis over whether staff had been directed to produce a citywide rollout plan or merely options, and how to balance immediate neighborhood expansion against lobbying Durham County to expand the joint 30% AMI grant.
disagreements.side_a_position: Clarify that Council asked for framework options rather than a finalized citywide mandate, and prioritize pressing Durham County to expand the joint City-County grant from 30% to 60% AMI while targeting city-invested neighborhoods in the interim.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton noted his recollection of the prior charge was to provide options and a framework rather than a directive to implement citywide immediately.

Mayor Steve Schewel and staff highlighted that $500,000 in City funds and $750,000 in County funds were already budgeted for the joint countywide 30% AMI tax grant, making expansion to 60% AMI with the County alongside broader neighborhood targeting the highest-leverage path.
disagreements.side_b_position: Move faster to deliver city grant relief in the current year rather than waiting until FY22 or relying on the County's separate deferral/grant timelines.
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman voiced concern that the current discussion meant no expanded relief would reach homeowners this year or before the 2022 fiscal year, and underscored that the County's earlier deferral program creates eventual repayment liability unlike the City's grant.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; staff continued cross-departmental work over the next three months to return with refined options alongside joint City-County program implementation.

meetings.title: Regular Durham City Council Meeting Aug 16, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 16, 2021 regular meeting, Durham City Council approved a 7-0 Consent Agenda covering Items 1-15, 17, and 22—including rescinding the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit corridor protection and advancing the Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot—and unanimously approved (7-0 across three votes) Item 18, Epcon Southpoint LLC's 42.83-acre Courtyards at Southpoint 2 annexation and PDR 1.682 rezoning (72 single-family units) after extended resident concerns prompted new mid-hearing proffers protecting American Tobacco Trail tree buffers, adding two trail connections, installing traffic calming, and contributing $40,000 for affordable housing. During the mid-meeting break at 02:15:31, Charlie Reece excused himself due to a family health issue, leaving six voting members for the final two items. Council then voted 5-1 (DeDreana Freeman dissenting) to annex 222 acres along Junction and Ferrell Roads (Item 19, over 1 million sq ft of industrial capacity by Scannell Properties) and adopted its companion Industrial Light translation zoning, before voting 6-0 to authorize a $150,000 economic development incentive for Nuvotronics Inc. tied to $39M-$50M capital investment and 113-150 jobs.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Consent Agenda (Items 1-15, 17, 22 incl. DOLRT Rescission and Guaranteed Income Pilot)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to adopt Consent Agenda Items 1-15, 17, and 22 in a single motion. Key approved items included rescinding Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit corridor policies, establishing the Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot contract, and renewing enterprise Microsoft licensing.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — Courtyards at Southpoint 2 (7852 Herndon Rd & 1404 Fenwick Pkwy)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and applicant Epcon Southpoint LLC (represented by Nil Ghosh and Gerard Masante) presented a 42.83-acre petition for up to 72 detached single-family homes under PDR 1.682 (recommended 7-5 by Planning Commission). Neighbors including Karen Francola, Dr. Eugene Granger, Barbara Taylor, Bansari Patel, and Trisha Smarr raised density, stormwater, traffic, and American Tobacco Trail (ATT) buffer concerns; during the hearing, the applicant added proffers for a second northern ATT tie-in, a Fenwick ATT tie-in prior to the 38th CO, an undisturbed 20-foot ATT buffer outside tie-ins, Phase 2 traffic calming, and a $40,000 affordable housing contribution, winning unanimous 7-0 approval.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 across Annexation, Zoning, and Consistency motions

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Junction & Ferrell Road Industrial (222 Acres, Scannell Properties)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Charlie Reece's departure during the break for a family health matter, staff (Alex Cahill, Rob Joyner) and Scannell Properties representatives (Patrick Byker, joined in support by NCRR's Anna Lee Moore and Chamber's Ryan Regan) presented a 222-acre, 11-parcel annexation for over 1 million sq ft of light-industrial facilities ranked 14/14 in the Industrial Land Study, directly translating county IL/FJB zoning. Residents Bonita Green and Jason Bazdula spoke in opposition; DeDreana Freeman voted against annexation citing premature site infrastructure and unaddressed homeowner tax burdens, while the 5-1 majority approved annexation and adopted direct-translation zoning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-1 (Annexation); Passed on Roll Call (Zoning translation)

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Nuvotronics Inc. ($150,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a $150,000 performance-based economic development incentive agreement with Nuvotronics Inc., tied to $39 million in three-year ($50 million five-year) capital investment and 113 three-year (150 five-year) jobs. Mark-Anthony Middleton briefly paused to ensure the $150,000 figure (misspoken as $150) was accurate before Council unanimously approved the agreement 6-0 and adjourned at 10:19 PM.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted statutory plan consistency statement for Courtyards at Southpoint 2.

votes.notes: Charlie Reece departed during the mid-meeting break (02:15:31). YouTube ASR misrecognized Freeman's vote as 'aye', but her floor speech opposing annexation (03:06:23) and the City Clerk's explicit tally announcement ('the motion passes five to one' at 03:10:30) confirm her Nay vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Meeting Aug 16, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Courtyards at Southpoint 2 Buffer Protections, ATT Connectivity, and Residential Accountability (Item 18)
disagreements.summary: Residents along Herndon Road and Fenwick Parkway objected to density, stormwater runoff, traffic, and loss of trees along the American Tobacco Trail, prompting Council to press Epcon Southpoint LLC into binding mid-hearing proffers before voting unanimously.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve only with binding written proffers guaranteeing American Tobacco Trail connections, undisturbed buffer trees, traffic calming, and affordable housing support.
side_a_arguments: Neighbors Karen Francola, Dr. Eugene Granger, Barbara Taylor, Bansari Patel, and Trisha Smarr raised flooding, buffer clearing, and Herndon/Fenwick traffic concerns.

Council members pushed Epcon Southpoint LLC to add concrete written commitments for two ATT trail tie-ins, an undisturbed 20-ft ATT buffer outside tie-in corridors, Phase 2 traffic calming, and a $40,000 affordable housing contribution.
disagreements.side_b_position: Initial developer submission relied on standard UDO compliance and a single trail tie-in without Phase 2 traffic-calming or undisturbed-buffer commitments.
side_b_arguments: Applicant attorneys initially defended standard site-plan review for stormwater and buffer management before agreeing to expand written commitments during the hearing.
disagreements.resolution: Epcon Southpoint LLC committed to the added proffers on the record (01:56:10), resolving Council concerns and yielding unanimous 7-0 approval.

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Meeting Aug 16, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Junction & Ferrell Road 222-Acre Industrial Annexation Timing and Neighborhood Impacts (Item 19)
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-1 on annexing 222 acres for speculative light-industrial warehousing along Junction and Ferrell Roads, balancing urgent industrial land supply against premature infrastructure and community-equity concerns.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve annexation to unlock a premier industrial site ranked 14/14 in Durham's Industrial Land Study and generate tax base and industrial jobs.
side_a_arguments: Majority members noted the scarcity of ready industrial land in Durham and highlighted regional economic-development support from NCRR and the Durham Chamber of Commerce.
County Industrial Light zoning already existed by right, so city annexation ensured municipal utility service, tax revenue, and direct zoning translation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose premature 222-acre annexation without an identified end-user, committed infrastructure readiness, or protection for long-time nearby homeowners facing tax pressure.
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman (03:06:23) opposed annexing 222 acres without confirmed tenants or full infrastructure and argued that industrial growth without parallel tax-relief tools burdens longtime neighboring residents.
Neighbors Bonita Green and Jason Bazdula raised local traffic, quality-of-life, and impact concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation and UEA passed 5-1 with DeDreana Freeman dissenting (Charlie Reece absent), followed by approval of direct translational zoning.

meetings.title: Budget Healing Event
meetings.executive_summary: On August 6, 2021, the City of Durham hosted Part 2 of its ARPA Budget Healing Series—co-facilitated by Budget Director Bertha Johnson, Leela Pedersen, Deputy City Manager Claudia Hager, Equity & Inclusion Director Sharon Williams, and NCCU professor Dr. Jim C. Harper II, with participation from Council members Javiera Caballero, Jillian Johnson, and Pierce Freelon. Presenters summarized over 300 community survey responses and 80 community funding proposals competing for Durham's $52 million city (and $62 million county) American Rescue Plan Act allocations, highlighting live Mentimeter prioritization polls topped by economic recovery, mental health, affordable housing, teacher pay, livable wages, and racial equity. Equity & Inclusion Director Sharon Williams introduced the Racial Equity Impact Assessment tool for evaluating ARPA proposals, followed by resident Q&A raising visually impaired website accessibility (Michelle Bush), application barriers for grassroots groups (Jesse Huddleston), and transition plans across the 2021 municipal election cycle addressed by Javiera Caballero before her closing remarks.

agenda_items.title: Introductions, Council Recognition, and ARPA Engagement Context
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Facilitator Leela Pedersen and NCCU's Dr. Jim C. Harper II welcomed residents alongside Council members Javiera Caballero, Jillian Johnson, and Pierce Freelon and Budget Director Bertha Johnson. Staff framed Part 2 of the Budget Healing series around community governance over $52 million in City ARPA funds alongside $62 million in County ARPA funds.

agenda_items.title: Review of 300+ Survey Responses, 80 Community Proposals, and Live Prioritization Polls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Leela Pedersen and Bertha Johnson presented themes from over 300 community surveys and 80 submitted ARPA project ideas, followed by interactive Mentimeter ranking exercises with participants. Top resident priorities were Economic Impacts (overall category), Mental Health (public health), Affordable Housing (housing), Teacher Pay (education), Livable Wages (employment), and Racial Equity (evaluation criteria).

agenda_items.title: Racial Equity Impact Assessment Tool Presentation by Equity & Inclusion Director Sharon Williams
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Equity & Inclusion Director Sharon Williams walked through Durham's Racial Equity Impact Assessment (REIA) framework intended to score ARPA proposals against historical racial disparities, community co-creation, and unintended burdens. Staff noted how REIA scoring would feed into Council's upcoming fall ARPA evaluation rubric.

agenda_items.title: Community Questions on Accessibility, Grassroots Barriers, Election Transition, and Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Participants questioned accessibility for visually impaired residents on city ARPA portals (Michelle Bush), criticized repetitive new application burdens rather than relying on prior task-force work (Jesse Huddleston), and asked how upcoming 2021 elections might impact ARPA decisions. Javiera Caballero explained Council continuity and upcoming fall allocation milestones at 01:09:21 before delivering closing remarks at 01:33:27.

meetings.title: Regular Durham City Council Work Session Aug. 5, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson opened the August 5, 2021 work session and Mayor Steve Schewel joined immediately after roll call with all seven council members present. Following tributes to retiring staffer Gene Bradham, Council Members DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece debated whether a proposed Tenants' Bill of Rights resolution should move forward at the next work session ahead of City Attorney review of state-preempted versus locally enforceable ordinances, before agreeing to wait a month for legal analysis. Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items (including adding the Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot and a new economic development incentive), heard a presentation from Digital Durham founder Laura Fogel requesting resolutions and ARPA/city support for the Digital Equity Plan, and reviewed the Office on Youth's shift from the Durham Youth Commission toward paid youth ambassadors ages 16–24 (with Freeman urging continued engagement for middle and high schoolers under 16). Following Cultural Advisory Board nominee Rodrigo Dorfman's withdrawal and submission of a seventh board recommendation, Council voted 7-0 to settle the August 16 agenda with Guaranteed Income Pilot Item 22 on consent.

agenda_items.title: Retirement Tribute to Gene Bradham and Discussion of Proposed Tenants' Bill of Rights Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council honored Gene Bradham on his retirement after more than 30 years of service at City Hall. Council Member DeDreana Freeman then proposed bringing forward a Tenants' Bill of Rights resolution at the next work session prior to ARPA allocations, prompting Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Member Charlie Reece to urge waiting until the City Attorney separates locally enforceable ordinances from state/federal advocacy; Freeman agreed to bring the item back in one month after legal review.

agenda_items.title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page presented priority updates moving Item 5 (United Minority Contractors of North Carolina contract) under Community Development and adding supplemental Items 20 (economic development incentive for public hearing August 16) and 22 (Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot carried over from August 2). Council approved the priority items unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Durham Digital Equity Plan (Digital Durham)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Digital Durham founder Laura Fogel, joined by Neighborhood Improvement Services Director Constance Stancil, presented data showing nearly 40% of Durham households earning $20,000 or less lacked broadband subscriptions despite 99% countywide infrastructure availability. Fogel requested Council resolutions of support and sustainable funding (distinct from or alongside ARPA funds) to expand broadband adoption, devices, and digital literacy.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Office on Youth Update and Restructuring of the Durham Youth Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office on Youth staff (Laura Khalil, Nori McDuffy, Elise Fraser, and youth project assistants) reported on growing a 260-provider youth network and replacing the volunteer-based Durham Youth Commission with a paid 'Change by Youth' Ambassador cohort ages 16–24 seated by October, while planning to update the 2003 establishing resolution. Council Members Pierce Freelon, DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson praised the compensated power-sharing model, though Freeman cautioned against losing engagement for youth ages 13–15.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations, Cultural Advisory Board Withdrawal Update, and Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced council board nominations (Environmental Affairs Board, Durham Workers Rights Commission, and Mayor's Council for Women) and reported that following Rodrigo Dorfman's withdrawal, the Cultural Advisory Board submitted a seventh nominee, which Council decided to take up at the next work session. Council then voted 7-0 to settle the upcoming meeting agenda including Consent Items 1–15, Item 22 (Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot), and public hearings 18–20.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items (Items 5, 20, and 22)
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote with all seven members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted priority items moving Item 5 (United Minority Contractors) and adding supplemental Items 20 (economic development incentive) and 22 (Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot).

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Work Session Aug. 5, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Timing of Tenants' Bill of Rights Resolution Relative to Legal Review
disagreements.summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman sought to introduce a Tenants' Bill of Rights resolution at the next work session prior to finalizing ARPA housing priorities, while Mayor Steve Schewel and Council Member Charlie Reece pushed to wait for City Attorney vetting of local authority versus state preemption.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring forward a general resolution supporting a Tenants' Bill of Rights within two weeks while developing enforceable local ordinances on a parallel legal track.
side_a_arguments: DeDreana Freeman argued community groups had already agreed on core guardrails and that adopting a resolution promptly would align housing priorities ahead of ARPA funding decisions without waiting on ordinance drafting.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay the resolution until the City Attorney advises which provisions Durham can legally enforce versus which require General Assembly or federal advocacy, and weigh staff budget capacity.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Steve Schewel cautioned that a symbolic resolution without attorney vetting would be unclear and unproductive.

Charlie Reece noted the proposal implicated significant city staff time and budget investments not included in the newly adopted budget and required distinguishing local powers from state/federal advocacy.
disagreements.resolution: Freeman agreed to bring the Tenants' Bill of Rights item back in one month after meetings with the City Attorney's Office.

meetings.title: Regular Durham City Council Meeting Aug 2, 2021 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the August 2, 2021 regular City Council meeting with all seven members in person, honoring retiring Finance Director David Boyd and proclaiming National Night Out. After approving the consent agenda 7-0 (excluding Item 3, pulled for public comment), Council approved Item 27 (Parcel K consolidated annexation, 837 units) on a 6-1 split vote—with Mayor Steve Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Pierce Freelon voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting Nay in opposition to annexation—before unanimously approving the accompanying UDO rezoning (7-0) and consistency statement (7-0). Council also approved Item 28 (405 T.W. Alexander annexation and PDR 19.745 rezoning) unanimously across three 7-0 votes. Pulled Item 3 triggered an intense debate over Cultural Advisory Board nominee Rodrigo Dorfman's 2019 email containing alleged coded racist remarks about Black women, dividing Middleton, Freeman, and Freelon against Johnson, Caballero, Schewel, and Reece before Council voted 7-0 to seat the five uncontested nominees and defer Dorfman to Thursday's work session, and closed with majority consensus to return temporarily to virtual meetings due to COVID-19 Delta risks.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation, Finance Director Retirement, Priority Items, and Consent Agenda (Except Item 3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel proclaimed August 3, 2021 as National Night Out and led tributes to retiring Finance Director David Boyd after 12 years of service. City Manager Wanda Page announced Item 31 (Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot) was referred back for final contract negotiations, and Council approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 3 by a 7-0 electronic vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated Annexation Parcel K (Jenks Investment LLC / U.S. Land Corp)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request for voluntary annexation, utility extension, FLUM amendment, and PDR 5.949 zoning for an 837-unit project near Leesville Road/US-70 featuring 20-year deed-restricted affordable housing, 100-year stormwater detention, and DPS/affordable housing contributions. Following lengthy neighborhood opposition over traffic and growth versus Planning Director Sara Young confirming the site lay inside the fill-in area west of Kemp Road, Council approved annexation 6-1 (DeDreana Freeman voting Nay) and then approved the UDO rezoning and consistency statement 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Annexation Passed 6-1 (Freeman Nay); UDO & Consistency Passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Consolidated Annexation 405 T.W. Alexander Drive (Eden Land Corp)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson presiding, staff presented a contiguous annexation, utility extension agreement with Eden Land Corp, and rezoning from OI(D) to PDR 19.745 with F/J-B watershed overlay (recommended favorably by the Planning Commission on May 11 without resident displacement). Council approved the annexation, UDO rezoning, and consistency statement unanimously across three votes.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 3: Durham Cultural Advisory Board Appointments (Rodrigo Dorfman Debate)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by former Council Member Jacqueline Wagstaff and community speaker Adele Ortiz, Item 3 sparked sharp debate over nominee Rodrigo Dorfman's 2019 email criticizing Black women's comprehension and speech. Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman, and Pierce Freelon opposed seating Dorfman without reparative accountability, while Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, Mayor Steve Schewel, and Charlie Reece raised concerns over double standards and turning past political conflicts into public trials before voting 7-0 to confirm the five uncontested appointees and hold Dorfman for Thursday's work session.

agenda_items.title: Council Meeting Format Discussion (Return to Virtual Meetings Amid Delta Variant)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel initiated a post-agenda discussion on whether to suspend in-person hybrid council meetings due to rising COVID-19 Delta transmission and close seating in chambers. Although Middleton expressed concern about the optics, Mayor Schewel noted a majority favored returning temporarily to virtual meetings and asking the City Manager to strengthen staff COVID precautions.

votes.item_title: Item 27 (Motion 3): Adopt Consistency Statement for Parcel K Rezoning
votes.notes: Electronic clicker vote passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 28 (Motion 1): Adopt Ordinance Annexing 405 T.W. Alexander Effective Sept. 30, 2021 and Authorize Utility Extension Agreement with Eden Land Corp
votes.notes: Electronic clicker vote passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved contiguous annexation and utility extension agreement for 405 T.W. Alexander Drive with Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson presiding.

votes.item_title: Item 28 (Motion 2): Adopt Ordinance Rezoning 405 T.W. Alexander from OI(D) F/J-B to PDR 19.745 F/J-B

votes.item_title: Pulled Item 3: Approve Five Durham Cultural Advisory Board Appointments and Defer Rodrigo Dorfman Nomination to Work Session
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman offered the original substitute motion to hold Dorfman's nomination; after nearly an hour of debate over whether to re-advertise or review at work session, Council passed the amended motion 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Meeting Aug 2, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Parcel K Voluntary Annexation and Growth Management in Southeast Durham (Item 27)
disagreements.summary: Council split 6-1 on annexing Parcel K for an 837-unit residential development, weighing urgent housing supply and rare mandatory affordable housing commitments against resident objections to annexation, traffic on Leesville Road, and outward suburban expansion.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve annexation and development to expand housing supply, secure 20-year deed-restricted affordable units and 100-year stormwater protections, and avoid pushing growth into neighboring counties.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Steve Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson argued Durham faces a severe housing shortage, cannot curb traffic by halting housing (needing transit investments instead), and cannot divert city infrastructure bonds from historically marginalized neighborhoods to state-maintained Leesville Road.

Charlie Reece noted it was the first private project in five years offering dedicated affordable housing and strong stormwater protections, while Javiera Caballero and Planning Director Sara Young noted the site sits inside the fill-in area west of Kemp Road.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject the voluntary annexation of outer Southeast Durham land over neighborhood opposition.
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman praised the project's commitments if annexed, but voted No on the annexation itself because residents had organized to protect their home area from city expansion.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation passed 6-1 (Freeman Nay); Council then voted 7-0 to adopt the PDR 5.949 zoning and consistency statement.

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Meeting Aug 2, 2021 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Appointment of Rodrigo Dorfman to the Durham Cultural Advisory Board (Pulled Item 3)
disagreements.summary: Council divided sharply over whether to seat Cultural Advisory Board nominee Rodrigo Dorfman despite community outcry over a 2019 email criticizing two Black women's comprehension and speech.
disagreements.side_a_position: Withhold or reject Dorfman's appointment until he performs reparative work and accountability for racist/coded remarks toward Black women.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton argued Dorfman's 2019 email invoked hurtful racist tropes about Black women's intellect ('you could tell by the way they spoke') and remained a distraction absent genuine reconciliation.

DeDreana Freeman proposed holding or re-advertising the seat because unrepentant harm disrespects community leadership, and Pierce Freelon suggested Human Relations Commission mediation while taking Black women's testimony seriously.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support Dorfman's appointment based on CAB's recommendation and avoid magnifying a 2019 political/interpersonal dispute or applying selective standards.
side_b_arguments: Jillian Johnson argued the 2019 email stemmed from a polarizing election conflict involving specific individuals rather than all Black women, noted Dorfman resigned from People's Alliance/Nuestra Gente, and warned against turning private disputes into public trials.

Javiera Caballero cited an uneven double standard where critics attacking her citizenship or making xenophobic/anti-Semitic remarks faced no consequences, while Mayor Steve Schewel and Charlie Reece supported Dorfman on the merits while agreeing to pause until Thursday to review the email.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 to confirm the five uncontested CAB nominees and defer Dorfman's nomination to the August 5 work session; Dorfman subsequently withdrew his application prior to August 5.

meetings.title: Regular Durham City Council Work Session July 22, 2021 at 1 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Returning to City Hall chambers in person for the first time since the COVID-19 shutdown, Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the July 22, 2021 work session with six council members present after voting 5-0 (before DeDreana Freeman's arrival) to excuse Charlie Reece's absence. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (6-0) and voted 6-0 to suspend the rules for immediate action on Item 22, a $100,000 contract with Made in Durham; on the main motion, Council passed Item 22 by a 5-1 split vote—with Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Pierce Freelon voting Aye and DeDreana Freeman voting Nay due to missing demographic outcome data on who is served. Council heard citizen proposals from Dr. Rochelle Newton on community IT support, reviewed pulled consent items (cemetery audit, Triangle regional model, water facility contract, and stormwater catch-basin pilot), and received major updates on Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 winners and the Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot (partnering with Step Up Durham via a $500,000 Mayors for a Guaranteed Income grant plus $110,000 in city administrative funds) before settling the August 2 agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Charlie Reece and Approval of City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Welcoming members back to City Hall chambers, Mayor Steve Schewel called for a vote to excuse Council Member Charlie Reece's absence (passed 5-0 prior to DeDreana Freeman's arrival at 00:10:29). City Manager Wanda Page presented priority updates requesting a rules suspension on Item 22 (Made in Durham), updated attachments on Parcel K (Item 27) and Dr. Rochelle Newton (Item 29), and supplemental Items 30 (booking agent contract) and 31 (Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot), which Council approved 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Action Item (Rules Suspended): Contract with Made in Durham ($100,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed a $100,000 fiscal-year contract with Made in Durham, with Pierce Freelon and Mark-Anthony Middleton asking about its funding history since 2015 and alternative youth funding pathways, while Mayor Steve Schewel requested a list of other private funders. DeDreana Freeman stated she could not support the contract without clear data showing who Made in Durham serves; after voting 6-0 to suspend the rules, Council passed the contract 5-1 with Freeman opposed.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Suspend Rules Passed 6-0; Approval Passed 5-1 (Freeman Nay)

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Dr. Rochelle Newton Proposal for Community IT Support
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Rochelle Newton presented a detailed proposal to establish community-based IT support for residents and organizations lacking technical resources. Council thanked Dr. Newton for submitting the proposal attached to the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items Review (Cemetery Audit, Triangle Regional Model, Water Reclamation Contract, and Catch-Basin Pilot)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed pulled items including the June 2021 Cemetery Operations Performance Audit (Item 11), the NC State University Triangle Regional Model agreement (Item 16), the Crowder Construction contract for North Durham Water Reclamation Facility (Item 17), and the SP 2021-01 catch-basin insert stormwater pilot (Item 23).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (held for Aug. 2 consent)

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Participatory Budgeting (PB) Cycle 2 Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Management Services staff presented winning projects from Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2, highlighting strong youth and DPS turnout during remote schooling. Council Members DeDreana Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton praised staff and budget delegates while urging tracking of grantee financial standing, prior county/public funding, and outcome metrics.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Durham Guaranteed Income Pilot (Step Up Durham) and Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayoral Assistant Amber Wade presented Durham's Guaranteed Income Pilot funded by a $500,000 Mayors for a Guaranteed Income (Jack Dorsey) grant plus up to $110,000 in city administrative funds committed by City Manager Wanda Page, selecting Step Up Durham to administer participant payments launching late 2021 through December 2022. Council Members Pierce Freelon, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Mayor Steve Schewel celebrated the milestone and pledged fundraising support, then voted 6-0 to settle the August 2 agenda.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Council Member Charlie Reece
votes.notes: DeDreana Freeman had not yet arrived; Charlie Reece absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Charlie Reece's absence at the start of the work session.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items (Items 22, 27, 29, 30, and 31)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved priority items adding supplemental Items 30 and 31, attachment updates, and rules-suspension request for Item 22.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules for Immediate Vote on Item 22 (Made in Durham Contract)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules so Council could vote immediately to meet the fiscal-year payment deadline utilizing 2021 funds.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Approve $100,000 Contract with Made in Durham
votes.notes: Voice vote; DeDreana Freeman stated opposition on the record and vote passed 5-1 (Charlie Reece absent).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved budgeted $100,000 contract with Made in Durham. DeDreana Freeman stated prior to the vote that she could not support the contract without clarity on who Made in Durham serves.

disagreements.meeting_title: Regular Durham City Council Work Session July 22, 2021 at 1 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Demographic Accountability and Immediate Approval of the $100,000 Made in Durham Contract (Item 22)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-1 to approve the $100,000 Made in Durham contract under suspended rules, with DeDreana Freeman dissenting over missing participant demographic reporting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the budgeted $100,000 Made in Durham contract immediately to meet the fiscal-year funding deadline while requesting follow-up information on private funders and program history.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton, Pierce Freelon, and Mayor Steve Schewel praised Made in Durham's youth workforce mission as an upstream public-safety and economic investment already budgeted by Council.
Administration noted suspending the rules was necessary because the funds came from the closing fiscal year.
disagreements.side_b_position: Withhold approval until the contract explicitly includes reporting on who is served by Made in Durham.
side_b_arguments: DeDreana Freeman reiterated prior concerns over who Made in Durham serves and stated she could not support the contract without seeing language requiring that data to come back to Council.
disagreements.resolution: Contract passed 5-1; City Manager Wanda Page committed to providing written historical and funding background on Made in Durham.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council June 21, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly five-hour session concluding the 2020-21 fiscal year, Durham City Council unanimously adopted the FY2021-22 Budget and FY2022-27 CIP (7-0), alongside pulled Consent loans for Commerce Street Apartments and Elizabeth Street Apartments (7-0) and a GoTriangle transit improvements ILA prioritizing Braggtown bus stops (7-0). Council also unanimously adopted Comprehensive Plan Community Goals and Objectives (7-0), excused annexation for Bertha Gamble's 1518 Hamlin Road residence under a utility extension agreement (7-0), annexed and directly zoned two industrial projects on Lumley Road and Project Suite/1 Litho Way (7-0), and passed resolutions backing the American Jobs Plan and supporting the DPS Board against NC HB 324 (7-0). After extensive debate over the East Durham Open Space Plan, mass grading, distributed tree cover, and cemetery relocation at 1051 Olive Branch Road (Item 43), Council continued the public hearing to September 7, 2021. Council split 6-1 (Javiera Caballero dissenting) on a $10 million TEFRA bond resolution for private Duke School (Item 45), approved a $256,000 incentive for CARsgen Therapeutics (with Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson voting aye under protest), and closed by directing staff to extend current Longtime Homeowner Grant applications through August 31 while returning in early August with a scoping plan for a gap-year citywide vs. targeted neighborhood tax-relief program.

agenda_items.title: Tribute to Alethea Bell, Proclamations, Council Announcements, and Consent Item 7 Referral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened with a tribute to former HR Director Alethea Bell, followed by proclamations for Cleft and Craniofacial Awareness Month (student Kai Hale), Olympic Day (Marcus Manning & Hill Carrow), and Mayor's Monarch Pledge Day (Ashley Robbins). Council members celebrated the 35th anniversary of Durham's 1986 anti-discrimination proclamation and Juneteenth, discussed remote meeting rules and Morreene Road DHA plumbing issues, accepted priority items, and voted 7-0 to refer a third Workforce Development Board appointment back to committee before passing the unpulled Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: FY2021-22 Budget and FY2022-27 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fayetteville Street Planning Group member Larry Hester urged 24-hour walking/bicycle patrols and corridor investment, while Donald Hughes urged doubling the Durham YouthWorks summer jobs budget and tracking public-engagement budget changes. Council adopted the FY2021-22 budget and FY2022-27 CIP 7-0; afterward, Denise Hester was heard under Zoom audio troubleshooting urging Fayetteville Street master-plan infrastructure funding, joined in remarks by DeDreana Freeman.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: Commerce Street Apartments, Elizabeth Street Apartments, and Transit ILA
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman questioned income-tier allocations and funding sources on three pulled Consent items. DHA CEO Anthony Scott confirmed the shift from competitive 9% to non-competitive 4% LIHTC tax credits on Commerce Street kept 30%/60% AMI targets intact while bundling mixed-income and senior units (Item 12); Reginald Johnson confirmed Affordable Housing Bond backing for Elizabeth Street (Item 17); and Transportation Director Sean Egan committed to prioritizing Braggtown Route 9 stops with GoTriangle (Item 20).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 each across three Roll Call votes

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Community Goals and Objectives Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Scott Whiteman presented the updated Comprehensive Plan Community Goals and Objectives incorporating Audubon Society biodiversity language from the June 15 joint hearing. After DeDreana Freeman requested clearer staff feedback loops for neighborhood groups such as the InterNeighborhood Council, Council adopted the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation / Utility Extension Alternative — Bertha Gamble Residence (1518 Hamlin Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Alexander Cahill explained that 1518 Hamlin Road is a 16.5-acre single-family home site whose septic is county-permitted but whose wells failed after construction began during COVID permitting delays, returning a revenue-negative fiscal impact. Representative Glenn White and homeowner Bertha Gamble explained their water hardship and agreed to Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson's request for a voluntary Affordable Housing Fund donation; Council adopted staff's alternative motion 7-0 excusing annexation under Code Sec. 70-129(9) while authorizing a landowner-funded water extension.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Lumley Road Industrial (5605 & 5513 Lumley Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and H&S Venture Group (Wyatt Bone, Justin Parker) presented a 7.5-acre contiguous annexation and direct Industrial Light translation for a 75,000 sq ft industrial facility. After Charlie Reece and DeDreana Freeman questioned tenant displacement from two existing houses on site and Justin Parker confirmed the prior tenant had already moved out, Council approved annexation/UEA and UDO zoning translation 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 across two Roll Call votes

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning — 1051 Olive Branch Road (Continued to Sept. 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Danny Cultra and the Pulte Home Company LLC / Horvath Associates team (attorneys Matthews and Jamie Schwedler, engineer Tim Sivers, and Jamie Davis) presented a 79.478-acre annexation and PDR 3.700 rezoning for 284 units, which the Planning Commission opposed 1-11; former Council member Larissa Seibel spoke in opposition. Extended Council questioning challenged East Durham Open Space Plan compatibility, mass grading, peripheral tree save, highway-aligned road relocation of an on-site cemetery, and housing affordability impacts, prompting Council and applicant Tim Sivers to leave the public hearing open and continue Item 43 to September 7.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — Project Suite (1 Litho Way)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and applicant representative Justin Parker presented a 5.5-acre satellite-infill annexation and Industrial Light zoning translation for a 41,000 sq ft manufacturing addition next to an existing 100,000 sq ft facility. At City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg's request to separate the utility extension agreement onto its own motion, Council approved annexation, the A.L. Meyer LLC UEA, and UDO zoning in three unanimous 7-0 votes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 across three Roll Call votes

agenda_items.title: TEFRA Revenue Bond Resolution ($10M Not-to-Exceed) for Duke School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Finance Director Emily Desiderio, bond counsel Jeff Paulie, and Duke School finance director Russell Rabinowitz sought statutory federal TEFRA approval for up to $10 million in Public Finance Authority bonds carrying no city debt obligation. Mark-Anthony Middleton questioned Duke School's $20,000-$23,000 tuition, 36% students of color, lack of free/reduced lunch or busing, and reliance on city emergency services before voting aye, while Javiera Caballero voted nay as the resolution passed 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with CARsgen Therapeutics Ltd. ($256,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Adria Graham Scott, Chamber's Brian Fox, Dr. Jia, and Donald Hughes spoke on a $256,000 performance-based city incentive paired with $1M County and $1.2M+ state JDIG awards for CARsgen Therapeutics' $97M phase-1 clinical manufacturing facility and 128 jobs allowing associate-degree hires. Charlie Reece and Jillian Johnson criticized the 'but-for' legal premise of corporate incentives for a $2B+ company while agreeing to vote yes under protest, Mark-Anthony Middleton defended positive fiscal math, and Council approved the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Resolutions Supporting the American Jobs Plan and Opposing NC House Bill 324
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from a late-evening break, Council rapidly adopted two supplemental legislative resolutions by 7-0 roll-call votes: Item 49 endorsing the federal American Jobs Plan, and Item 50 supporting the Durham Public Schools Board of Education in opposing NC House Bill 324.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 each across two Roll Call votes

agenda_items.title: Longtime Homeowner Grant Program Deadline Extension and Gap-Year Scope Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Reece proposed extending current Longtime Homeowner Grant applications and directing staff to design a temporary citywide program until the joint City-County tax-office program scales up. City Manager Wanda Page and Reginald Johnson noted the current cycle covers 2015-2019 revaluations (extended administratively to August 31 due to staff retirements/leave) and lacked capacity to build a new program immediately; following debate with Mark-Anthony Middleton favoring targeted neighborhood equity and DeDreana Freeman advocating Braggtown, Merrick-Moore, and Walltown, Council gave consensus thumbs-up at 04:53:00 for staff to bring back a scoping/resource timetable at an early August work session before adjourning at 11:59 PM.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus thumbs-up (6 thumbs) directing early August scoping report

votes.item_title: Refer Third Workforce Development Board Vacancy (Mr. Atkinson) Back to Workforce Development Executive Committee
votes.notes: Roll-call audio in captions stopped after Freelon's aye prior to Clerk confirmation at 00:44:17; no dissent occurred and Council confirmed the referral prior to the Consent vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred one of three Item 7 Workforce Development Board vacancies back to committee as requested by the City Clerk and Office of Economic & Workforce Development.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted unpulled Consent Agenda items, including Item 7 appointments of Kevin Griffin and Leslie Elaine Madison.

votes.item_title: Item 9: Adopt Fiscal Year 2021-22 Budget and Fiscal Year 2022-27 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the annual operating budget and five-year CIP following public comment from Larry Hester and Donald Hughes; Denise Hester spoke afterward due to Zoom audio troubleshooting.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved revised development loan commitment accommodating DHA's shift to 4% LIHTC financing combining Commerce Street mixed-income (84 units) and senior (88 units) phases.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved affordable housing development loan backed by the dedicated Affordable Housing Bond after staff confirmed interim Finance cash mechanics.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved interlocal transit agreement after Transportation Director Sean Egan committed to prioritizing Braggtown Route 9 bus stop upgrades.
