meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Dec 21, 2020 (full meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: Convening virtually on December 21, 2020 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council opened with reflections on the pandemic and federal COVID-19 relief legislation before unanimously passing the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding Item 1, which Mayor Steve Schewel pulled). The Consent Agenda approved GoTriangle commuter rail technical service reimbursements, water facility and paving contracts, police and automated refuse vehicles, a Blue Benevolence grant, a DOJ Sexual Assault Kit Initiative (SAKI) grant, and a Duke University fiber-optic network agreement for Durham Housing Authority campuses. Following a closed-captioner break and public hearing on Item 22, Council unanimously voted 7-0 across four roll-call motions to annex 4115 Angier Avenue, enter a utility extension agreement, amend the Future Land Use Map to Low-Medium Density Residential, adopt a consistency statement, and amend the UDO. At the close of the meeting, Council agreed by unanimous consent to refer pulled Item 1 (a mayoral appointment to the RDU Airport Authority) back to Mayor Schewel.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, W.H. Auden Reading, Moment of Silence, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel read an excerpt from W.H. Auden's 'September 1, 1939' before leading a moment of silence, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Council announcements addressed COVID-19 vaccine equity (declining to jump the line ahead of service and frontline workers), the pending federal COVID-19 relief package including transit, rental aid, and Save Our Stages funds, and local restaurants offering outdoor/to-go cocktail service under the governor's order.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reported attachment and motion updates for Item 5 (water facility expansion design services with Stantec Architecture), Item 6 (Williams Water Treatment Plant paving award), and four consolidated annexations: Item 19 (Carrington Woods 2), Item 20 (924 Old Oxford Road), Item 21 (551 Olive Branch Road), and Item 22 (4115 Angier Avenue). The City Attorney had no priority items, and the City Clerk confirmed the social media livestream was operating.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Item 1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel pulled Item 1 (Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority mayoral reappointment) and read the remaining consent items covering Safety and Wellness Task Force appointments, the Workers' Bill of Rights discussion, GoTriangle commuter rail technical services reimbursement, water management design and paving contracts, refuse and police patrol vehicles, pest and elevator contracts, employment and training grants, the 2020 Blue Benevolence and DOJ SAKI grants, and a Duke University fiber-optic network agreement for DHA campuses. Council approved the Consent Agenda unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation, FLUM Amendment, and Rezoning for 4115 Angier Avenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a brief pause to give closed captioners a break, Council resumed the public hearing for 4115 Angier Avenue and heard from four speakers (Nate Bueller, Bob Mishler, Patrick Byker, and Jamal Levonne). Council Member Charlie Reece noted the applicant's engagement with Planning Commission concerns and contrasted the site favorably against the environmental concerns at Olive Branch, while DeDreana Freeman noted traffic and pedestrian safety concerns. Council approved annexation/utility extension, Future Land Use Map amendment to Low-Medium Density Residential, consistency statement, and UDO amendment across four unanimous 7-0 roll-call votes.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 1 — Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Mayoral Appointment Referral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel consulted the City Attorney on procedural handling of pulled Item 1, a mayoral appointment to the RDU Airport Authority requiring council concurrence. On the City Attorney's parliamentary guidance, Council agreed by unanimous consent (thumbs up without a formal roll-call vote) to refer Item 1 back to the Mayor.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Work Session Dec 10, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 10, 2020 virtual work session with all seven members present, the Durham City Council opened with COVID-19 holiday stay-at-home guidance from Javiera Caballero, gun violence condolences and concern over shootings at the 900 East Main Street apartments from DeDreana Freeman, and consensus to bring forward a CROWN Act anti-hair-discrimination resolution. Council voted unanimously 7-0 to accept the City Manager's priority item, then voted 7-0 to suspend the rules and 7-0 to approve an interlocal agreement receiving $250,000 in additional Durham County CARES Act funds for the Durham CARES Small Business Grant Program before the December 31 deadline. Members also heard public comment opposing Walltown displacement around the Northgate Mall sale, reviewed the Durham County Transit Plan update (including commuter rail vs. bus tradeoffs and cost-sharing), and questioned City Manager Wanda Page on one-time emergency funding options for violence interruption ahead of a January 7 staff report before settling the regular agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Council Announcements (COVID-19 Order, Gun Violence, CROWN Act)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven council members answered roll call. Javiera Caballero urged virtual holiday celebrations under the governor's 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. stay-at-home order amid surging COVID-19 rates, another member mourned a recent shooting homicide and promoted the Durham Arts Council auction, and DeDreana Freeman highlighted five to six recent shootings near 900 East Main Street while gaining council consensus to draft a local CROWN Act resolution banning natural hair discrimination.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item 24 — Durham County Interlocal Agreement for CARES Small Business Grant Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented Supplemental Item 24, an interlocal agreement to accept $250,000 in Durham County CARES Act funding for the Durham CARES Small Business Grant Program prior to the December 31 federal spending deadline. Council voted 7-0 to accept the priority item, 7-0 to suspend the rules for same-day action, and 7-0 to authorize execution of the interlocal agreement.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Pulled Items and Public Comment on Northgate Mall / Walltown
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Items 3 (Workers' Bill of Rights), 6 (Williams Water Treatment Plant paving), 7 (Synagro Central biosolids contract), and 16 (Duke University/Durham Housing Authority fiber-optic agreement), while praising Item 15 (DOJ SAKI grant). A Walltown community organizer addressed the sale of Northgate Mall to Northwood Investors and its potential tax and rent displacement impacts on Black working-class families.

agenda_items.title: Presentation — Durham County Transit Plan Update and Regional Commuter Rail Cost-Sharing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning and transit staff updated Council on socially distanced community engagement, integration with the Comprehensive Plan, and prioritization under the Durham County Transit Plan. Council members reflected on balancing regional commuter rail commitments with local bus service needs, referencing the $160 million spent on the prior light-rail effort and noting that county commissioners would negotiate commuter rail cost-sharing with Raleigh.

agenda_items.title: Violence Interruption Funding Options and Settling the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting City Manager Wanda Page confirmed staff would return January 7 with funding and geographic options for expanding violence interruption, and explained to Mark-Anthony Middleton that one-time fund balance and pro-rated 1/12 monthly county ILA payments could support mid-year action outside the regular budget cycle. Council then voted 7-0 to settle the regular Consent Agenda (Items 1-16, including Item 3 with an updated motion) and General Business public hearings (Items 19-22).

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Item (Supplemental Item 24)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not explicitly named in audio transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the City Manager's presentation of Supplemental Item 24 (CARES Small Business Grant ILA with Durham County), Council moved, seconded, and approved accepting the priority item 7-0 by roll call.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Supplemental Item 24 at Work Session
votes.discussion_detail: Because CARES Act funds had to be obligated before December 31, Pierce Freelon moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded suspending the rules to vote immediately on Item 24. Passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 24 — Authorize City Manager to Execute City-County Interlocal Agreement for Durham CARES Small Business Grant Program
votes.discussion_detail: Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and Pierce Freelon seconded authorizing the City Manager to execute the interlocal agreement accepting $250,000 from Durham County for small business CARES grants. Passed unanimously 7-0, with Mayor Schewel thanking Mr. Pettigrew's department for administering the grants in-house.

votes.item_title: Settle Upcoming Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-16; GBA Public Hearings Items 19-22)
votes.discussion_detail: Pierce Freelon moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded settling the Consent Agenda (Items 1-16, keeping Item 3 on consent with a revised motion) and General Business public hearings (Items 19-22). Passed unanimously 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Mtg. with Durham Delegation Dec 9, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: In a virtual joint legislative consultation on December 9, 2020, members of the Durham City Council and legislative staff (including Carmisha Wallace) presented the city's 30-item 2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda and 10-item advocacy agenda to members of the Durham General Assembly delegation, including Senator Mike Woodard, Senator Natalie Murdock, Representative Vernetta Alston, and Representative Marcia Morey. Discussions covered statewide housing and tax proposals such as expanding the circuit breaker property tax exemption, inclusionary zoning and impact fees, and using county land near old Lowe's Grove School, alongside enterprise-fund utility rate flexibility, driver's licenses for undocumented residents, repealing the controlled-substance excise tax, Ban the Box expansion, Extreme Risk Protection Orders, and ending non-DWI license suspensions. Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton and delegation members also examined two proposed local charter amendments—adding election flexibility for filling council vacancies and expanding grant-making flexibility for COVID-style relief—before Senator Woodard outlined next steps ahead of legislative bill filing. Because this was a consultative intergovernmental briefing, no formal council votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Welcome and Framing of the 2021 Legislative Committee Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members, city staff, and Durham state legislators gathered virtually in place of the traditional legislative breakfast. Mayor Steve Schewel turned table-setting over to Legislative Committee Chair Charlie Reece, Vice Chair Mark-Anthony Middleton, and staff coordinator Carmisha Wallace to walk through the 2021 legislative items.

agenda_items.title: Circuit Breaker Tax Exemption, Inclusionary Zoning, and Utility Enterprise Funds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Delegation members and city leaders distinguished state bills requiring broader municipal coalitions (such as removing age/disability limits on the circuit breaker property tax exemption and inclusionary zoning/impact fees) from local bills. Senator Mike Woodard noted prior Senate opposition to affordable housing land-use bills (such as a county parcel near old Lowe's Grove School) and flagged Local Government Commission scrutiny over utility enterprise fund rate changes.

agenda_items.title: Undocumented Driver's Licenses, Ban the Box, Gun Violence Prevention, and License Suspensions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Participants reviewed items carried over from 2019 and justice-reform priorities, including issuing driver's licenses to undocumented immigrants, repealing the controlled-substance excise tax, expanding Fair Chance Hiring (Ban the Box) to state contractors and private employers, supporting gun violence prevention and Extreme Risk Protection Orders (ERPOs), and eliminating permanent driver's license suspensions for non-DWI offenses.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Charter Amendments on Council Vacancy Filling and Grant-Making Flexibility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Mark-Anthony Middleton explained two proposed local charter amendments requested after the 2020 council vacancy process and CARES Act grant distribution: allowing the option of an election alongside appointment when filling a vacant seat, and granting Raleigh-style local grant flexibility subject to state constitutional public-purpose constraints. Legislators asked clarifying questions about the breadth of flexibility under the vacancy proposal.

agenda_items.title: Advocacy Agenda Review and Pre-Session Delegation Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Wallace noted the finalized package comprised 30 legislative items plus 10 advocacy items (including Environmental Affairs Board energy-efficiency priorities). Senator Mike Woodard commended the early December outreach ahead of January bill filing and stated legislators would review items with council staff before Mayor Steve Schewel adjourned the meeting at 4:39 p.m.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Dec 7, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on December 7, 2020 with all seven members present, the Durham City Council established a new two-hour closed-captioner break custom and unanimously approved the Consent Agenda 7-0, covering the FY21-22 budget schedule, Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws, police impound storage leasing, NCCU police jurisdiction, street/sidewalk contracts, and a WIOA workforce contract amendment. On Item 8 (2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda), Council debated whether to include two local charter amendments—on council vacancy election flexibility and grant-making authority—with Charlie Reece voicing caution about drawing state legislative scrutiny to Durham's charter while Mark-Anthony Middleton and colleagues argued for presenting them to the Durham delegation for vetting; Council ultimately passed the full agenda 7-0 after removing staff drafting notes. On Item 25, following a public hearing on the CARES Act First Substantial Amendment to the FY2020-21 Annual Action Plan and 2020-25 Consolidated Plan covering $5,449,225 in HUD CDBG-CV, ESG-CV, and HOPWA-CV funds, Council passed five unanimous 7-0 roll-call motions before adjourning at 8:57 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Closed-Captioner Break Policy, Condolences, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the meeting with a moment of silence for residents affected by COVID-19 and gun violence, instituted a five-minute break every two hours for closed captioners, and extended condolences to DeDreana Freeman and Beverly Thompson on family losses. Council announcements congratulated newly sworn-in Durham County Commissioners and discussed gun violence and policing ahead of upcoming work session updates.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted added attachments for Item 8 (2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda) and Item 24 (UDO Omnibus Changes 15, TC2000002). The City Clerk reported that the Durham Affordable Housing Implementation Committee appointment had been referred back to her office and the 'We Are the Ones' COVID-19 response was discussed at the prior work session.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Budget Schedule, Task Force Bylaws, Street/Water Contracts, Police Impound, WIOA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the Consent Agenda including Durham Housing Authority and Planning Commission appointments, the FY21-22 Budget Development Schedule, revised Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws, the Stagecoach Road lift station condemnation, a police impound storage lease, NCCU Police extended jurisdiction, paving and sidewalk repair contracts, Lakewood Avenue/NC 54 utility work, and a PY2020 WIOA contract amendment. Council approved the Consent Agenda unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: 2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda (Including Proposed Local Charter Amendments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carmisha Wallace and Senior Assistant City Attorney Krista Kukarot presented research on two unresolved legislative proposals requested by Mark-Anthony Middleton: charter amendments for council vacancy election flexibility and Raleigh-style grant-making authority (noting state constitutional public-purpose limits). Charlie Reece expressed concern over inviting General Assembly intervention into Durham's charter, while Middleton, Mayor Schewel, and Javiera Caballero favored forwarding the proposals for the Durham delegation to vet; after confirming removal of extraneous staff notes flagged by DeDreana Freeman, Council approved the agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — CARES Act First Substantial Amendment (FY2020-21 Annual Action Plan & 2020-25 Consolidated Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Wilma Conyers presented the first substantial amendment allocating $1,875,324 of Durham's $5,449,225 HUD CARES Act award ($2,716,217 CDBG-CV, $2,662,668 ESG-CV, and $70,340 HOPWA-CV) to reimburse local dedicated housing funds spent on summer COVID-19 contracts, with $3,573,901 slated for a spring 2021 second amendment. With no public speakers, Council unanimously approved all five motions 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 8 — Adopt 2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda (Including Proposed Charter Amendments)
votes.discussion_detail: Following debate over two proposed local charter amendments and confirmation that extraneous staff notes on page 3 were removed per DeDreana Freeman's request, Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and Charlie Reece seconded adopting the 2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda. All seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 1) — Approve Draft First Amendment to FY2020-21 Annual Action Plan & 2020-25 Consolidated Plan for HUD
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded approving the draft First Amendment to the FY2020-21 Annual Action Plan and 2020-25 Consolidated Plan for submission to HUD. Passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 2) — Authorize City Manager to Execute Administrative and Contractual Documents for Amended Action Plan
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Jillian Johnson seconded authorizing the City Manager to execute administrative requirements and contractual documents for CARES Act activities under the amended action plan. Passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 3) — Adopt CDBG-CV Grant Project Ordinance ($2,716,217)
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the HUD Community Development Block Grant Coronavirus (CDBG-CV) project ordinance in the amount of $2,716,217. Passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 4) — Adopt ESG-CV Grant Project Ordinance ($2,662,668)
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the HUD Emergency Solutions Grant Coronavirus (ESG-CV) project ordinance in the amount of $2,662,668. Passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 25 (Motion 5) — Adopt HOPWA-CV Grant Project Ordinance ($70,340)
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the HUD Housing Opportunities for Persons With AIDS Coronavirus (HOPWA-CV) project ordinance in the amount of $70,340. Passed 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Dec 7, 2020 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Including Local Charter Amendments in the 2021 Long Session Legislative Agenda
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to formally include two proposed local charter amendments—council vacancy filling flexibility and Raleigh-style grant-making flexibility—in the 2021 Legislative Agenda presented to the General Assembly.
disagreements.side_a_position: Questioned taking charter amendments to the current state legislature due to risk of inviting General Assembly interference with Durham's charter and doubts over whether the grant amendment overcomes constitutional hurdles.
side_a_arguments: Opening Durham's charter before the current composition of the North Carolina General Assembly could invite unwanted modifications.
The grant charter language may still be constrained by the state constitution's exclusive emoluments and public-purpose clauses.
disagreements.side_b_position: Include both charter amendments in the agenda so the Durham delegation can vet their viability during the December 9 consultation.
side_b_arguments: Constituents and civic groups asked for expanded democratic options on council vacancies and municipal agility to distribute COVID-style relief grants.
Durham's charter is already a creature of the state and the city routinely takes principled positions without self-censoring.
Placing the items on the agenda allows candid feedback from the Durham delegation before any bill is filed.
disagreements.resolution: Accepting that the December 9 delegation meeting would vet what was legislatively movable, Charlie Reece joined Mark-Anthony Middleton in moving/seconding the full agenda, which passed unanimously 7-0.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Nov 19, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on November 19, 2020 with five members present (DeDreana Freeman previously excused and Charlie Reece absent due to illness), the Durham City Council voted 5-0 to grant an excused absence to Charlie Reece and 5-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items. Council agreed by unanimous thumbs-up consensus to schedule the Workers' Rights Commission's Workers' Bill of Rights on the December 10 work session agenda, and heard a Citizen's Matter from William Powell regarding street hazards from ATVs and dirt bikes. Staff then delivered two major presentations: Water Management reported on non-payment disconnection suspensions, virtual hold improvements, ESL outreach, and roughly $70,000-$75,000 remaining in utility assistance funds with fewer than 20 accounts disconnected, while Police Chief C.J. Davis presented the 2020 Third Quarter Crime Report covering gun violence task forces, pandemic-depressed clearance rates, and sexual assault kit processing. Council concluded by voting 5-0 to settle the upcoming regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence for Charlie Reece, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With DeDreana Freeman on a previously approved excused absence, Council voted 5-0 to grant an excused absence to Charlie Reece, who was under the weather. In announcements, Javiera Caballero urged Thanksgiving COVID-19 testing and gathering limits, and Jillian Johnson secured unanimous thumbs-up consensus to place the Workers' Rights Commission's Workers' Bill of Rights on the December 10 work session agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented added attachments for Item 8 (2021 Legislative Agenda), Item 20 (water disconnections), Item 21 (Q3 crime report), Item 26 (William Powell Citizen's Matter), and Supplemental Item 27 (Eckerd Alternatives PY2020 WIOA contract amendment). Council approved the manager's priority items 5-0, and the City Clerk introduced new staff member Paula Roland.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Consent Review and Citizens' Matters — William Powell on ATVs and Dirt Bikes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Item 5 (FY21-22 budget development schedule) and Item 6 ('We Are the Ones' COVID-19 response) while Mayor Schewel noted public infrastructure contracts sustain employment during the recession. Resident William Powell (Item 26) raised concerns about dirt bikes and ATVs on city streets, noting police pursuit constraints and discussing temporary dedicated riding spaces as a stopgap measure.

agenda_items.title: Presentation — Water Disconnections for Non-Payment Suspension and Resumption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff briefed Council on customer billing call-center virtual hold options, leak/high-bill challenges for residents working or schooling from home, and utility assistance utilization—noting roughly $155,000 spent through October and $70,000-$75,000 remaining from the second allocation ahead of a mid-year funding check-in. Members commended staff's multilingual outreach and noted fewer than 20 accounts were currently without water service.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Nov 16, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: With six members present and DeDreana Freeman excused absent (approved 6-0 for both November 16 and 19), the Durham City Council recognized Internal Audit Week, heard Jillian Johnson read a statement backed by Unite Here Local 23 affirming the 2020 presidential election results, and heard Pierce Freelon and Mark-Anthony Middleton call for immediate emergency funding to expand violence interruption programs. Following a contested public hearing on Item 20 (Doc Nichols Road consolidated annexation and townhome rezoning), Council split 4-2 across three roll-call votes to approve the annexation/utility extension, consistency statement, and UDO amendment, with Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, and Mark-Anthony Middleton voting Aye and Pierce Freelon and Charlie Reece voting Nay over Montague Street traffic and off-site road-improvement costs. Council then concluded the evening by unanimously approving 6-0 the consistency statement and UDO zoning map change for 851 Slater Road (Item 21) before adjourning at 11:34 p.m.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel honored civic leader John Clarence 'Skippy' Scarborough and City employee Laverne McDonald before a moment of silence and roll call. With six members present, Council voted 6-0 to grant DeDreana Freeman an excused absence for both the November 16 meeting and the November 19 work session.

agenda_items.title: Internal Audit Week Proclamation, Election Results Statement, and Gun Violence Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson presented the Internal Audit Week proclamation to Dr. Germaine Brewington, citing resilience after the city's malware attack, and read a Unite Here Local 23-supported statement affirming the 2020 presidential election results. Pierce Freelon and Mark-Anthony Middleton praised Mayor Schewel and Chief Davis's gun violence press conference, with Middleton urging Council to move within days or weeks to fund and expand violence interruption on an emergency basis.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted updates to Item 10 (Balfour Beatty Public Works Operations Center CMAR/GMP contract), Item 18 (1432 Ellis Road annexation), Item 19 (Cortez Drive Residential rezoning), Item 20 (Doc Nichols Road annexation), and Item 21 (851 Slater Road rezoning). The City Attorney and City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Consolidated Annexation and Rezoning for Doc Nichols Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated the Doc Nichols Road townhome annexation after Fennel Farms and Montague Street neighbors objected to cut-through traffic on street stubs and pedestrian safety for seniors. Jillian Johnson, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Steve Schewel supported approving the attainable townhome project along planned street stubs, whereas Charlie Reece and Pierce Freelon urged voting no to send the developer back to fund off-site NCDOT or one-way traffic solutions. All three motions passed 4-2.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Zoning Map Change for 851 Slater Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the 851 Slater Road rezoning request, noting its consistency with the Industrial designation on the Future Land Use Map, and applicant Neil Ghosh gave brief remarks. With no further public speakers, Council unanimously approved the consistency statement and UDO zoning ordinance 6-0 before adjourning at 11:34 p.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Nov 16, 2020 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Doc Nichols Road Townhome Annexation: Montague Street Stub Traffic vs. Housing Supply and Predictable Rules
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-2 over whether to approve a townhome annexation and rezoning connecting to Montague Street in Fennel Farms or reject it to compel the developer to fund off-site NCDOT/traffic mitigations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Doc Nichols Road townhome annexation and rezoning because street stubs are intended to connect, the project supplies relatively attainable townhomes, and by-right development would lack proffers.
side_a_arguments: Existing street stubs in newly built subdivisions like Fennel Farms are explicitly designed to be extended into adjacent developments.
The townhomes offer more attainable pricing than surrounding single-family homes and generate modest additional trips compared to by-right development.
Refusing projects under existing rules risks capricious decision-making driven by neighborhood opposition while traffic calming can still be explored.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote no to send the developer back to the drawing board to finance an alternative NCDOT connection or pursue a one-way traffic hardship solution for Montague Street.
side_b_arguments: Neighbors on Montague Street raised serious pedestrian and senior safety concerns from cut-through traffic.
The developer had not priced or engineered an alternative NCDOT road connection or one-way street arrangement, which only a no vote would force them to pursue.
disagreements.resolution: All three motions (annexation and utility extension, consistency statement, and UDO amendment) passed 4-2, with DeDreana Freeman excused absent.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Nov 5, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 5, 2020 virtual work session with all seven council members present, the Durham City Council opened with Charlie Reece advising mail-in and provisional voters on checking ballot status at dcovotes.com before November 12, then voted unanimously 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items (setting the FY2020 CAFR as a presentation and postponing Item 5, 'We Are the Ones,' by two weeks). Council reviewed departmental items—pulling deputy finance officer appointments, the virtual city auction, and Street Smart LLC software, and asking for floodplain vehicle relocation plans at the Public Works Operations Center—before hearing two key staff briefings. The Equity and Inclusion Department reported on department-level data disaggregation, a 25-member frontline racial equity team, and survey confusion between diversity and equity as council members pushed for structural funding shifts, while Transportation staff reviewed 4,000K LED streetlight conversions, shielding/removal procedures, and the 40% city cost share to replace fixtures. Council closed by voting 7-0 to settle the regular meeting agenda and adjourned at 3:48 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Election Ballot Cure Announcements, and City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven council members answered roll call. Charlie Reece urged absentee voters to verify and cure mail-in ballots via dcovotes.com by November 12 and explained provisional ballot verification; another member explained requesting postponement of Item 5 ('We Are the Ones'). Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items placing the FY2020 CAFR as a presentation and referring Item 5 to the next work session.

agenda_items.title: Departmental Items Review and Pulled Items 8, 9, and 14
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed departmental items including the October 2020 employee evaluation audit, NC Justice Center Welcome Home grant, Participatory Budgeting bylaws, Farrington/Fayetteville Road apartments loan, Wheels Fun Park land acquisition, remote learning center grants, and Balfour Beatty's Public Works Operations Center CMAR amendment (with Mayor Schewel requesting an email on floodplain vehicle relocation plans). Council discussed pulled Item 8 (signature controls for deputy finance/tax collector appointments) and pulled Item 9 (potential revenue impacts of a virtual city vehicle/equipment auction).

agenda_items.title: Presentation — Equity and Inclusion Department Racial Equity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Equity and Inclusion staff reported on expanding racial equity teams (including 25 self-nominated employees and frontline workers), tracking departmental data disaggregation capabilities, and addressing Racial Equity Viewpoint Survey findings showing confusion among diversity, inclusion, and equity. Council members pressed staff and Acting City Manager Wanda Page on moving beyond symbolic steps toward structural resource reallocation, reparations/UBI/grant possibilities, and state/federal advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Presentation — LED Street Lighting Conversion Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff (Mr. Judge) presented on the Duke Energy LED streetlight conversion, detailing limited data on lower-Kelvin alternatives compared to 4,000K fixtures, alignment verification and shield installations for glare complaints, majority-block polling for streetlight removals, and the city's 40% cost share if fixtures were swapped out. Javiera Caballero and Mayor Schewel agreed that spending millions on a mass swap was infeasible under current budget constraints while urging careful standards going forward.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Upcoming Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager recommended placing Items 1-4 and 6-14 on the Consent Agenda and General Business public hearings Items 18-21 (1432 Ellis Road, Cortez Drive, Doc Nichols Road, and 851 Slater Road). Council approved the settled agenda unanimously 7-0 and adjourned at 3:48 p.m.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Item 1 CAFR Presentation & Item 5 Referral)
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded approving the City Manager's priority items setting Item 1 (CAFR) as a presentation and referring Item 5 ('We Are the Ones' COVID-19 response) to the next work session. All seven members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Settle Upcoming Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-4, 6-14; GBA Public Hearings Items 18-21)
votes.discussion_detail: Javiera Caballero moved and Charlie Reece seconded approving the City Manager's settled agenda placing Items 1-4 and 6-14 on Consent and Items 18-21 on the General Business public hearing agenda. The clerk recorded the motion passing 7-0.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Nov 2, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on November 2, 2020, all seven Durham City Council members opened with a proclamation honoring the late Honorable Mary Ann E. Black (with remarks from her son Jonathan Black), election-eve transit updates recognizing GoDurham for distributing roughly 100,000 masks, and council comments calling for measurable short-term and long-term outcomes on violence interruption initiatives. City Manager Wanda Page presented priority updates covering the Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan, Multifamily Production and Preservation RFP awards, a Coronavirus Relief Fund plan amendment, and the ordering of Chesterfield Avenue street closing after 1700 Hillandale Road. Council unanimously approved 7-0 a multifamily housing revenue bond authorization not to exceed $12 million and, following a public hearing featuring Durham CAN and resident concerns over Durham Housing Authority (DHA) transparency and maintenance standards, unanimously passed 7-0 up to $15.4 million in multifamily housing revenue bonds for J.J. Henderson Towers.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Honoring the Life and Legacy of the Honorable Mary Ann E. Black
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel read a proclamation honoring former Durham County Commissioner, Duke University Health Systems leader, and N.C. House District 29 Representative Mary Ann E. Black for her public service in health care, aging, and education. Her son, Jonathan Black, thanked the Council and reflected on his mother's devotion to helping people across Durham.

agenda_items.title: Election Day Transit Access, GoDurham Pandemic Service, and Gun Violence Interventions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council shared Election Day transportation resources including GoDurham routes and DurhamRides.com, while praising GoDurham bus operators as pandemic MVPs who maintained essential-worker service and distributed approximately 100,000 face masks. Members also addressed recent gun violence and ongoing work-session deliberations on violence interruption, stressing the need for clear timelines and measurable policy metrics during the emergency.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Updates and Consent Agenda Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page reported updated attachments for Item 7 (2020 Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan), Item 19 (2020-2021 Multifamily Production and Preservation RFP recommendations), and Item 27 (Durham City Coronavirus Relief Fund plan amendment), and requested Item 21 (Z180013 Chesterfield Avenue Street Closing) be heard after Item 22 (Z180032 1700 Hillandale Road). Mayor Schewel then introduced the Consent Agenda.

agenda_items.title: Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds Authorization (Not to Exceed $12 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered an authorization for multifamily housing revenue bonds in an aggregate amount not to exceed $12 million. DeDreana Freeman moved and Pierce Freelon seconded approval of the financing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Bond Authorization — J.J. Henderson Towers Multifamily Housing Facility ($15.4 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a staff report by Mr. Johnson, Council held a public hearing in which speakers A.J. Williams/Willy and Heather Ladd (Durham CAN) criticized Durham Housing Authority (DHA) property management staffing, unresolved mold/maintenance issues, and unposted public hearings, urging Council to tie future affordable housing bond funding to transparency and quality-of-life benchmarks. DHA staff acknowledged failing to post the September hearing online as an oversight, and Council members debated minimum housing code enforcement and incremental use of the $95 million housing bond toward DHA's $544 million capital needs before voting unanimously to authorize up to $15.4 million in bonds.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Virtual Special Meeting (Live Stream) Nov 2, 2020 6 p.m.
meetings.executive_summary: Convening a virtual special meeting at 6:00 p.m. on November 2, 2020, Mayor Steve Schewel and five council colleagues waited ten minutes while attempting to reach absent Council Member DeDreana Freeman by phone and text before calling the roll at 6:10 p.m. With Police Chief Cerelyn Davis, City Manager Wanda Page, and City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg in attendance for an administration-requested personnel discussion, Charlie Reece moved and Jillian Johnson seconded a motion to adjourn into closed session. The six present council members voted unanimously 6-0 on roll call to enter closed session and locked the virtual meeting.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call and Attendance Verification for Special Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the 6:00 p.m. special meeting, resolved a brief connection drop for City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg, and held until 6:10 p.m. while attempting to reach Council Member DeDreana Freeman by phone and text. Roll call confirmed six council members present with DeDreana Freeman absent, alongside Police Chief Cerelyn Davis and City Manager Wanda Page.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session on a Personnel Matter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg confirmed the administration called the closed session to discuss personnel matters with Council, Chief Davis, and City Manager Page. Charlie Reece moved and Jillian Johnson seconded adjourning to closed session, which passed 6-0 before the clerk locked the virtual room.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session to Discuss a Personnel-Related Matter
votes.notes: Transcript ASR rendered DeDreana Freeman as 'Council Member Friedan' and did not record a response from her during either roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: At the City Attorney's guidance, Charlie Reece moved and Jillian Johnson seconded going into closed session to discuss a personnel matter called by the administration with Police Chief Cerelyn Davis present. All six present council members voted Aye while DeDreana Freeman remained absent.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session Oct 22, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 22, 2020 work session, all seven Durham City Council members recognized retiring Assistant City Clerk Laverne Brooks and unanimously approved 7-0 priority items from the City Manager, City Attorney (closed session on Darryl Howard v. City of Durham), and City Clerk (supplemental Workforce Development Board appointments, after DeDreana Freeman requested clearer vetting transparency). Council received presentations on Bull City United and violence interruption—where Pierce Freelon pledged to push in upcoming budget talks to shift millions from the $70 million policing budget into community-led violence prevention—and on the first post-bond Multifamily Production and Preservation RFP targeting households below 50–60% AMI. Council suspended the rules 7-0 and voted unanimously 7-0 to support the Upper Neuse River Basin Association's Interim Alternative Implementation Approach for Falls Lake compliance, settled the November 2 agenda 7-0, and entered closed session on the Darryl Howard litigation.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Tribute to Assistant Clerk Laverne Brooks, and Community Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven council members answered roll call for the 1:00 p.m. work session. Mayor Schewel honored Assistant City Clerk Laverne Brooks on her final work session prior to retirement, and council members discussed community correspondence connected to North Carolina Central University.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim City Manager Wanda Page presented updates to Item 15 (DPS property exchange for Snow Hill Road Park and Lucas Middle School), Item 16 (UNRBA IAIA), Item 18 (Bull City United), Item 22 (1700 Hillandale Road), and Item 27 (Coronavirus Relief Fund plan amendment), approved 7-0. Council also approved 7-0 the City Attorney's closed session request for Darryl Howard v. City of Durham (1:17-cv-477) and approved 7-0 the City Clerk's Workforce Development Board priority item after DeDreana Freeman questioned ballot timing and applicant vetting transparency.

agenda_items.title: Review of Administrative Consent Items and Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read through administrative consent items including participatory budgeting support for the LGBTQ Center of Durham, water and utility contracts, the DPS Snow Hill Road Park/Lucas Middle School exchange, and public hearings on annexations and UDO amendments. Mayor Schewel pulled Item 7 (Eno-Haw Hazard Mitigation Plan) and a council member pulled Item 23 (UDO text amendment TC1900004).

agenda_items.title: Bull City United and Violence Interruption Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the Bull City United presentation, Pierce Freelon contrasted Durham's $70 million policing budget with $500,000 for violence interruption and recounted Police Chief Cerelyn Davis's openness to offloading non-policing responsibilities to capable community groups. Freelon pledged to advocate during upcoming budget deliberations for multi-million-dollar institutional investments in violence interruption and youth programming alongside Interim City Manager Wanda Page.

agenda_items.title: 2020-2021 Multifamily Production and Preservation RFP Funding Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson, Assistant Director Karen Lado, and Project Manager Matt Walker presented results of the first multifamily RFP issued since passage of the affordable housing bond, targeting households below 60% AMI with preference for units under 50% AMI. Staff noted individual project contracts will return to Council for approval over the coming months.

agenda_items.title: Support for Upper Neuse River Basin Association (UNRBA) Interim Alternative Implementation Approach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Stormwater and GIS staff presented the UNRBA Interim Alternative Implementation Approach (IAIA) for Falls Lake Stage 1 existing development compliance, noting Durham's five-year expenditure share of roughly $337,000 covers planning and long-term maintenance as well as construction. Council suspended the rules 7-0 and unanimously approved the support resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Human Relations Commission Nominations, Settling Agenda, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council nominated Emily Lofton to the Human Relations Commission and deferred a split ballot between Terrick Willis (3 votes), C. Duane Hinnett (2), and Kevin McIver (1) to collect remaining ballots before the regular meeting. Council then unanimously settled the regular meeting agenda 7-0 and voted by roll call to enter closed session on Darryl Howard v. City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: All seven seated members present; Mayor Schewel declared the motion passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded acceptance of the City Manager's priority updates to Items 15, 16, 18, 22, and supplemental Item 27. Roll call passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney's Priority Item (Closed Session — Darryl Howard v. City of Durham)
votes.discussion_detail: Pierce Freelon moved and Javiera Caballero seconded adding the City Attorney's closed session item for attorney-client consultation on Darryl Howard v. City of Durham et al. (1:17-cv-477, M.D.N.C.). All seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Approve City Clerk's Priority Item (Workforce Development Board Supplemental Item)
votes.discussion_detail: After DeDreana Freeman raised questions about vetting transparency and noon ballot cutoffs for the Workforce Development Board, Jillian Johnson moved and Javiera Caballero seconded approving the Clerk's priority item so Council could deliberate on it later on the agenda. All seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Item 16 — Suspend the Rules to Vote on UNRBA Interim Alternative Implementation Approach
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not verbally identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded suspending the rules to act on Item 16 during the work session. All seven members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Item 16 — Approve Support for UNRBA Interim Alternative Implementation Approach (IAIA)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not verbally identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Following suspension of the rules, Council voted unanimously 7-0 to approve support for the Upper Neuse River Basin Association's five-year IAIA compliance strategy for Falls Lake.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session for Attorney-Client Consultation (Darryl Howard v. City of Durham, 1:17-cv-477)
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero's name was called at 03:06:11 without an audible response captured in the transcript before Pierce Freelon was called; no opposition was recorded.
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded going into closed session for attorney-client consultation regarding Darryl Howard v. City of Durham (1:17-cv-477). Six members are explicitly recorded voting Aye before entering closed session.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 19, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: During its October 19, 2020 regular meeting, all seven Durham City Council members celebrated the virtual Run with the Mayor event, issued proclamations for Indigenous Peoples' Day and Arts and Humanities Month, and heard an announcement from Pierce Freelon on canvassing McDougald Terrace and launching a grassroots fund to address root causes of violence. The evening centered on two contested public hearings (Items 20 and 21) for resident-petitioned curb, gutter, paving, water, and sewer improvements (including a portion of Linden Terrace). On Item 20, a motion to accept the petition's certificate of sufficiency failed 3-4 with Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman, and Charlie Reece voting Aye and Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, and Pierce Freelon voting Nay; immediately afterward on Item 21 (Linden Terrace), an identical motion also failed 3-4 with DeDreana Freeman, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Charlie Reece voting Aye and Steve Schewel, Jillian Johnson, Javiera Caballero, and Pierce Freelon voting Nay. Council closed with an equity debate over balancing full cost-recovery rules against historical infrastructure disparities for annexed neighborhoods lacking city water and fire hydrants.

agenda_items.title: Run with the Mayor Recognition, Indigenous Peoples' Day Proclamation, and Arts and Humanities Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel recognized more than 120 city employees who logged nearly 360 miles in the virtual Run with the Mayor. DeDreana Freeman read a proclamation declaring October 12, 2020 as Indigenous Peoples' Day in Durham, and Mark-Anthony Middleton read the National Arts and Humanities Month proclamation.

agenda_items.title: Early Voting Turnout and Grassroots Anti-Violence Initiative in McDougald Terrace
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council highlighted strong early voting turnout led by Durham's Parkwood precinct. Pierce Freelon invited colleagues and residents to canvas in McDougald Terrace and announced a grassroots fund for community organizers and youth alternatives, citing Police Chief Davis's comment that Durham's $70 million policing budget is reactionary.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Petitioned Curb, Gutter, Paving, Water, and Sewer Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff (Robert Joiner) contrasted the city's dirt-road paving program with full petition projects covering curb, gutter, paving, and utilities, and committed to bringing full cost-recovery policy options in January. After closing the public hearing, Mayor Schewel argued for full cost recovery rather than open-ended municipal obligations, and a motion by Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman to accept the certificate of sufficiency failed 3-4.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Curb, Gutter, Paving, Water and Sewer Laterals on a Portion of Linden Terrace
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joiner presented Item 21 for petitioned improvements on a portion of Linden Terrace inside city limits, and no public speakers appeared during the hearing. DeDreana Freeman moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded accepting the certificate of sufficiency, which failed 3-4, prompting debate among Middleton, Schewel, and Freeman over historical annexation inequities, racial equity criteria, and residents lacking city water or fire hydrants.

votes.item_title: Item 20 — Accept Certificate of Sufficiency for Petitioned Curb, Gutter, Paving, Water, and Sewer Improvements
votes.notes: Steve Schewel and Jillian Johnson are explicitly recorded voting No, and Mark-Anthony Middleton, DeDreana Freeman (mover/seconder), and Charlie Reece as the three Ayes; Javiera Caballero and Pierce Freelon's roll-call lines fell inside a digest gap between 03:10:47 and 03:11:04 and match the identical 3-4 split recorded four minutes later on Item 21.
votes.discussion_detail: After Robert Joiner confirmed accepting the certificate of sufficiency obligates the city to complete improvements at future cost, Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded acceptance. The motion failed 3-4, halting subsequent preliminary and final improvement resolutions.

votes.item_title: Item 21 — Accept Certificate of Sufficiency for Curb, Gutter, Paving, Water and Sewer Laterals on Linden Terrace
votes.notes: Because accepting the certificate of sufficiency was a condition precedent, no further motions were taken.
votes.discussion_detail: With no public speakers at the hearing, DeDreana Freeman moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded accepting the certificate of sufficiency for Linden Terrace. Roll call failed 3-4, with Freeman, Middleton, and Reece voting Aye and Schewel, Johnson, Caballero, and Freelon voting No.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 19, 2020 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Petitioned Street Paving and Utility Extensions vs. Full Cost-Recovery Policy (Items 20 and 21, including Linden Terrace)
disagreements.summary: Council split 3-4 on whether to accept certificates of sufficiency for two resident-initiated infrastructure petitions for curb, gutter, paving, water, and sewer improvements while awaiting January staff cost-recovery proposals.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the petitions now to advance long-awaited basic street, water, and fire-hydrant infrastructure for residents.
side_a_arguments: Residents whose land was historically annexed into the city have faced longstanding infrastructure inequities.
Applying a uniform 'fairness' rule going forward ignores past history and leaves existing residents without city water or fire hydrants to fight fires.
disagreements.side_b_position: Decline the petitions under the current framework and establish a full cost-recovery, equity-prioritized citywide policy.
side_b_arguments: Accepting the certificate of sufficiency legally obligates the city to build the improvements at whatever future cost applies rather than under full cost recovery.
Capital prioritization should rely on a racial-equity-informed system that no petitioner can jump ahead of, pending January staff options.
disagreements.resolution: Both motions to accept the certificates of sufficiency failed 3-4 (at 03:10:43 and 03:14:50), ending both petitions while Council awaited staff's January cost-recovery policy presentation.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Work Session Oct 8, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 8, 2020 virtual work session, six Durham City Council members voted 6-0 to excuse Charlie Reece's absence due to illness and unanimously approved 6-0 the City Manager's priority items, including a FY2020-2021 CIP ordinance title update and an economic development closed session (Item 28). During consent review, members noted a $2.8 million bond refunding savings, pulled several items for further clarity, and debated the equity and tenant-displacement impacts of resident-petitioned dirt-road paving and utility assessments ahead of upcoming public hearings. Council also reviewed board and commission nominations—resolving a Workers Rights Commission ballot tie in favor of Bria Williams and flagging COVID-19 budget cuts to board stipends for DHA residents—before settling the regular meeting agenda 6-0 and breaking for closed session.

agenda_items.title: Attendance Roll Call, Excused Absence for Charlie Reece, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six council members answered roll call and voted 6-0 on a motion by DeDreana Freeman and Jillian Johnson to grant Charlie Reece an excused absence due to illness. Freeman also shared historical remarks on Federal Street Apartments/Fayette Place and praised County Commissioner Brenda Howerton's work with Black Agenda 909 on the countywide Race Equity Commission.

agenda_items.title: Manager Priority Items, Extern Introduction, and Consent Agenda Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to approve Interim City Manager Wanda Page's priority items updating Item 7 (FY2020-2021 CIP ordinance) and adding Item 28 (economic development closed session). During consent review, members praised $2.8 million in 15-year debt refunding savings on Item 10 (with Freeman requesting public web access to bond lists) and pulled Items 8, 9, and 19 plus requested a presentation on Item 15 (Odyssey Drive culvert).

agenda_items.title: Campus Runoff Concerns and Dirt Road / Petitioned Improvement Equity Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker raised street-runoff incidents affecting their campus over the past three years. Later, DeDreana Freeman warned that passing paving and utility assessment costs onto dirt-road property owners threatens renters with higher rents and displacement; Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson and Robert Joiner recommended deciding the pending petitions before holding a broader policy session on full cost recovery.

agenda_items.title: Nominations to Affordable Housing Implementation Committee, BPAC, Planning, and Workers Rights
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council agreed by consensus to grant an exceptional-circumstances policy override for Vickie Lewis to serve on the Affordable Housing Implementation Committee, while Jillian Johnson and Javiera Caballero discussed how COVID-19 cuts to board stipends hinder participation by DHA residents. Council also reviewed nominations for BPAC, Discover Durham, and Planning Commission, and Freeman cast her vote for Bria Williams to break a technical ballot gap on the Workers Rights Commission (4-2 over Stephen Carnegie).

agenda_items.title: Settle Regular Meeting Agenda and Recess for Economic Development Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pierce Freelon moved and Jillian Johnson seconded settling the next regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1-15 and GBA Public Hearings 16-21, passing 6-0. Council then recessed at 3:01 p.m. for a five-minute break before locking the meeting for Closed Session Item 28.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence to Council Member Charlie Reece
votes.notes: Charlie Reece absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Schewel noted Charlie Reece was under the weather and unable to attend. DeDreana Freeman moved and Jillian Johnson seconded granting an excused absence; all six present members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Item 7 Title Update and Item 28 Closed Session)
votes.notes: Charlie Reece absent.
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded approving the City Manager's priority updates for the FY2020-2021 CIP ordinance title and supplemental economic development closed session Item 28. All six present members voted Aye.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting Oct 5, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In the live-streamed October 5, 2020 Durham City Council meeting, all seven members recognized Hispanic Heritage Month, Mammography Awareness Day, and the 75th anniversary of Jack and Jill of America's Durham chapter, while sharing 2020 Census outreach reminders, COVID-19 warnings, and praise for the Item 18 property conveyance at 505 West Chapel Hill Street for mixed-income housing. City Manager Wanda Page noted priority attachment updates on participatory budgeting, communications consulting, GoDurham planning, and water-plant service contracts. After closing a continued public hearing for the Sykes property annexation and rezoning (M/I Homes), Council passed all three implementing motions unanimously 7-0. Council also voted 7-0 to adopt a Race Equity Task Force follow-up resolution urging federal enactment of reparations, universal basic income, guaranteed living-wage jobs, and an inflation-indexed $15-per-hour or higher federal minimum wage.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations, 2020 Census Reminder, COVID-19 Remarks, and 505 W. Chapel Hill St.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council read proclamations for Hispanic Heritage Month (including recognition of Planning Director Sara Moreno Young), Mammography Awareness Day with Alpha Kappa Alpha, and Jack and Jill of America's 75th Durham chapter anniversary, scheduling the full Arts and Humanities Month proclamation for October 19. Members also urged residents to complete the 2020 Census, cautioned that COVID-19 remained serious nationwide, and celebrated the Item 18 conveyance of 505 West Chapel Hill Street for mixed-income housing.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page presented priority updates adding attachments or revisions for Item 6 (FY21 participatory budgeting), Item 7 (Moss and Ross LLC communications consulting), Item 9 (WSP USA Inc. GoDurham planning and operations), and Item 12 (Hach Company nutrient analyzer service agreement).

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing — Sykes Property Annexation, Consistency Statement, and UDO Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed existing water/sewer capacity and immediate revenue positivity for the Sykes property application presented by Nil Ghosh (Morningstar Law Group), Bob Zumwalt (McAdams), and Erica Latham (M/I Homes). Council closed the public hearing and approved three separate 7-0 motions for the annexation/utility agreement, consistency statement, and UDO zoning ordinance, with DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece expressing satisfaction with the scaled-down conservation-district commitments.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Federal Action to Increase Racial Equity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson explained her revision raising the resolution's federal minimum wage demand to $15/hour or higher with regular inflation/cost-of-living adjustments per DeDreana Freeman's prior request. After Johnson read the full text into the record at Mark-Anthony Middleton's request, Council approved the resolution 7-0.

votes.item_title: Sykes Property — Adopt Annexation Ordinance and Enter Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and Javiera Caballero seconded adopting the annexation ordinance and utility extension agreement for the Sykes property. All seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Sykes Property — Adopt Statutory Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and Pierce Freelon seconded adopting the consistency statement for the Sykes property rezoning. All seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Sykes Property — Adopt Ordinance Amending the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO)
votes.discussion_detail: Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and Jillian Johnson seconded adopting the UDO amendment for the Sykes property. Roll call passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution in Support of Federal Action to Increase Racial Equity
votes.notes: Requested transmission to Reps. G.K. Butterfield and David Price and Sens. Thom Tillis and Richard Burr.
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Charlie Reece seconded adopting the federal racial equity advocacy resolution. Following a full reading by Jillian Johnson, all seven members voted Aye.

meetings.title: Special Virtual City Council Meeting - October 1, 2020 (with captions)
meetings.executive_summary: At a special virtual meeting on October 1, 2020, Durham City Council met with staff (Ms. Youngblood) to establish the recruitment process for Durham's next City Manager. Members discussed updating the job description—with DeDreana Freeman recommending sections modeled on Chapel Hill, Greensboro (public-private partnerships), and Raleigh—and debated whether to conduct a formal RFP for an executive search firm. Although Mayor Steve Schewel initially worried an RFP plus the holidays would delay the search until February 2021, colleagues including Pierce Freelon and Mark-Anthony Middleton favored an open RFP given full confidence in Interim City Manager Wanda Page, leading Schewel to agree to the RFP approach. Council also reached consensus on forming a small council subcommittee to help screen search firms and expedite the schedule, with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Job Description Updates and Search Firm RFP Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman suggested strengthening the City Manager job description using Chapel Hill's organizational overview, Greensboro's public-private partnerships requirement, and Raleigh's summary language. Council debated whether to issue an RFP for a search firm; despite Mayor Schewel's concern over delaying the launch until February 2021, Freelon, Middleton, and colleagues backed an RFP due to confidence in Interim Manager Wanda Page, and Schewel concurred.

agenda_items.title: Creation of a Council City Manager Search Subcommittee and Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel proposed forming a council subcommittee to work with Ms. Youngblood on tightening the schedule and narrowing RFP responses to the top two or three search firms for full council selection. After members stressed transparency and avoiding any appearance of exclusion, a majority/consensus emerged for the subcommittee, with a colleague noting he would step aside from serving so interested peers could join before the meeting adjourned at 11:00 a.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special Virtual City Council Meeting - October 1, 2020 (with captions)
disagreements.issue: Formal RFP Process vs. Expedited Search Firm Selection for City Manager Recruitment
disagreements.summary: Council members differed on whether to issue a competitive RFP to hire an executive search firm for the City Manager search given holiday delays into early 2021.
disagreements.side_a_position: Skip or shorten the RFP process to avoid delaying the search until February 2021.
side_a_arguments: Combining a formal RFP with the holiday season would push the start of the active candidate search to February 2021.
Budget and retreat timelines make starting expeditiously desirable.
disagreements.side_b_position: Conduct a full RFP process despite the extra 1–2 months to maximize search firm options.
side_b_arguments: An open RFP surfaces strong firms and ideas that strict upfront narrowing might miss, similar to the 505 West Chapel Hill Street RFP.
Strong confidence in Interim City Manager Wanda Page mitigates the risk of a 60-day schedule difference.
disagreements.resolution: At 00:30:00–00:30:33, Mayor Schewel yielded to his colleagues' arguments and agreed to move forward with an RFP while asking staff to tighten timelines where feasible.
