meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council August 3, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the Durham City Council virtual meeting on August 3, 2020 with all six seated members present, City Manager Tom Bonfield announced his retirement effective September 30, 2020 after 12 years of service, prompting warm tributes from Mayor Steve Schewel and council members. Council reviewed a broad consent slate including the Racial Equity Task Force Final Report, Recovery and Renewal Task Force funding, an employee holiday, transit and water infrastructure contracts, and police grants, with DeDreana Freeman requesting staff follow-up on MWBE/WBE percentage shifts in Items 32 and 33. Following a public hearing, Council voted unanimously 6-0 on a motion by DeDreana Freeman, seconded by Jillian Johnson, to permanently close 89.91 linear feet of Q Place right-of-way to enable two flag lots. Finally, despite public opposition from resident Ms. Plass regarding public engagement and statutory development agreements, Council voted unanimously 6-0 on a motion by DeDreana Freeman, seconded by Jillian Johnson, to approve an expedited hearing request for zoning map change Z1900036 (Farrington Road Multifamily) so the developer could meet an October deadline for 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to build 82 affordable units.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and City Manager Tom Bonfield's Retirement Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the 7:00 p.m. virtual meeting to order, Charlie Reece led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all six seated members answered roll call. City Manager Tom Bonfield reported attachment updates on Items 16, 27, and 45, congratulated Fire, Police, and partners on Safe Kids North Carolina's 'Fit It and Fix It' Program of the Year recognition, and formally announced his retirement effective September 30, 2020 after 12 years as Durham City Manager.

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent Items Including Equity Reports, Audits, Infrastructure, and Grants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel read the consent agenda covering board appointments, PCI compliance and timekeeping audits, an employee holiday item, the Racial Equity Task Force Final Report (Item 13), Recovery and Renewal Task Force funding (Item 14), Planning FY21 work program (Item 15), transit and parking contracts, water line and utility billing amendments, and police HIDTA grants. DeDreana Freeman flagged Items 32 and 33 for staff follow-up regarding shifting MWBE/WBE participation percentages without pulling them from consent.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (middle consent vote truncated in digest)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing — Order Permanently Closing 89.91 Linear Feet of Q Place Right-of-Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff, City Manager Bonfield, and City Attorney Kim Rehberg discussed whether Q Place was platted or fee-simple right-of-way and any associated closing fees. Applicant Mr. Blazovich and representative Tom Tiba explained the street closing and lot recombination with neighbor Mr. Henderson would create two flag lots served by common access easements while increasing property tax value; Council closed the hearing and approved the closing order 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Expedited Hearing Request — Zoning Map Change Z1900036 (Farrington Road Multifamily)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Caller Ms. Plass, who pulled the item, opposed expediting Z1900036, arguing it undermined public engagement and invoked statutory development agreements previously barred by Durham's UDO. Applicant representative Dan Jewell explained the proposal provides 82 affordable housing units along a future transit corridor without city subsidy and required an October hearing to apply for 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits; DeDreana Freeman, Charlie Reece, and Jillian Johnson praised the unsubsidized 4% LIHTC model while separating the broader statutory development agreement policy review, approving the expedited hearing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Order Permanently Closing 89.91 Linear Feet of Q Place Right-of-Way
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing with applicant Mr. Blazovich and Tom Tiba, DeDreana Freeman moved and Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson seconded adopting the order permanently closing 89.91 linear feet of Q Place. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve Expedited Hearing Request for Zoning Map Change Z1900036 (Farrington Road Multifamily)
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson seconded approving the expedited hearing request for Z1900036 so the 82-unit 4% LIHTC affordable housing project could meet its tax credit deadline, with council members affirming that the separate UDO text amendment on statutory development agreements would still undergo full scrutiny. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session July 23, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 23, 2020 virtual work session with all six seated members present, the Durham City Council opened with a moment of silence for Durham's 74th COVID-19 fatality, civil rights leaders John Lewis and C.T. Vivian, and 12-year-old gun-violence victim Tom McLean. Council unanimously voted 6-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items requesting rule suspension for immediate action on COVID-19 emergency rental assistance, rapid rehousing, and shelter case management contracts (Items 22-24), and voted 6-0 to approve the City Attorney's closed-session request regarding newly filed federal litigation (Tony Scott Jr. and Tony Scott Sr. v. City of Durham, et al.). Later in the session, members debated how to confront escalating gun violence through the Community Safety & Wellness Task Force, violence interrupters, and ShotSpotter, clashing over Mark-Anthony Middleton's comparison of ShotSpotter scrutiny to Participatory Budgeting (PB) equity metrics—with Javiera Caballero defending PB and requesting a dedicated staff/NCCU briefing while Middleton and DeDreana Freeman urged prioritizing urgent gun-violence interventions. Council concluded by settling the regular agenda 6-0 and voting 6-0 to enter closed session on the federal lawsuit.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Roll Call, and Black Artists Celebration Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the 1:00 p.m. work session with a moment of silence honoring Durham's 74th COVID-19 death, civil rights leaders John Lewis and Rev. C.T. Vivian, and 12-year-old gun-violence victim Tom McLean, and all six members answered roll call. DeDreana Freeman announced that the Black Artists celebration was advancing across five community-selected neighborhoods with youth stipends, while Mayor Schewel held the recent gun-violence discussion until after consent agenda review.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items (COVID Homelessness Contracts & Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested suspending the rules for immediate action on three urgent Community Development COVID-19 homelessness and rental assistance items: Item 22 (Durham County CDBG-CV emergency rental assistance), Item 23 (Housing for New Hope Inc. ESG-CV rapid rehousing), and Item 24 (Project Access of Durham County ESG-CV shelter case management), which Council approved 6-0. The City Attorney then requested a closed session for attorney-client consultation on newly filed federal litigation (Tony Scott Jr. and Tony Scott Sr. v. City of Durham, et al., M.D.N.C. No. 1:20-cv-558), approved 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Consent Items Overview and Planning FY21 Work Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items, pulling Item 25 (Demand Response Services), Item 26 (cloud parking management), Item 27 (Otis Elevator), and Items 40-41 (2019 and 2020 Police HIDTA grants) for discussion. DeDreana Freeman noted low female staffing representation on Item 28 (Scotty's pressure washing) and praised the equity lens on combined utility billing (Item 34), while Mayor Schewel commended JCCPC Chair Charlie Reece on the detailed Planning FY21 work plan.

agenda_items.title: Gun Violence Response, Community Safety Task Force, ShotSpotter, and Participatory Budgeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members debated next steps on gun violence, crisis response, and expanding violence interrupters—noting DPS agreed to appoint five residents to the 10-member Community Safety & Wellness Task Force regardless of County participation. Tensions surfaced as Javiera Caballero objected to linking Participatory Budgeting (PB) equity critiques to gun-violence debates and requested a dedicated staff/NCCU briefing on PB metrics, while Mark-Anthony Middleton and DeDreana Freeman urged urgent funding and experimentation on violence interrupters and ShotSpotter; Mayor Schewel committed to scheduling future work-session items on both topics.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Settling Regular Agenda, and Closed Session on Tony Scott Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson updated her vote to Ashley Ferrell on an appointment, and the clerk noted Recreation Advisory Commission vote totals. Council voted 6-0 to settle Consent Items 1, 3, 4, 6-21, and 25-44 (with Items 22-24 already acted upon) and GBA Public Hearings 45-47, and then voted 6-0 to enter closed session on the federal Tony Scott lawsuit.

votes.discussion_detail: Following the City Manager's request to suspend the rules for same-day votes on Items 22, 23, and 24 (CDBG-CV emergency rental assistance, Housing for New Hope rapid rehousing, and Project Access shelter case management), a motion was made and seconded and passed 6-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney's Priority Item (Closed Session for Tony Scott Jr. & Sr. v. City of Durham)
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson moved and Javiera Caballero seconded approving the City Attorney's priority item to hold a closed session for attorney-client consultation on Tony Scott Jr. and Tony Scott Sr. v. City of Durham, et al. (M.D.N.C. No. 1:20-cv-558). All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.discussion_detail: With Items 22-24 already disposed of via rule suspension, Charlie Reece moved and Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson seconded settling the agenda with Consent Items 1, 3, 4, 6-21, and 25-44 and GBA Public Hearings Items 45-47. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded entering closed session for attorney-client consultation on federal case 1:20-cv-558 (Tony Scott Jr. and Tony Scott Sr. v. City of Durham, et al.). All six members voted Aye on roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session July 23, 2020 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Gun Violence Response Priorities (ShotSpotter and Violence Interrupters) vs. Participatory Budgeting Equity Scrutiny
disagreements.summary: During a wide-ranging work session debate following recent fatal gun violence, council members clashed over prioritizing urgent gun-violence interventions such as ShotSpotter and violence interrupters versus repeated critiques of Participatory Budgeting's equity outcomes.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize immediate action and funding for gun-violence interventions—including violence interrupters and testing ShotSpotter—while subjecting all city initiatives, including Participatory Budgeting, to equal equity scrutiny.
side_a_arguments: Addressing gun violence affecting Durham children is far more urgent than Participatory Budgeting.
Children's lives justify experimenting with tools like ShotSpotter, and Council can discontinue it if evidence proves it ineffective.
Council must schedule concrete funding and operational steps for violence interrupters and gun-violence prevention.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid conflating the gun-violence crisis with Participatory Budgeting criticism, correct incomplete PB demographic data claims, and schedule a dedicated PB staff and NCCU evaluation briefing alongside advancing the Community Safety Task Force and violence interrupters.
side_b_arguments: Claims that Participatory Budgeting failed its equity goals rely on incomplete demographic data because paper ballots and DPS student votes lacked racial data.
PB staff, the steering committee, and North Carolina Central University produced a full evaluation with improvement proposals that merit an accurate agenda briefing.
Crisis response and expanding violence interrupters should move forward in concert with the Community Safety & Wellness Task Force.
disagreements.resolution: Informational discussion; Mayor Steve Schewel agreed to work with the City Manager to schedule future work-session discussions on both gun-violence/violence-interrupter funding and the Participatory Budgeting evaluation.

meetings.title: Special Virtual Durham City Council July 1, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the July 1, 2020 special virtual City Council meeting with all six seated members present at roll call. During opening announcements, Schewel reported that the City Attorney had filed an expedited Superior Court petition seeking the public and Council release of Durham Police Department body-worn camera footage in a case filed on behalf of Tony Scott Jr. Council held a public hearing on Item 44 (South Mineral Springs and Pleasant consolidated annexation and zoning for up to 191 single-family detached units with $22,000 proffered for schools and $28,650 for the Durham Affordable Housing Fund), though the middle portion of the meeting—including the final disposition of Item 44—is omitted in the truncated transcript digest. Later in the session, Council unanimously approved (5-0, with Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson having stepped out) a temporary ordinance expanding outdoor seating for small businesses and restaurants into rights-of-way and private parking areas, and discussed Council Member DeDreana Freeman's proposal to fund a youth-focused Black Lives Matter public arts project using Participatory Budgeting funds or a $25,000 Bloomberg grant.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements: Body-Worn Camera Release Petition (Tony Scott Jr. Case)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel announced that after consulting with the City Manager and City Attorney regarding a legal action filed on behalf of Tony Scott Jr. against the Durham Police Department, the City Attorney had initiated a Superior Court petition seeking expedited release of relevant body-worn camera footage to both Council and the public. Schewel added that he offered to contact Chief Judge Hudson as recommended by the City Attorney once courts resumed from COVID-19 mode.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Zoning: South Mineral Springs and Pleasant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a consolidated annexation petition (effective September 30, 2020) and rezoning for up to 191 single-family detached homes, noting proffers of $22,000 for schools and $28,650 to the Durham Affordable Housing Fund and a Budget and Management Services finding of immediate positive revenue impact; the Planning Commission had recommended approval 10-2 in December 2019. Proponents Jared Edens and Casey Buchanan spoke, while neighboring resident Jeff Mazad raised concerns about construction disruption and housing affordability for local renters. Council Member Charlie Reece questioned the applicant on post-Planning Commission changes, 100-year floodplain mitigation, and road improvements, and Council Member DeDreana Freeman asked staff about neighbor notification and the two Planning Commission dissenting concerns before the digest truncated the middle of the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Temporary Ordinance for Outdoor Seating in Rights-of-Way and Suburban Parking Lots
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public remarks from Ms. Turnbull, Council Member DeDreana Freeman noted small business owners' concerns about feeling left behind and issues with grants and loans, while Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton urged ensuring suburban restaurants outside downtown could also benefit. Planning Director Pat Young explained that staff proposed complementary amendments to the Mayor and BOCC Chair's emergency order suspending parking minimums so suburban businesses could use private parking lots for outdoor seating, and noted Transportation Director Sean Egan was seeking funding for required protective barriers. Council adopted the temporary ordinance by roll-call vote (5-0, with Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson stepped out).

agenda_items.title: Proposed Youth-Focused Black Lives Matter Public Arts Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman proposed mobilizing Participatory Budgeting funds alongside General Services and the Public Arts Program to commission a youth-focused Black Lives Matter street mural or public arts project led by Black and artists of color to curb violence and engage youth. Mayor Steve Schewel noted the City had just received a $25,000 Bloomberg grant that might align, Council Member Javiera Caballero voiced support for outdoor art during COVID-19, and City Manager Tom Bonfield committed to following up with Freeman and reporting back on grant eligibility and manager budget authority.

meetings.title: Special Virtual Durham City Council Meeting June 24, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the June 24, 2020 special virtual meeting with all six seated members participating. Council heard a Pride Month proclamation and unanimously passed (6-0) a resolution declaring racism a public health crisis, drafted by Wanda Boone of the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People, while announcements also noted a $1 million set-aside for the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force and scheduled August 6 for the next Ward 3 vacancy discussion. In land-use public hearings, Council split 4-2 to approve both the consistency statement and UDO amendment for a residential development project presented by Mr. Sivers—with Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, Council Member Javiera Caballero, and Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton voting Aye, and Council Members DeDreana Freeman and Charlie Reece voting Nay after Freeman raised citywide flooding concerns. Council then voted 6-0 on the consistency statement and 5-1 to adopt UDO Text Amendment TC1900005 (Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit Definition), with Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and Council Members Freeman, Middleton, and Reece voting Aye and Council Member Caballero casting the lone Nay vote per the 5-1 Clerk tally, before voting 6-0 to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamation: LGBTQ Pride Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson read a proclamation celebrating LGBTQ Pride Month, highlighting recent U.S. Supreme Court protections for LGBTQ workers under the Civil Rights Act and Durham's history from its 1981 Pride March through opposition to Amendment 1 and HB 2. J-Clap, director of the local LGBTQ Center, accepted the proclamation.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Resolution Declaring Racism a Public Health Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Moved up from the end of the agenda, Mayor Steve Schewel read the resolution committing the City to ongoing anti-racism and racial equity training for Council, staff, and community partners/vendors, alongside periodic progress reporting. Drafter Wanda Boone (Chair, Health and Safety Committee, Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People) urged accountability and living implementation following Durham County's June 8 adoption of the resolution, and Council approved it 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Council and Staff Announcements (Ward 3 Vacancy, Wellness Task Force, Backlog, Closed Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Charlie Reece announced that Council was scheduled to next discuss the Ward 3 vacancy at its August 6 work session and that he would consult colleagues and community members beforehand. Discussion also referenced a $1 million allocation toward the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force and its recommendations, the City Manager thanked Council for holding extra special meetings to clear land-use backlogs, and the City Attorney requested a closed session on pending claims.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Amendment / Residential Development Item (Mr. Sivers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-digest truncation gap, planning staff described work on interim UDO changes and a new Planning Commission UDO text amendment committee, while Council Member DeDreana Freeman emphasized recurring neighborhood flooding during heavy downpours that needs to be addressed across the city. After Mayor Schewel thanked Mr. Sivers and his team for post-Planning Commission revisions and housing at the proposed price point, Council split 4-2 on both the consistency statement and the UDO ordinance (Schewel, Johnson, Caballero, Middleton Aye; Freeman, Reece Nay).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1900005 (Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit Definition)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC1900005, updating the affordable housing dwelling unit definition to distinguish rental and for-sale units, provide flexibility as resident incomes rise, and tie requirements to the compliance rules and procedures Council adopted June 1. Council Member Charlie Reece asked about Planning Commissioner Miller's legal drafting concerns, while Council Member DeDreana Freeman questioned post-site-plan monitoring and public complaint pathways with Community Development's Karen Lado responding on agency monitoring. Council approved the consistency statement 6-0 and adopted the ordinance 5-1.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Motion for Attorney-Client Consultation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney read the statutory motion under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation regarding handling of pending claims. Council unanimously approved entering closed session (6-0) and recessed at 5:02 p.m.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council June 15, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the June 15, 2020 virtual City Council meeting (running past midnight to 12:10 a.m. on June 16), which opened with a moment of silence for 55 Durham residents lost to COVID-19 and for those suffering under systemic racism, alongside Council Member DeDreana Freeman's announcement that Durham had joined the Cities and Counties for Fines and Fee Justice network. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda (6-0, excluding Items 14 and 26) and voted on Item 14 (Affordable Housing Density Bonus Rules and Procedures) before a middle truncation gap in the digest omitted the FY 2020-21 Budget (Item 12) and Water/Sewer Rates (Item 50) proceedings. In the final hour captured in the digest, Council unanimously approved all eight motions for Item 47 (the 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan, FY 2020-21 Annual Action Plan, and CDBG, HOME, HOPWA, and ESG grant ordinances, 6-0 each), as well as Supplemental Item 51 supporting national reparations legislation (HR 40/SB 1083, 6-0) and Supplemental Item 52 recognizing Juneteenth (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel noted that an electrical surge at City Hall prevented DTV8 broadcast while streaming remained live on YouTube and social platforms, and led a moment of silence for 55 Durham COVID-19 victims and systemic racism struggles. Council Member DeDreana Freeman highlighted the Andrea Lynette Harris resolution, Durham's selection into PolicyLink's Cities and Counties for Fines and Fee Justice network, and upcoming resolutions on racism as a public health crisis, reparations, and Juneteenth.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Agenda Order
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield flagged Attachment 46 added to Item 12 (FY 2020-21 Budget and FY 2021-26 CIP) and three supplemental items: Item 50 (Proposed Water and Sewer Rates), Item 51 (National Action on Reparations), and Item 52 (Juneteenth Resolution). Council confirmed Item 50 would remain on the General Business Agenda to be acted upon prior to budget adoption.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 14 and 26)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including minutes, board and commission appointments, the resolution honoring Andrea Harris, NC Coalition to End Homelessness and DHA Downtown/Neighborhood Plan contracts, Wake County tax collection ILA, GDS Associates carbon neutrality and renewable energy action plan, Rebuilding Together grant, economic development/MSD contracts, bridge engineering, Atlas Organics composting, and Ecoflo household hazardous waste contracts. With Items 14 and 26 pulled, Council approved the consent agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Rules and Procedures for the Affordable Housing Bonus
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled for public comment by resident Mimi Kastler, who remarked that seeing tracked changes would have helped residents evaluate what was modified. Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson moved and Council Member Javiera Caballero seconded adoption, with four Aye votes recorded before the digest truncated the middle of the meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (partial roll call 4-0 before digest truncation)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Action: 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan, FY 2020-21 Annual Action Plan, and HUD Grant Ordinances
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following confirmation that written public comments on the Consolidated Plan would continue to be accepted through June 22, Council voted unanimously (6-0) across eight separate motions to submit the 2020-2025 Consolidated Plan and 2020-2021 Annual Action Plan, approve the revised Citizen Participation Plan, authorize contract execution, adopt CDBG ($2.14M/$2.2M), HOME, HOPWA, and ESG grant project ordinances, and approve the FY 2020-21 draft funding chart. Council Member DeDreana Freeman also asked staff to increase outreach engagement in the Southside community.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Resolution in Support of National Action on Reparations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman explained that the revised resolution reflects Dr. William 'Sandy' Darity's framework holding the federal government accountable to descendants of enslaved people from 1776 to 1865. Mayor Schewel expressed hope that Durham's vote would encourage other cities to support national reparations legislation, and Council passed the resolution unanimously (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Juneteenth Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman introduced the standalone Juneteenth resolution recognizing the 1619 context of slavery, stolen land, and stolen labor alongside national efforts to establish Juneteenth as a federal freedom holiday. Council unanimously approved the resolution (6-0) before adjourning at 12:10 a.m. on June 16.

meetings.title: Special Virtual Durham City Council June 10, 2020 (with captions)
meetings.executive_summary: In the captioned recording of the June 10, 2020 special virtual meeting presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel, all six seated members attended roll call. Council unanimously suspended the rules (6-0) and approved (6-0) creating a 15-member Housing Bond Implementation Committee with three Durham Housing Authority resident seats, while scheduling reparations and Juneteenth resolutions for June 15. Council split 5-1 on suspending the rules and appointing Stelfanie Williams to the GoTriangle Board—with Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, and Council Members Javiera Caballero, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Charlie Reece voting Aye, and Council Member DeDreana Freeman voting Nay. Following a public hearing on UDO Text Amendment revisions to the Neighborhood Protection Overlay (NPO) initiation process, Council split 4-1 on both the consistency statement and ordinance—with Schewel, Johnson, Middleton, and Reece voting Aye, Freeman voting Nay, and Caballero absent/non-voting—before voting 5-0 to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements: Reparations and Juneteenth Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel introduced a draft resolution supporting national reparations legislation following discussions with Dr. Darity and Kirsten Mullen, and Council Member DeDreana Freeman added a companion Juneteenth resolution tied to the 1619 Project. Council agreed to place both resolutions on the June 15 consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Housing Bond Implementation Committee Governance Structure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel proposed launching the Housing Bond Implementation Committee with a six-year sunset, three-year terms, and six-month Council check-ins, expanded to 15 members with three DHA resident representatives instead of one. Council voted 6-0 to suspend the rules and 6-0 to adopt the committee framework.

agenda_items.title: GoTriangle Board Appointment (Stelfanie Williams)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Schewel proposed appointing Stelfanie Williams, a non-Council member, to succeed Ellen Reckhow on the GoTriangle Board. Council voted 5-1 to suspend the rules and 5-1 to approve the appointment, with Council Member DeDreana Freeman voting Nay on both motions.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item: Closed Session Request on Eminent Domain Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Council Member DeDreana Freeman congratulated Council Member Javiera Caballero on her MPO board appointment, the City Attorney requested an attorney-client closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding an eminent domain case handled by Fred Lamar. Council approved the priority item 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Request to Initiate a Neighborhood Protection Overlay (NPO)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reported insufficient staff bandwidth to process an NPO while completing the Comprehensive Plan without $50,000 for an external consultant, and noted policy conflicts with recent Council decisions. The rest of Item 25 fell inside the omitted middle portion of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Neighborhood Protection Overlay (NPO) Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Scott Whiteman presented Planning Commission-backed UDO amendments requiring Council initiation before staff begins NPO drafting, drawing opposition from resident Ms. Plass who argued the changes politicize and erode citizen-led neighborhood protections. Council members debated housing diversity versus historic exclusion, staff resource constraints, and whether an absence counts as a No vote before adopting both the consistency statement and ordinance 4-1 (Freeman Nay; Caballero absent/non-voting).

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney read the NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) motion for attorney-client consultation on pending claims, and the five seated members present voted 5-0 to move into closed session.

votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules for immediate action on the Housing Bond Implementation Committee outline.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session June 4, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the nearly six-hour June 4, 2020 virtual City Council work session with all six seated members participating. Council began with a moment of silence for Durham's 'Butterfly', scheduled a 7:00 p.m. Race Equity Task Force session, accepted the City Manager's priority additions (FY 2021 budget reconciliation and the Durham Small Business Recovery Fund), and reviewed virtual board/commission ballot procedures and upcoming June–July consent and public hearing items. In the final budget reconciliation discussion captured in the digest, Council reviewed six proposed Public Works positions—supporting two general-fund right-of-way safety roles—while Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson questioned preserving a ~16.3–16.7% fund balance rather than drawing it down toward 12%, with staff warning that recurring pay raises ($7 million) would strain FY 2022. After resolving an overlapping board nomination for Cassandra Stokes in favor of the Women's Commission, Council voted unanimously (6-0) to settle the upcoming agendas, keeping the FY 2021 budget on the General Business Agenda without a presentation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the 1:00 p.m. work session, led a moment of silence for Durham's 'Butterfly', and confirmed a 7:00 p.m. meeting to hear Race Equity Task Force recommendations. City Manager Tom Bonfield added Item 48 (FY 2021 budget reconciliation) and Item 49 (Durham Small Business Recovery Fund), which Council moved and voted to accept.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Virtual Balloting and Agenda Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk walked Council through virtual board/commission balloting via Granicus and email, and Council agreed to re-advertise vacancies on the Carolina Theatre Board (Item 2), Homeless Services Advisory Committee (Item 5), Open Space and Trails Commission (Item 6), and potentially Housing Appeals Board (Item 9). Council also previewed June 15, June 24, and July 1 agenda items including the Andrea Harris resolution, DHA and DDI contracts (held pending presentations), GDS Associates carbon neutrality plan, composting and HHW contracts, and planning public hearings (Items 37–47).

agenda_items.title: FY 2020-21 Budget Work Session Reconciliation: Public Works Positions and Fund Balance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams detailed six requested positions—three fee/stormwater-funded, two general-fund right-of-way safety positions, and one general-fund survey position—with Council voicing support for the right-of-way safety roles. Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson asked why the budget kept fund balance at ~16.3–16.7% rather than suspending policy to 12%, and Manager Bonfield and Budget Director Bertha Johnson explained that using one-time reserves for $7 million in recurring pay raises would create an FY 2022 cliff, though one-time employee bonuses could be weighed while holding the line against tax increases.

agenda_items.title: Resolution of Overlapping Board Ballots and Settling the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council resolved an overlapping straw ballot in which Cassandra Stokes received three votes each for the Women's Commission and Housing Appeals Board, shifting a vote so she received four votes for the Women's Commission. Council then debated whether to place Item 12 (the FY 2021 budget) on consent or GBA, agreed to keep it on GBA without a presentation so Council could respond to emailed public comments, and voted 6-0 to settle the June 15, June 24, and July 1 agendas.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Items 48 and 49)
votes.notes: Roll call truncated in digest after Mayor Pro Tem Johnson's Aye vote at [00:14:51]; both items were added and Item 48 was taken up later in the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted adding Item 48 (FY 2021 budget reconciliation) and Item 49 (Durham Small Business Recovery Fund) to the work session agenda.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Meeting June 1, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In the live-stream recording of the June 1, 2020 virtual City Council meeting presided over by Mayor Steve Schewel, Council opened with a moment of silent meditation for George Floyd and extended remarks from Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson and Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero on structural racism, policing practices, and activating the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force. Following the Clerk's announcement of a 72-hour public hearing comment inbox and reading of the consent agenda (whose vote fell inside an omitted middle truncation gap), the digest captures the public hearing on revising stormwater rates effective July 1, 2020 to meet Falls Lake Stage 1 water quality obligations. Council passed the stormwater rate ordinance 5-1—with Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and Council Members Caballero and Reece explicitly recorded as Ayes, and the roll-call responses of Council Members DeDreana Freeman and Mark-Anthony Middleton falling inside a 6-second omitted transcript gap (though Freeman immediately thereafter opposed raising utility rates during COVID-19). On Item 12 (Proposed FY 2020-21 Water and Sewer Rates), Council deferred action and referred the rate decision to the June 4 budget reconciliation work session.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence for George Floyd, and Council Remarks on Racism and Policing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel convened the 7:00 p.m. virtual meeting with a moment of silent meditation for George Floyd, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Charlie Reece. Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson and Council Members Mark-Anthony Middleton, Charlie Reece, and Javiera Caballero spoke on police violence nationwide, Durham's de-escalation posture under Chief C.J. Davis, structural racism alongside COVID-19, and shifting public safety investments toward community-based interventions.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk Priority Item and Consent Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced the 72-hour written public-comment email window (PublicHearing.Comment@DurhamNC.gov), after which Mayor Schewel began reading the consent agenda (minutes, El Futuro PB grant, sales tax sharing, Commerce Street Seniors and Elizabeth Street housing loans, and pedestrian improvements). The consent vote itself occurred inside the omitted middle truncation gap.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Stormwater Rates Fee Schedule Revision (Effective July 1, 2020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following staff remarks from Paul Wiebke citing ongoing Falls Lake Stage 1 existing-development water quality requirements effective since January 2011, Mayor Schewel closed the public hearing with no additional speakers. Council voted 5-1 to adopt the ordinance revising stormwater rates effective July 1, 2020.

agenda_items.title: General Business Agenda: Proposed FY 2020-21 Water and Sewer Rates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented revised FY 2020-21 water and sewer rate options (2.1% vs. 1.7% Tier 3 increase depending on $755,000 in requested positions). Council Member DeDreana Freeman opposed raising utility rates during the pandemic, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson objected to setting rates prior to budget decisions on positions, and Council Member Middleton inquired about 22–23 open departmental vacancies; Council referred the item back to administration and the June 4 work session.

meetings.title: Special Durham City Council Meeting May 28, 2020 (with captions)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on May 28, 2020 for the second day of its FY 2020-21 budget work sessions, all six seated Durham City Council members heard department briefings from City-County Planning, Public Works, Community Development, Economic and Workforce Development, and Community Engagement. Council held an informal unanimous thumbs-up straw poll directing staff to include FY 2020-21 funding to continue the existing Long-Term Homeowner Property Tax Assistance Grant for one year, and after debating whether to send a letter citing $1 million or an official resolution without a fixed dollar figure, voted unanimously 6-0 (preceded by a 6-0 rule suspension) to adopt an official Council statement inviting a joint tax-relief proposal from the Durham County Board of Commissioners. Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton questioned launching Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 virtually in Fall 2020 while pushing the Strategic Plan refresh to 2021, citing digital-divide equity barriers, while Budget Director Bertha Johnson agreed to extend the post-public-hearing written comment period from 24 hours to 72 hours.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Day 2 Budget Work Session Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the special virtual budget work session to order at 10:00 a.m., and the clerk confirmed all six seated council members were present. City Manager Tom Bonfield and Budget Director Bertha Johnson outlined the Day 2 department presentation sequence: Planning, Public Works, Community Development, Office of Economic and Workforce Development, and Community Engagement.

agenda_items.title: City-County Planning Department COVID-19 Adaptation and FY 2020-21 Budget Highlights
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat briefed Council on transitioning development review operations to a paperless remote environment with Technology Solutions and Finance, clearing 12 to 14 postponed zoning, annexation, and UDO cases through virtual public hearings beginning June 1 and special meetings in June and July. Staff highlighted Comprehensive Plan engagement stipends for community ambassadors reaching youth, Latinx, and rural county residents, noted zero new budget requests with only a modest projected FY21 revenue dip, and cited Moody's Analytics ranking Durham number one nationally for rapid post-pandemic recovery.

agenda_items.title: Long-Term Homeowner Property Tax Assistance Grant Continuation and County Partnership Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following presentations from Community Development Director Reginald Johnson, Council members Jillian Johnson, DeDreana Freeman, Charlie Reece, Mark-Anthony Middleton, and Javiera Caballero unanimously voiced support for extending the city's existing Long-Term Homeowner Property Tax Assistance Grant for another year and gave unanimous thumbs-up direction via straw poll to fund it in the FY 2020-21 budget. Later, members debated how to urge Durham County to partner on an expanded program—with Charlie Reece suggesting a letter citing $1 million, Mayor Schewel favoring a letter without a set dollar figure, and Mark-Anthony Middleton insisting on a formally voted Council statement—before suspending the rules 6-0 and passing Middleton's motion 6-0 to adopt an official Council statement welcoming a County proposal in the upcoming fiscal year.

agenda_items.title: Community Engagement, Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 Timing, and 2020 Census
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the Budget and Management Services and Engagement wrap-up, Mark-Anthony Middleton questioned relying on virtual-only community engagement to launch Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 in Fall 2020 while pushing the Strategic Plan refresh to 2021, arguing the same virtual-access concerns raised over replacing the Ward 3 seat still applied. Staff clarified the Strategic Plan refresh had always been scheduled for 2021 and noted Durham County's 2020 Census response rate stood at 55%, prompting Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson to highlight digital divide barriers.

agenda_items.title: Budget Work Session Follow-Up Schedule, Public Hearing Notice, and 72-Hour Comment Window
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield noted that Police and Fire did not present during the abbreviated two-day sessions and asked whether Council needed a June 4 morning budget check-in prior to the June 15 adoption vote; Mayor Steve Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson preferred handling any flagged general fund items during the June 4 afternoon work session. Staff reminded the public of the first virtual budget public hearing on June 1 at 7:00 p.m., shared a virtual birthday cake for Tom Bonfield's May 30 birthday, and agreed to extend the post-hearing written comment period from the statutory 24-hour minimum to 72 hours before adjourning at 2:33 p.m.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Official City Council Statement Regarding Joint City-County Homeowner Tax Relief
votes.notes: Earlier at 01:54:50, Council used an informal thumbs-up straw poll (per City Manager and City Attorney guidance) to direct staff to include FY 2020-21 funding for continuing the existing homeowner property tax assistance grant.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Mark-Anthony Middleton's motion to adopt an official City Council statement rather than a letter, Council moved and seconded to suspend the rules for immediate action. The deputy clerk called the roll and all six seated members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Adopt Official City Council Statement Inviting a Durham County Proposal for Long-Term Low-Income Homeowner Tax Relief
votes.discussion_detail: Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded adopting an official City Council statement inviting and welcoming a proposal from the Durham County Board of Commissioners and County Tax Office for long-term low-income homeowner tax relief at any time in the upcoming fiscal year without specifying a fixed dollar commitment. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special Durham City Council Meeting May 28, 2020 (with captions)
disagreements.issue: Form and Financial Specificity of City Council Outreach to Durham County on Homeowner Tax Relief
disagreements.summary: While all council members favored partnering with Durham County on an expanded long-term low-income homeowner tax relief program, members differed on whether to send a letter citing roughly $1 million, send a letter without a specific dollar figure, or adopt a formally voted City Council statement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Send a Council-signed letter committing roughly $1 million in city funds (or a formal letter without a dollar figure) to invite a County proposal.
side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece suggested a joint letter under all members' signatures indicating readiness to commit around $1 million in administration and grants.
Mayor Steve Schewel supported a Council letter inviting a County proposal at any time during the fiscal year without naming a specific dollar figure because Council lacked consensus on a number.
disagreements.side_b_position: Issue an official voted City Council statement carrying the full formal weight of the governing body rather than an informal letter.
side_b_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton argued the issue crossed the letter-writing threshold and needed a formal voted Council statement with the clerk's stamp and raised seal to signal Durham's commitment.
disagreements.resolution: Council suspended the rules 6-0 and unanimously passed Middleton's motion (seconded by DeDreana Freeman) 6-0 to adopt an official City Council statement without a fixed dollar amount.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special Durham City Council Meeting May 28, 2020 (with captions)
disagreements.issue: Virtual-Only Community Engagement and Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 Timing
disagreements.summary: Council Member Mark-Anthony Middleton questioned proceeding with Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 in Fall 2020 under virtual-only engagement while deferring the Strategic Plan refresh to 2021.
disagreements.side_a_position: Virtual-only community engagement poses unresolved equity and public-health barriers that make launching Participatory Budgeting Cycle 2 in Fall 2020 problematic.
side_a_arguments: No public-health assurance guaranteed full in-person reopening by Fall 2020.
The same virtual-access objections used to hold up filling the Ward 3 Council vacancy apply to selecting artists or launching Participatory Budgeting solely online.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain the pre-existing 2021 schedule for the Strategic Plan refresh while proceeding with Fall 2020 Participatory Budgeting planning.
side_b_arguments: Staff noted the Strategic Plan refresh had always been scheduled for 2021 rather than being delayed specifically over virtual engagement.
disagreements.resolution: Informational discussion; no formal vote taken.

meetings.title: Special Durham City Council Meeting May 27, 2020 (with closed captions)
meetings.executive_summary: In the closed-captioned broadcast of Durham City Council's May 27, 2020 Day 1 FY 2020-21 virtual budget work session, all six seated council members reviewed COVID-19 revenue losses and department updates covering pay and benefits, General Services, Parks and Recreation, and Transportation. Budget Director Bertha Johnson detailed holding the property tax rate flat, keeping the collection rate at 99.6% rather than 99% (a $1 million loss from February projections), projecting flat motor vehicle taxes, absorbing a 25% Powell Bill reduction, and drawing down fund balance at levels not seen since 2009. Council members questioned Transportation on bus sanitation, GoDurham mask penetration, 12-to-18-month parking operations, and slow streets; DeDreana Freeman urged stronger racial equity rigor in budget cuts, and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece flagged the new Transportation Financial Manager position for follow-up review. No formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Day 1 Budget Work Session Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel opened the 10:00 a.m. virtual budget work session and thanked budget, finance, technology, and clerk staff. City Manager Tom Bonfield introduced the two-day hybrid COVID-19 budget review, and Budget Director Bertha Johnson outlined Day 1 topics including revenue, pay and benefits, General Services, Parks and Recreation, and Transportation.

agenda_items.title: General Fund Revenue Projections, Property Tax Base, and Powell Bill Reduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson reviewed FY 2020-21 General Fund revenue assumptions compared to February 14 pre-COVID estimates, noting no property tax rate increase, 2.31% assessed value growth led by real property, flat motor vehicle taxes, and holding the tax collection rate at 99.6% rather than raising it to 99%. She confirmed a newly incorporated 25% loss in state Powell Bill street-aid funding and substantial fund balance utilization, while reminding residents to separate city and county property tax bills.

agenda_items.title: Transit Mask Penetration, Bus Sanitation, Parking, Slow Streets, and Budget Equity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members asked Transportation staff about GoDurham rider mask usage, bus sanitation protocols while offline, parking revenue recovery over the next 12 to 18 months, and slow-streets planning with cycling and pedestrian advocates. DeDreana Freeman warned against rushing cost-cutting decisions without deeper racial equity accountability, while staff emphasized that GoDurham investments represent the largest budget increase and disproportionately serve riders of color (about 90% of ridership).

agenda_items.title: Flagged Follow-Up Items: Transportation Financial Manager and Parks & Rec Staffing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel thanked Charlie Reece and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson for sharing presiding duties, and City Manager Tom Bonfield stated all service restoration uses an equity lens. Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece placed the proposed Transportation Financial Manager position on the follow-up list (noting the proposal to shift its funding from General Fund to Transit), while Javiera Caballero asked about CARES Act options, requested a breakdown of Parks and Recreation kept versus furloughed staff, and praised maintaining in-house custodial living wages before the meeting adjourned at 1:27 p.m.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special Durham City Council Meeting May 27, 2020 (with closed captions)
disagreements.issue: Racial Equity in Budget Reductions and New Transportation Financial Manager Position
disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether COVID-19 budget adjustments adequately centered racial equity and flagged the proposed Transportation Financial Manager position for further review against competing city priorities.
disagreements.side_a_position: Insist on deeper racial equity safeguards in cost-cutting and scrutinize adding a new Transportation Financial Manager position relative to other city needs.
side_a_arguments: DeDreana Freeman stated the council must avoid rushing into easy cost cuts with inequitable outcomes ('I can't do a Katrina outcome').
Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson asked to flag the new Transportation Financial Manager position to weigh against all other potential city needs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Highlight equitable transit spending and potential Transit-fund or CARES Act offsets for the Transportation position.
side_b_arguments: Transportation staff noted GoDurham transit expansion is the largest budget increase and serves a ridership roughly 90% people of color, and City Manager Tom Bonfield stated service restoration applies an equity lens.
Charlie Reece pointed out Transportation Director Sean proposed shifting the position from the General Fund to Transit, and Javiera Caballero asked whether CARES Act funds could help.
disagreements.resolution: Staff recorded the Transportation Financial Manager position and Parks and Recreation staffing breakdown as flagged follow-up items with no formal vote.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session May 21, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on May 21, 2020, all six seated Durham City Council members passed nine unanimous 6-0 roll-call votes spanning priority agenda items, COVID-19 mask distribution, board Zoom security, and small-business relief. After DeDreana Freeman urged directing Cover Durham mask funds to local or people-of-color-owned businesses rather than Original Mattress Factory in Raleigh, Council unanimously amended and approved 6-0 the mask funding transfer to prioritize transit riders in distribution and prioritize hiring people of color. Following a Zoom-bombing incident at the Environmental Affairs Board meeting, Council accepted Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson's proposal to fund four shared Zoom webinar licenses rather than 20 individual licenses and passed it 6-0 alongside DeDreana Freeman's call for liaison training. At the close of the session, following sharp council criticism from Mark-Anthony Middleton, Jillian Johnson, and DeDreana Freeman over Office of Economic and Workforce Development (OEWD) delays and equity barriers in the proposed small-business loan program, Council suspended the rules and voted 6-0 to allocate $1 million for the small business relief program before settling the upcoming regular agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the 1:00 p.m. virtual work session to order, and the clerk confirmed all six seated council members present. Mark-Anthony Middleton commended Durham Clergy United for announcing they would refrain from holding mass in-person religious gatherings despite a federal court ruling, and members discussed COVID-19's disproportionate toll on communities of color.

agenda_items.title: Forest Hills Neighborhood Protection Overlay and FY 2021 Stormwater Rate Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented two priority items: revising Agenda Item 25 (initiating a Forest Hills Neighborhood Protection Overlay) from a public hearing to routine consent, and adding Agenda Item 27 (FY 2021 stormwater rate proposal) to schedule a June 1 public hearing. Council approved the manager's priority items 6-0 on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Cover Durham Phase 1 Mask Distribution Project Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a 6-0 vote to consider the clerk's priority items, the City Clerk read details from coordinator Isaac Haran on Phase 1 of Cover Durham to distribute 50,000 reusable masks free to low-income and disproportionately Black neighborhoods via the Community Health Coalition, sourced from Original Mattress Factory in Raleigh. After DeDreana Freeman pushed to support local Durham or POC-owned producers such as LCI, Council suspended the rules 6-0 and passed Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson's motion (seconded by Mark-Anthony Middleton) 6-0 to approve the fund transfer with friendly amendments prioritizing transit riders in distribution and hiring people of color.

agenda_items.title: Zoom Webinar Licenses to Prevent Zoom-Bombing of Boards and Commissions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported a severe Zoom-bombing incident at the Environmental Affairs Board meeting the prior evening and proposed funding 20 Zoom webinar licenses ($40/month each, up to $5,800 from the $5,000 volunteer reception budget) to restrict public participant audio/video. Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson pointed out at most four board meetings ever overlap simultaneously so four shared licenses would suffice, and DeDreana Freeman stressed training tech liaisons on webinar controls; Council suspended the rules 6-0 and approved the expenditure 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Small Business COVID-19 Relief Loan Program Structure and $1 Million City Allocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD presented proposed eligibility rules for a small business loan fund (independently owned local businesses operating 18+ months, priority for Neighborhood Revitalization and Opportunity Zones, fair-and-above credit scores, and Duke University's $1 million challenge) targeting a June council vote and July 1 check writing. Council members voiced strong dissatisfaction over the omitted budget amount, lack of a selected CDFI partner, slow July 1 timeline, and equity criteria; after suspending the rules 6-0, Council voted unanimously 6-0 to allocate $1 million to the small business relief program.

agenda_items.title: Settle Upcoming Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized the settled agenda placing Items 1-11 and 13-17 on Consent and Items 12 and 25 on the General Business Agenda. Council approved the agenda 6-0 on roll call before adjourning at 5:10 p.m.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Item 25 Forest Hills NPO Reclassification and Item 27 FY 2021 Stormwater Rate Public Hearing)
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded approval of City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority items moving Item 25 to routine consent and adding Item 27 for a June 1 public hearing. All six seated members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve Discussion of City Clerk's Priority Items (Mask Project Funding and Zoom-Bombing Security)
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded adding the City Clerk's two priority items to the work session discussion. The roll call passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Cover Durham Mask Project Funding
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded suspending the rules to take immediate action on the Cover Durham mask transfer. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve Fund Transfer for Cover Durham Mask Purchasing and Distribution (with Transit and Equity Amendments)
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded approving the transfer of funds for Cover Durham masks, incorporating friendly amendments requesting the nonprofit prioritize transit riders in mask distribution and prioritize hiring people of color in distribution efforts. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Zoom Webinar Licenses for Boards and Commissions
votes.discussion_detail: Following discussion of Zoom webinar controls and liaison training, Council moved and seconded suspending the rules for an immediate vote. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Authorize City Clerk Expenditure for Zoom Webinar Licenses for Active Boards and Commissions
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded authorizing the City Clerk to spend necessary month-to-month funds (reallocated from the volunteer reception line item, pursuing four shared licenses to minimize cost) to provide Zoom webinar security for boards and commissions. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on $1 Million Allocation for Small Business Relief Program
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded suspending the rules to vote immediately on allocating $1 million to the small business relief program. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Allocate $1 Million to Upcoming Small Business Relief Program
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded formally allocating $1 million for Durham's upcoming small business COVID-19 relief program in response to Duke University's $1 million challenge and council concern over delayed disbursement. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve / Settle Upcoming Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-11, 13-17; GBA Items 12, 25)
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded approving the settled agenda for the next regular meeting under Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson presiding. All six members voted Aye on roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session May 21, 2020 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Vendor Sourcing and Equity Conditions for Cover Durham Mask Project
disagreements.summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman questioned sourcing all 50,000 masks from Original Mattress Factory in Raleigh rather than local Durham or POC-owned producers, while Mayor Steve Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson noted the direct vendor allocation was already set and added hiring and transit-rider amendments instead.
disagreements.side_a_position: Direct mask procurement funding to local Durham or people-of-color-owned businesses rather than an out-of-county vendor in Raleigh.
side_a_arguments: DeDreana Freeman noted local producers such as LCI were already making masks in Durham and urged finding ways to fund local or POC-owned businesses.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the transfer as structured for Original Mattress Factory while requesting prioritization of transit riders and hiring people of color for distribution.
side_b_arguments: Jillian Johnson noted the funding was already designated to go directly to Original Mattress Factory so a POC-owned manufacturer could not be substituted at this stage.
Requesting the nonprofit prioritize hiring people of color in distribution and prioritizing GoDurham transit riders addressed equity goals.
disagreements.resolution: Jillian Johnson's motion incorporating both friendly amendments (seconded by Mark-Anthony Middleton) passed 6-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session May 21, 2020 (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Small Business COVID-19 Relief Fund Timeline, Sizing, and Equity Design
disagreements.summary: Council members sharply criticized OEWD's presentation for omitting a concrete fund size, delaying check writing until July 1 while searching for a CDFI partner, and relying on traditional underwriting criteria that could preserve racial disparities.
disagreements.side_a_position: Commit funding immediately, deploy already-budgeted Built to Last funds by early June, and redesign eligibility around racial equity rather than waiting for July 1.
side_a_arguments: Mark-Anthony Middleton objected that the plan omitted a fund size, lagged behind peer NC cities, and came without a ready 'yea or nay' structure.
Jillian Johnson urged immediately deploying the $300,000 already budgeted for Built to Last rather than waiting for the new fiscal year.
DeDreana Freeman warned that relying on existing credit and longevity criteria keeps racial disparities intact and urged equitable relief for struggling cash-flowing businesses.
disagreements.side_b_position: Work with Council, the City Manager, Duke University's $1 million commitment, and a vetted CDFI partner to bring a structured budget and program to the next council meeting for July 1 disbursement.
side_b_arguments: OEWD staff cited administrative capacity, bottleneck avoidance, demographic performance tracking, and NC Exclusive Emoluments Clause legal constraints as reasons to finalize a CDFI-administered loan model for July 1.
disagreements.resolution: Council suspended the rules 6-0 and voted unanimously 6-0 to allocate $1 million to the small business relief program while directing staff to finalize the framework.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council May 18, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: In the live-stream recording of Durham City Council's May 18, 2020 virtual meeting, all six seated members remembered 37 Durham residents lost to COVID-19 and heard City Manager Tom Bonfield present the proposed $504.3 million FY 2020-21 budget, including a $214.6 million General Fund (-0.6%), flat 53.17-cent property tax rate, and projected $4.4 million (-6.6%) sales tax decline. During Council's first virtual public hearing on $2,853,191 in HUD CDBG Annual Action Plan amendments, technical barriers initially prevented preregistered speakers from entering Zoom; after DeDreana Freeman flagged YouTube commenters and Wanda Page shared the phone/password access, Stella Adams testified in support of CDBG, homeowner tax relief, and retaining $8 million from 505 West Chapel Hill Street in the housing fund. Council voted 6-0 on roll call to approve the HUD CDBG amendments and, at Javiera Caballero's prompting to comply with NC's new remote-meeting law, re-voted 6-0 by roll call to approve the Consent Agenda (Items 1 and 3-15).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, COVID-19 Moment of Silence, Pledge, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., led a moment of silence for 37 Durham COVID-19 fatalities and ~1,000 infections, and called on Charlie Reece for the Pledge of Allegiance before the clerk confirmed all six seated council members present.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item and Consent Agenda (Items 1 and 3-15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield noted added work-session information for Item 3 (Affordable Housing Loan Portfolio Servicing). Council approved Consent Items 1 and 3-15 (FY21 budget guidelines, East Club Blvd sidewalks, SCADA contract, South Durham Water Reclamation design, Lake Michie acquisition, employment training grant, development fee ordinance, paving/street amendments, University Dr bike/ped SW-39C, and 919 Storage utility extension) 6-0 by raised hands on Mark-Anthony Middleton's motion and Javiera Caballero's second, and later re-approved the slate 6-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's FY 2020-21 Proposed Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented the proposed $504.3 million FY 2020-21 budget (+$26.5 million due to $24.3 million in October 2020 debt refunding accounting and $4.1 million in county-funded GoDurham expansion), with a $214.6 million General Fund (-0.6%). The budget keeps the property tax rate flat at 53.17 cents per $100 valuation (about $1,229/year on a $231,000 median home, reflecting ~$1.1 million in COVID-19 property tax loss) while projecting a 6.6% ($4.4 million) drop in sales tax collections to $64.2 million.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval — HUD CDBG Annual Action Plan Amendments ($2,853,191)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During Council's first virtual public hearing on reconciling $2,853,191 in FY 2015-20 CDBG funds, Mayor Schewel and Council addressed public-comment access after none of the preregistered external speakers initially entered Zoom and DeDreana Freeman relayed YouTube viewers trying to join. Once Wanda Page posted dial-in access, Stella Adams urged keeping $8 million from selling 505 West Chapel Hill Street in the housing fund (which Freeman asked staff to detail at budget work sessions), and Council approved the HUD amendments 6-0 by roll call while keeping the 24-hour written comment window open.

meetings.title: Virtual Durham City Council Work Session May 7, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on May 7, 2020, all six seated Durham City Council members opened with announcements from DeDreana Freeman on decolonizing wealth, Mark-Anthony Middleton condemning the killing of Ahmaud Arbery and COVID-19 racial disparities, and Mayor Steve Schewel apologizing for not briefing Council before naming Katie Galbraith and Letitia Sims as Recovery and Renewal Task Force co-chairs. Council approved the City Manager's priority items 6-0 and immediately suspended the rules (6-0) to accept an FAA CARES Act grant for the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (6-0). After pulling Items 1, 3, 6, 12, and 13 for review—including affordable housing loan servicing and Equity and Inclusion engagement on street projects—Council affirmed holding virtual meetings for the next couple of months, advised staff toward three-hour special evening sessions in June to clear roughly 20 backlogged land-use public hearings, and voted 6-0 to settle the regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Remarks on Racial Justice and Task Force Co-Chairs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the 1:00 p.m. work session to order with all six seated members present. DeDreana Freeman discussed a panel on decolonizing wealth and Durham Cares' COVID-19 forum; Mark-Anthony Middleton spoke in solidarity with the family of Ahmaud Arbery and highlighted COVID-19's disproportionate toll on Black and brown frontline workers; and Mayor Schewel apologized for not giving Council advance notice before naming Duke Regional Hospital President Katie Galbraith and Blue Cross Blue Shield VP/Controller Letitia Sims as Recovery and Renewal Task Force co-chairs.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Immediate Acceptance of RDU FAA CARES Act Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested same-day rule suspension and approval for Item 2 (Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority acceptance of a Federal Aviation Administration CARES Act grant covering revenue shortfalls, requiring approval by all four airport owners) and asked for end-of-meeting time to schedule June special land-use public hearings. Council approved the manager's priority items 6-0, suspended the rules 6-0, and accepted the FAA grant 6-0 by raised hands.

agenda_items.title: Departmental Agenda Review and Pulled Items (Items 1, 3, 6, 12, and 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Item 1 (FY21 budget guidelines), Item 3 (affordable housing loan portfolio servicing), Item 6 (South Durham Water Reclamation Facility renovations), Item 12 (ST-301C paving services), and Item 13 (SW-39C University Drive bicycle/pedestrian project) for staff Q&A while praising Item 7 (Lake Michie land acquisition) and Item 9 (Development Reference Guide). agenda_items.title: Virtual Meeting Continuation and Scheduling June Land-Use Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield reported roughly 20 land-use public hearing items backlogged since March and recommended keeping meetings virtual at least through June while adding two or three special June meetings alongside June 1 and June 15. Council affirmed remaining virtual for the next couple of months, noted compliance with North Carolina's newly enacted remote public-comment statute, and favored three-hour evening sessions over four-hour sessions.

agenda_items.title: Settle Upcoming Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield recommended Consent Items 1 and 3-15, GBA Item 16, and GBA Public Hearing Item 17 (with Item 2 already disposed of). Council unanimously approved settling the agenda 6-0 by raised hands before adjourning at 1:55 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 2 — Approve Acceptance of RDU Airport Authority FAA CARES Act Grant Offer
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved and seconded accepting the FAA CARES Act grant offer for the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority. All six members voted Aye by raised hands.

votes.discussion_detail: Following City Manager Tom Bonfield's agenda recommendation placing Items 1 and 3-15 on Consent, Item 16 on General Business, and Item 17 as a public hearing, Council moved and seconded approval. All six members raised hands and the motion passed unanimously.

meetings.title: Virtual Special City Council Meeting - Budget
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired virtually by Mayor Steve Schewel on April 24, 2020, the Durham City Council held a special budget session as the COVID-19 pandemic reshaped FY 2020–21 fiscal projections. City Manager Tom Bonfield and Budget Director Bertha Johnson reported that the projected General Fund shortfall had widened from roughly $750,000 in February to an estimated $11.8 million to $12.5 million gap due to a 1% property tax collection rate reduction ($1.1 million), a 10% sales tax drop ($7.2 million), a 9% occupancy tax drop ($297,000), and Parks and Recreation revenue losses, prompting staff to remove $4 million in planned additional fund balance for street maintenance. No formal votes were taken, though Council members gave informal thumbs-up consensus (including Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson, Council Member Javiera Caballero, and Council Member DeDreana Freeman) to hold a separate Dedicated Housing Fund discussion prior to budget adoption. Staff also updated Council on coordinating targeted small business relief with federal and state programs, confirmed that Council- and staff-initiated new budget requests would be held in abeyance ahead of the May 18 budget presentation and June 1 public hearing, and Mayor Schewel noted Durham's unified stay-at-home order was extended through May 15 with curbside retail pickup and farmers markets permitted.

agenda_items.title: FY 2020–21 COVID-19 Budget Financial Projections and Budget Guidelines Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel called the virtual special meeting to order at 1:00 p.m., and City Manager Tom Bonfield explained that within 60 days COVID-19 had shifted the General Fund from near balance to a roughly $12.5 million gap, requiring a flexible, evolving FY 2020–21 budget to avoid layoffs or major service cuts. Budget Director Bertha Johnson detailed revised revenue assumptions—reducing property tax revenue by 1% ($1.1 million, lowering the collection rate from 99.6% to 99% to match Durham County with vehicle taxes held flat), sales tax by 10% ($7.2 million), and occupancy tax by 9% ($297,000)—which pushed the multi-year General Fund deficit from $750,000 in February to $11.8 million. Staff also removed $4 million in planned additional fund balance for street maintenance (reducing that transfer from $5.9 million to $0) alongside other fund-balance offsets, and the Clerk began an attendance roll call at 00:13:05 before a transcript gap.

agenda_items.title: Dedicated Housing Fund Scheduling, Small Business Relief, Timeline & Stay-at-Home Order
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the meeting, City Manager Tom Bonfield sought Council guidance on holding a separate Dedicated Housing Fund discussion prior to budget adoption, receiving informal thumbs-up support from Council Members Javiera Caballero, DeDreana Freeman, and Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson. Staff reported working with partners to design targeted small business assistance aligned with federal and state aid rather than rushing funds to businesses with easier access, and confirmed the timeline for individual check-ins, the May 18 formal budget presentation, and the required June 1 public hearing while holding new Council and staff initiatives in abeyance. Mayor Schewel closed by briefing Council on Durham's extended stay-at-home order through May 15 (allowing retail curbside pickup, relaxed real estate rules, and safe farmers markets), while Council Member Javiera Caballero noted the Governor had closed schools for the remainder of the academic year.
